We have dealt with solicitors who told us not to contact their client, the landlord. We have not contacted him, but he keeps texting us. When we reply, he then texts back telling us to stop texting him. We need to raise this with the lawyers: who is supposed to be dealing with what.

We have received this letter. Kimberley signed for it at the door. It is addressed to Miss Kimberley Bath, McDonnell Court. It should have been addressed to me. It has “mental health” marked at the top. I do not think that is fair.

Look at the paperwork. See how it has been ripped open? It has already been opened. It was not sealed properly. We have the same interference with the mail again. It has a Ledingham Chalmers solicitors stamp on the back, and a mental health postal stamp. We will see what they say. I predict they will say they spoke to their client, he accepts responsibility for the doors and windows, and he will get them fixed. There will be nothing about the heating, and nothing about the claim. We asked for £5,000. If anything has come back on that, it will be a rejection.

Working out what we would be entitled to for the length of time we have been here, if we go to the Housing and Property Chamber, the figure is about £35,000. We have only asked for £5,000. We will see what the lawyer has said.

The letter says they are writing on behalf of their clients, Gary and Alison Smith, the landlords of the property in which we currently reside at 78B Duke Street, Aberdeen, AB24 3HB. It is a response to an email received on Tuesday 16 April 2024 with a link to a video recording. They say they have listened to the entire recording, discussed it with their client, and been instructed to address a number of points.

They say that throughout the video we claimed both clients were not registered landlords, and that Gary in particular was acting as an agent. They say that is incorrect, and that both are registered landlords with Aberdeen Council, with registration numbers that can be checked on the council website.

That registration is recent. When we first took the tenancy, Alison Smith was registered and Gary was doing all the talking. He provided the keys and came back to see the property a couple of times in the first year. It was him who later abandoned the property. Alison Smith was abusive about the property, which caused me to call the police. Gary turned up boisterous until he realised we were on the phone to the police. That video will be at the end of this recording.

They may be registered now, but they have not been registered for the whole tenancy. We have screenshots of the registration for this house showing periods when it was deregistered and not in anyone’s name. It has now been re-registered in Gary Smith and Alison Smith’s names. We need the date of that registration. We also have video of Kimberley at the council, where it was confirmed that neither Gary nor Alison was registered at that time. We have that in letter form and on audio. We can defeat any claim at the Housing and Property Chamber that Gary and Alison Smith were the registered landlords of this property continuously from 20 September 2020.

The letter says we raised several issues about the condition of the property, that we told Gary, and that he did not fix them. Their clients say only two issues were brought to their attention. One was a broken shower around 12 to 18 months ago. Gary says that when he heard about it he arranged for a plumber to fix it, and that he can produce the invoice. I agree he did fix it, but only after we reported that we had no shower and went without one for about six months. My body temperature drops and I need to get into hot water. We have three days of video of me severely ill, vomiting, drinking milk to cool the acid and vomiting it straight back up. These episodes come on when I cannot get a hot shower or bath. There is a name for the condition. I cannot pronounce it and I cannot remember it. Being at an address with no hot water is dangerous for me.

I believe the shower was reported about 40 months ago. I have a recorded telephone call telling Gary the shower was broken. He did nothing for several months. Only when Kimberley persevered on one particular day, explaining my health and that I needed a shower, did he visit. He was not pleasant. He said things to Kimberley that are open to question, including that the only reason he allowed her to live here was because he knew what she was going through. That is the same pattern we have seen with landlords and letting agents in the north-east of Scotland. The letter misstates the priority given to the shower, the need for hot water, and my health.

When it was fitted, the joiner told me to wait until morning for the sealant. I still got in that shower, kept water off the unit, and sat there for hours. I still have to do that.

He fixed the shower only after a long period without one, and during a period when no one was registered for the property.

They say the only other issue raised directly with Gary, when he was at the property, was the kitchen roof. They say my carer, Mr James Fraser, brought it to his attention, that Gary undertook to arrange a repair, but that Mr Fraser insisted he would repair it himself because it was minor, and that no further damage has been reported. They say they cannot be held responsible for any other alleged issues if they were not reported and they had no knowledge of them.

That is not right. We have every recorded telephone call and text to Gary and Alison Smith, where Gary was the person who responded. We reported the doors, windows, shower and toilet. We have video of Gary at the address every time he visited, just as we have video of the joiner who visited today. Every word is recorded. Gary knows about the toilet, the shower and the sinks. We have him on video looking at the sink and saying he would go to B&Q or another hardware store for the proper taps. As it stands, the sink has been running for almost two years. If you try to turn the taps off, the pipes buzz. We think that is pressure from other tenants in the building. We have it set so it does not buzz, but when someone else uses water it starts again, so it tends to run all the time. Water leaks down the pipes. The back of the kitchen is mouldy. Gary has been told. The condition today is the result of his failure to get it fixed at the time. His solicitors have been misinformed. He may be busy and may not remember everything. When they see the videos of him in the house, he may remember.

On the ceiling, it was discussed on camera. I said I would fix it. But after flood after flood, the damage is more extensive. It is structural, not cosmetic. The wall that holds the ceiling is splitting. One part of the wall in the corner is straight by a spirit level, but where the big crack is, the wall is leaning into the kitchen, which is parting the ceiling in the middle of the living room. That cannot be fixed with plasterboard. I think I pointed this out to Gary when he came back to look at the toilet, the kitchen sink and other parts. He was aware of the ceiling, and I told him I thought it was structural. At the time both he and I thought it was cosmetic and easy to fix. It is not. The wall is moving and parting the living-room ceiling. Where the letter says I insisted I would repair it myself because it was minor, and that they had no knowledge of other issues, we disagree. We will add the other videos of Gary at this address, showing issues reported over a long period, until he told us not to contact him and abandoned the property and the problems he had witnessed. He is on video saying he would go to a hardware store, I am sure he mentioned B&Q, for parts for the toilet, which constantly runs, and the sink, which constantly runs. He looked at the extractor fan in the toilet, saw it did not work, and said it needed replacing. There was also the front door. The original door was broken by the police and by Orbis joiners. It would not fit back into the latch. Gary gave me permission to change the fascia so the latch would fit. That was not possible, because the door I got had to go into its own frame. That is the door there today.

My memory of dates over four years may be foggy. Anyone’s would be. The recordings are time-stamped and dated, and can be checked against the property. We can show that their clients have misled them.

The main reason they can be held responsible is that the house is below the tolerable standard for many reasons. There is no proper fire protection. The property is not fit for the letting market. As registered landlords, the council had a duty to inspect and check that what the registration purported was actually being provided. It has not been. I find it astounding that they deny knowledge of particular issues when I have it on video.

They say that on entry the property was in good tenantable repair, with no mould or damp, and that any mould and damp now is likely from lack of ventilation or the way the property is used. So we are to blame. They say it has not been reported. They say all appliances and fixtures were in good order at the start and the property was fit to let, and that any claim is misconceived.

It is not misconceived. We have strong points on harassment and denial of access to services. Gary was at the address, on camera, seeing the faulty sink and saying he would fix it. If he has not fixed it for two years, mould and damp follow. That is not about how we use the property. We have had to boil and drink from the hot tap because it cannot be turned off. With the mixer, cold comes through mixed with hot from another line. That water is not treated as drinking water. We cannot get proper drinking water at this address. It has affected us, including gut problems. Phil is drinking tea. Gary’s claim that he had no knowledge is false. He was in the house, witnessing the faults, and saying he would get them fixed.

The letter then refers to an undisputed lack of rental payments for the four years the lease was in operation, and says their clients are likely to succeed in a claim for arrears at the First-tier Tribunal. It says failure to obtain housing benefit is not a defence, because it is not the landlord’s job to apply for a tenant’s benefits, although they understand Gary tried to assist.

He did attend the council with Kimberley and asked why he was not getting his rent. The reason rent is not being paid, even if it were available from the council, is the tolerable standard. When Gary recognised the property was not above the tolerable standard, he should have offered a rent reduction immediately. He did not. He kept trying to charge the same rent. If he applies to the Housing and Property Chamber for arrears, we will attend with years of video and audio showing the state of the property, how long we have been deprived of services, the effect on our lives, and the lack of heating. He is not entitled to that rent in the first place.

Gary entered an agreement under which Kimberley was renting the property, including an additional room for overnight stay by a carer. There is a European and domestic line of authority on housing policy, rent arrears and rent relief not being applied properly in favour of pushing disabled people onto Universal Credit. In Scotland the approach has been to put disabled people on Universal Credit and then pay the rent. We say Aberdeen City Council’s conduct has included hate-related treatment, recorded on video, and that they tried to move Kimberley onto Universal Credit before the disability elements were in place. She has been evicted from three addresses because of what we say are ultra vires decisions, contrary to the Scotland Act 1998. That is why council rent has not been paid into Kimberley’s account. Even if it had been, she would have held it until the tolerable standard was met. If the landlord abandoned repairs, she is entitled to instruct a qualified tradesman and apply that month’s rent, and the next month’s if the cost exceeds the £550 that should have been paid.

There is no realistic prospect of Gary succeeding at the Housing and Property Chamber on the evidence we have. When we moved in, we recognised a pattern we had seen with previous landlords and letting agents. I am asking the police to investigate what I believe is organised interference: denial of heating, hot water and cooking facilities, year after year, across many addresses over more than ten years — 23 addresses in 16 years. Some of those landlords and agents later told us that Aberdeen City Council was hostile to us, and that information about me came first from the police and then from the council, which led landlords to treat us abusively: threats, attempts to remove Kimberley from the door while she was having a panic attack, and police turning a blind eye. I want the criminal side of Gary and Alison Smith’s behaviour on a particular date looked at, and the same pattern from landlord to landlord.

The letter says everything worked when the property was let. It might be lawful for an owner-occupier. To put it on the letting market they needed to think about fire doors and the rest of the standards. A joiner did attend today. We allowed access. He was polite. He measured the windows and the door. He measured the door in the wrong place. I pointed out that the original frame is still there, so the new door has to fit from that point. He remeasured and thanked me. He would not have known that, because he had not fitted a door there before and I had. We agreed he would go away and see what he could do. He did not say when he would be back. We have no proper lock security on the door. The solicitors’ advice that the landlord should not speak to us has assisted the abandonment of the property. The shower was fitted one day after about four or five months of calls, and we had largely given up until I was seriously ill. We are used to cold water at many addresses: Boddam in 2018 to 2019, Froghall Terrace from 2019 to 2020, and here from 2020 to date.

We also have recordings of people who were asked to act against us and later spoke more honestly once they saw the effect on Kimberley’s health, including a stroke, and the condition she has been living in. Gary had a duty to assist in preventing antisocial behaviour and to involve the council. The police had a duty too. Gary’s friends have been at this address. One had a key. We have recorded mail being taken and reported it. Police have attended. Credit cards, driving licences, gold rings and stolen mail have been left at the address.

One morning I caught an elderly resident taking everybody’s mail from the communal mailbox, on CCTV. The recording is still on the drive, time-stamped, and bagged with a list of what is on it. Every visit by Gary, and every time he was told about a defect, is on a drive and on other recordings. After she took the mail and shut the box, I went to the door as she left. We often leave the front door open in the morning to air the house, as my mother did, regardless of temperature. The door is open as I speak. I videoed her putting the mail into another container. I kept the camera on it, opened it, and with gloves bagged and sealed everyone’s envelopes, with notes of how it happened. I have put the relevant footage together showing theft, damage, harassment and the same neighbour behaviour we have seen at other addresses after police have spoken to people. Gary is not outside that pattern.

Other landlords have succeeded at the Housing and Property Chamber because legal points sent to the legal chair were never answered. Before a proof, the chair said no legal points had been entered. We have a year and a half of video, audio and recorded calls of clerks not understanding why points were not being answered, and months of clerks emailing, every time we phoned, asking us to correct the spelling and send it back.

On rent, there are cases where a landlord knew of a failed service or appliance, did not fix it promptly, and did not offer a rent reduction. It is the failure to offer the reduction that holds the landlord to account, and the sheriff has treated that as meaning the landlord is not entitled to the full rent. I have that authority and will use it on any Housing and Property Chamber application. We have already lodged a failure-to-repair application and set it out in detail. We have the same problem with email attachments not opening. I am surprised these solicitors could open the link and watch the video, because the Crown, the sheriff court, the tribunal service, Aberdeen City Council, the Sheriff Appeal Court and the High Court have all said they cannot open our attachments. The First-tier Tribunal has said the same in this case. That interference protects Gary.

AI Overview
The word rubio comes from the Latin word rubeus, which means "red". [1]

Etymology and Meaning Evolution
Latin Origin: It derives from rubeus (red or reddish, like a blackberry before it ripens).
Shift in Spanish: Over time in Spanish, the meaning shifted from "red" to describe golden, yellowish, or fair hair and complexions (blond). It historically started as a nickname for someone with red hair, a red beard, or a ruddy complexion before generalizing to fair-haired individuals.
Catalan Variant: In Catalan (Rubió), it can also function as a habitational name taken from places named Rubió in Catalonia.

Red giants are evolved from main-sequence stars with masses in the range from about 0.3 M☉ to around 8 M☉.[13] When a star initially forms from a collapsing molecular cloud in the interstellar medium, it contains primarily hydrogen and helium, with trace amounts of "metals" (in astrophysics, this refers to all elements other than hydrogen and helium). These elements are all uniformly mixed throughout the star. The star "enters" the main sequence when its core reaches a temperature (several million kelvins) high enough to begin fusing hydrogen-1 (the predominant isotope), and establishes hydrostatic equilibrium. (In astrophysics, stellar fusion is often referred to as "burning", with hydrogen fusion sometimes termed "hydrogen burning".) Over its main sequence life, the star slowly fuses the hydrogen in the core into helium; its main-sequence life ends when nearly all the hydrogen in the core has been fused. For the Sun, the main-sequence lifetime is approximately 10 billion years. More massive stars burn their fuel disproportionately faster and so have a shorter lifetime than less massive stars.[14]

When the star has mostly exhausted the hydrogen fuel in its core, the core's rate of nuclear reactions declines, and thus so do the radiation and thermal pressure the core generates, which are what support the star against gravitational contraction. The star further contracts, increasing the pressures and thus temperatures inside the star (as described by the ideal gas law). Eventually a "shell" layer around the core reaches temperatures sufficient to fuse hydrogen and thus generate its own radiation and thermal pressure, which "re-inflates" the star's outer layers and causes them to expand.[15] The hydrogen-burning shell results in a situation that has been described as the mirror principle: when the core within the shell contracts, the layers of the star outside the shell must expand. The detailed physical processes that cause this are complex. Still, the behavior is necessary to satisfy simultaneous conservation of gravitational and thermal energy in a star with the shell structure. The core contracts and heats up due to the lack of fusion, and so the outer layers of the star expand greatly, absorbing most of the extra energy from shell fusion. This process of cooling and expanding is the subgiant stage. When the envelope of the star cools sufficiently it becomes convective, the star stops expanding, its luminosity starts to increase, and the star is ascending the red-giant branch of the Hertzsprung–Russell (H–R) diagram.[14][16]

**Quran**  
- Frequent reminders of human weakness and need for divine help (e.g., **4:28**: “And Allah wants to lighten for you [your difficulties]; and mankind was created weak”).  
- The overall narrative stresses dependence on Allah rather than self-reliance.

**Bible**  
- **Romans 7:18–25 / Galatians 5:17**: The flesh desires what is contrary to the Spirit; the struggle within.  
- **2 Corinthians 12:9**: “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.”  
- **Matthew 26:41**: “The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

### 6. The Temple Veil and the Son (Bible-specific)
Your closing line—“And the Son of Allah Delights in the veil upon his Temple”—most directly evokes Christian interpretation of the events at the crucifixion:

- **Matthew 27:50–51** (ESV/NIV): “And Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and yielded up his spirit. And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom. And the earth shook, and the rocks were split.” (Parallel accounts in Mark 15:37–38 and Luke 23:44–46.)  

In Christian theology this tearing (from top to bottom) signifies that the barrier between God and humanity has been removed through the death of Jesus, the Son of God. Hebrews 10:19–20 elaborates: believers now have “confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way opened for us through the curtain, that is, his body.”

The Quran does not contain a parallel narrative about a Temple veil or a “Son of Allah”; classical Islamic teaching affirms Jesus (Isa) as a prophet and Messiah but rejects divine sonship (e.g., Quran 4:171, 5:72–75, 112:1–4).

### Additional Notes on Context and Use
- Both scriptures repeatedly link **resistance to evil** with **positive practices** (charity, prayer, seeking knowledge/wisdom, honoring parents, trusting divine provision). The “war” is fought more through fidelity, generosity, and dependence on God than through mere opposition.  
- Wisdom literature (Proverbs in the Bible; numerous Quranic calls to reflect and seek knowledge, e.g., 2:269 on wisdom as a great good) supports the call to clear judgment unclouded by nostalgia and to seek knowledge in “the halls of great tidings.”  
- Translations vary slightly in wording; consulting multiple reliable versions or original languages (Arabic for Quran, Greek/Hebrew for Bible) can deepen study. Commentaries (Ibn Kathir for Quran; standard evangelical or historical-critical for Bible) provide further layers.

These passages offer a rich scriptural foundation for the themes of spiritual resistance, charitable action that delights the divine, maternal/parental wisdom, trust in provision, recognition of human weakness, and (in the Christian tradition) the significance of the torn veil. If you would like fuller quotations, specific tafsirs/commentaries, related hadiths, additional verses on any single theme, or help comparing particular passages side-by-side, let me know.

'Chalchiuhtlicue's relation to Tlaloc (the rain god) and the Tlaloques (lesser storm gods) varies with the sources. Some call her Tlaloc's wife, others the elder sister of Taloc and the Tlaloques and still others their mother. Like them, she resided inside mountains. From these cavernous containers, Chalchiuhtlicue released groundwater, with both positive and negative effects. She could send calm water gently splashing and splattering the shore or rough waters that could be threatening, tossing people about or crushing those in its path, overturning boats and drowning people. Among the Tlaxcalans, she was known as Matlacueye (She of the Blue Skirt) and was believed to live on the highest mountain in that region, known today as Malinche.

Chalchiuhtlicue was celebrated during the 6th and 16th veintenas (Etzalcualiztli and Atemoztli). The feast of Etzalcualiztli is described in detail by Sahagún. People formed the image of the goddess over a framework of wood and placed offerings in front of her in a temple called Tlalocan. Priests strewed the herb yauhtli before her and then sacrificed a female slave provided by the water merchants and those who owned boats. Moctezuma is said to have especially honored Chalchiuhtlicue. He offered incense and beheaded a quail in front of her: a significant gesture, as the king's penance before the goddess would assure water for his people. Sahagún remarks on the enormous reverence that this goddess received from the native peoples.'

text:
A 24-year-old founder burned $1,000 acquiring customers who paid him $100.

He was weeks away from running out of cash.

Then a 3-minute screen recording unlocked 70,000 signups in 24 hours without spending a single dollar on ads.

Drew Houston exposed this exact nightmare at Stanford:

In 2007, Dropbox was struggling. The classic marketing playbook said: "Buy Google AdWords to drive traffic."

Houston spent thousands on search ads. 

The result was a total disaster: 
• Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): $1,000+
• Product Price: $99/year

Dropbox was literally paying $900 out of pocket for every single customer they gained.

They were burning cash on paid ads for a product that people didn't even know they needed.

Search ads require someone to SEARCH for a specific solution. But nobody was searching for "cloud storage" in 2007 because the category didn't exist yet.

Houston scrapped the entire ad budget and built a simple 3-minute screen recording.

He demoed Dropbox in action, dropping inside jokes and memes tailored specifically for the Digg community.

Overnight, the beta waitlist exploded from 5,000 to 75,000 people. Zero ad spend.

You are making this exact same suicidal mistake in your business right now:

• You have a conversion problem, but you keep buying more paid traffic.
• You spend $200 to acquire a client who yields $50 a year in profit.
• You assume that "more traffic" will magically fix a broken acquisition channel.

If your customer doesn’t know your solution exists, throwing more dollars at Google or Meta won't save you.

Fix your acquisition before you go broke:
1. Stop paying for traffic until your organic conversion actually works.
2. SHOW the transformation in 60 seconds instead of explaining it in a wall of text.
3. Put your offer in front of communities where your exact target audience already hangs out.

Bookmark this before your next "we just need a bigger ad budget" meeting destroys your runway.

The tragic crash of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 in Ondo State has left our nation grief-stricken, and I write with a heavy heart to mourn one of our own.

Squadron Leader Ahamefule Aham Man-Ugwueje, an indigene of Umuahia in Abia State, was among those who did not return from that ill-fated flight. He was a young man of promise, a trained pilot who wore his uniform with pride, and a newly married husband whose future was only just beginning to unfold. That death should snatch him away so soon is a loss that stings deeply.

To his young wife, his grieving family, and the people of Umuahia, I offer my sincere sympathy. Abia State shares in your pain. We have lost not just a pilot, but a representative of the courage and excellence that our state is known for.

My condolences also go to the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and to the households of the other 24 victims whose loved ones will never come home. This tragedy has touched families across the country, and we stand with them all.

It is my prayer that God, who alone understands the mystery of life and death, will wrap His arms around every mourner and grant the departed souls peaceful rest.

Rt. Hon. Barr. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha.

text:
“WE CAN’T EAT ROAD SALT.” THE LINE WENT VIRAL. BUT WHAT DID SUSAN COLLINS ACTUALLY SAY?

Updated: October 7, 2026

Five words from Maine’s first Senate debate are racing across social media:

“We can’t eat road salt.”

Democrat Troy Jackson delivered the line after Republican Sen. Susan Collins defended her work getting Canadian road salt and other products exempted from U.S. tariffs.

The exchange is real.

But Collins did NOT tell Mainers to eat road salt—and one viral moment does not tell us who won the debate, much less the election.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

During Tuesday night’s debate, Collins argued that she opposed the trade fight with Canada while working to reduce its effects on Maine.

She pointed to exemptions for road salt and other products and described one small Maine town that she said would have faced roughly $10,000 in additional winter salt costs.

Jackson responded:

“I didn't mock the fact that she got road salt back. I mocked the fact that—what about everything else? We can't eat road salt.”

The broader debate centered on Trump, tariffs, Iran, abortion and the cost of living.

AP:
https://t.co/oUEysrPubG

THE CONTEXT THE CLIP DOESN’T SHOW

The road-salt relief itself is real.

On September 8, Collins announced that road salt and cement had been exempted from the Canadian tariffs after she pressed the administration. Her office specifically cited Frenchville, Maine, as facing approximately $10,000 in additional road-salt costs.

But Collins also acknowledged that significant tariffs remained, including tariffs affecting forest products.

Sen. Susan Collins:
https://t.co/9jdDN6FnyG

That makes Jackson’s argument clearer: he wasn’t claiming the road-salt exemption was fake. He was arguing that specific exemptions were too small compared with the broader economic burden.

THE TEMPERATURE GAP

The viral version can make the exchange sound like Collins offered road salt as an answer to grocery prices.

She didn't.

Collins was pointing to specific tariff relief as evidence that she had delivered tangible savings for Maine.

Jackson challenged the SCALE of that accomplishment: what about everything still subject to higher costs?

Those are two legitimate arguments—and very different from “Collins told Mainers to eat road salt.”

EVIDENCE STATUS

CONFIRMED: Jackson said, “We can't eat road salt.”

CONFIRMED: Collins cited tariff exemptions during the debate.

CONFIRMED: Collins’s September 8 announcement documents exemptions for road salt and cement.

CONFIRMED: Collins’s office cited approximately $10,000 in additional road-salt costs facing Frenchville without the exemption.

CONFIRMED: Collins’s office also acknowledged that significant tariffs, including on forest products, remained.

NOT ESTABLISHED: That this exchange changed the race, determined who won the debate, or tells us who will win November 3.

TRUTH MATTERS TAKEAWAY

The five-word comeback was real.

So was the road-salt exemption it was responding to.

Jackson’s argument was that specific exemptions don't address the much larger affordability problem. Collins’s argument was that getting specific costs removed matters to Maine communities.

A viral clip can capture a powerful moment.

It can't replace the rest of the evidence.

Facts first. Context second. You decide.

#TruthMattersNews #Maine #Midterms2026 #SusanCollins #TroyJackson

text:
Idealists believe the rule book protects people. Realists know the rule book is only as strong as the person enforcing it.

In Mississippi Burning (1988), FBI Agents Ward and Anderson arrive in Mississippi to investigate the murder of three civil rights workers. Agent Ward relies on federal authority, procedure, and institutional pressure. But Agent Anderson (Gene Hackman) a former Southern sheriff knows a brutal truth: when the local lawmen are the criminals, relying on formal protocol is just a slower way to lose.

In this scene, Anderson steps into a local club filled with hostile officers and Klansmen. He doesn’t offer a speech on civil rights or cite federal statutes. He speaks their language, reads their dynamic, and directly asserts physical dominance to break their illusion of immunity.

It highlights an uncomfortable truth about systemic corruption: entrenched power rarely yields to moral appeals or paperwork. It only yields when it meets a force it can’t intimidate.

When confronting an entrenched, corrupt system, does strictly following the rules preserve institutional integrity or does it just protect the perpetrators ?

Your post relies poorly and leans on several weak inferences. The sinus point has some outside expert support; the rest of the narrative does not.

Hitchens’s Razor (“what can be asserted without evidence can be dismissed without evidence”) puts the burden on the person making the claim. @LobesPoet asserts a specific mechanism (drunk, shorts partly raised, slip off the ocean side of a boat into shallow water while defecating), a transfer of New England coastal drowning patterns to this case, advanced decomposition after 30–34 hours in 85° water as decisive, and that two medical examiners “missed” or “hid” evidence by not examining the paranasal/sphenoid sinuses. Those are positive claims. “Prove me wrong” reverses the burden.

What is actually on the public record for Nolan Wells :

Both the state medical examiner and the independent pathologist hired for the family (Roger Mitchell) listed cause and manner as undetermined. Limitations cited included decomposition, a second autopsy, inability to fully examine airway/lungs/stomach contents, and incomplete toxicology at the time of the independent exam.
A grand jury later described the circumstances as consistent with drowning (a diagnosis of exclusion) and found insufficient evidence of criminal conduct. Bruising on the back of the head was noted and not treated as fatal; a witness described an awkward slip from a boat earlier, after which Wells continued socializing.
A separate forensic pathologist (Priya Banerjee), reviewing the state report for People, said the sphenoid sinus was not mentioned and that fluid there can support active aspiration. That narrower criticism is not invented by the your account.

Literature on paranasal-sinus fluid is mixed in a way the post flattens. Meta-analyses find a strong association between sinus fluid and drowning and treat absence as useful for ruling drowning out in some settings. Other work (including experimental postmortem submersion) finds passive influx from being underwater, volume changes with handling, and limited ability to separate drowning from postmortem immersion—especially once putrefaction is advanced. Absence of a documented sinus exam is a legitimate criticism of completeness; it does not by itself prove the examiners concealed a definitive finding, nor that Wells entered the water already dead.

●Logical problems in the post:

•Appeal to ancestry / borrowed authority: relatives’ combined 53 years as pathologists, plus “case studies brought home,” is not a qualification and does not outweigh the two pathologists who examined this body.
•Anecdote as mechanism: the New England “party cove / dump off the boat” story is presented as the typical pathway and then mapped onto Wells without case-specific evidence (location is the Mississippi Gulf, not coastal Maine–Connecticut; water temperature and recovery interval are asserted, not shown from the reports).
•False dichotomy and overclaim: non-examination of the sinuses is treated as if it must have produced either “definitive accidental drowning” or proof of death before entry. Forensic sources treat sinus fluid as supportive, not pathognomonic, and note passive entry and putrefaction as confounders.
•Moving the goalposts on expertise: disagreement with the examiners is offered as proof the poster is “more knowledgeable,” which is circular.

text:
You don’t desire “being a mom” in the simple way this sentence imagines.

You desire a Fantasy called motherhood.

That doesn’t make the Desire false. It means you’ve confused the reality of Desire with the truth of its explanation.

You have never met your child. You don’t know its Face, its voice, what it will love, whether it will resemble you, reject you, disappoint you, surpass you, or become something your present Fantasy cannot tolerate. The Being whose existence would actually make you a mother is presently absent.

So what exactly are you desiring?

An image. A future. A relation without its second term. A child-shaped opening in Fantasy.

And you certainly did not sit outside yourself and choose that Desire. Desire arrived first. Then the “I” looked backward, found itself already oriented toward an absent future, and said: I want to be a mom.

That sentence is not the origin of the Desire. It is the story the Being tells after Desire has already bent its World.

This becomes stranger when you put birth beside death. You cannot experience your own absence, yet you know a future exists in which you will be absent. A child offers one of the most powerful mirrors imaginable for that impossibility: a Being who may enter the future through you without being you.

That is why I wouldn’t sentimentalize this.

Parenthood is ontologically terrifying.

You imagine that you desire a child, and if the child arrives, reality answers by producing someone you could never have imagined completely. Pregnancy can place another Body literally inside yours, and birth then performs the impossible-looking operation: what was inside becomes outside without ceasing to matter as part of you.

The Fantasy says: I want to become a mother.

Then another Being arrives and asks:

Did you want me—or did you want the person you imagined I would allow you to become?

That’s where motherhood actually begins.

And please stop calling yourself “delulu.” You are almost impressively basic.

Stanford. AI. Frontier technology. Open source. Abundance. Wanting children. Wanting those children to inherit a beautiful technological future. Reading respectable philosophy books and then publicly emphasizing that reading, philosophy and intellectual curiosity are important—as though being the educated person who thinks everyone should read more is itself somehow against the grain.

This is an archetype.

You aren’t delulu. You are extraordinarily legible. Even your ‘rebellion’ is socially legible. “I care about ideas instead of status.” “I read philosophy.” “Technology can create abundance.” “I want to be a mother.” “I believe in intellectual curiosity.” There are thousands of intelligent people constructing almost exactly this Face.

Cool. But don’t confuse having an intellectual aesthetic with being difficult for reality to categorize.

You are basic.

Language understands you. Silicon Valley understands you. Academia understands you. The government understands you.

Even the X algorithm understands you.

In fact, it understands you so well that it apparently understood me well enough to put your post in front of me because it knew your pseudo-intellectual optimism would annoy me.

Think about how funny that is. The machine can already model the distance between your Fantasy and mine well enough to manufacture an encounter between us.

There is practically a dropdown menu for every major thing you presently claim to want.

Someone like me is actually beyond delulu. Not because I put “delulu” in a post, but because I keep producing claims, businesses, books, systems and categories that don’t fit comfortably inside the available Names—and then occasionally produce enough evidence that people are forced to reconsider whether the original absurdity was absurd.

That’s the funny part. Calling yourself delulu has itself become one of the safest ways to signal that you’re not.

Your Fantasy is already culturally available to you.

Mine keeps requiring new words.

text:
On energy, Greece is emerging as a vital hub for Southeastern and Central Europe infrastructure, such as the Alexandroupolis FSRU.  Together with our leading role in the Vertical Corridor, this diversifying supply is strengthening resilience and giving our neighbors greater energy security.  The growing engagement of U.S. energy companies, including Severn and ExxonMobil, underscores confidence, increases potential, (inaudible) the opportunities our partnership offers.   

Our maritime strength are the third strategic dimension.  With Greek-owned vessels accounting for almost one-fourth of global energy shipping capacity globally, Greek shipping plays a pivotal role in connecting energy producers with consumers and sustaining transatlantic energy flows.  The transformation of the Greek economy has opened a new chapter in our bilateral relationship.  Renewed growth and investment confidence are creating opportunities for American businesses to participate in Greece’s progress.   

Investment by leading U.S. technology companies in data centers’ digital infrastructure is helping to establish Greece as a regional center for innovation.  Our ambition is to build on this momentum through partnerships that create skilled jobs, support research, and bring new opportunities to the next generation.   

At the heart of this relationship, however, are our people.  The Greek American community has helped shape America while sustaining a close and abiding connection with Greece.  Its achievements in business, science, public service, and the arts are a source of pride for both our nations.  Greek Americans have made Greece’s heritage part of America’s success.  They embody a relationship rooted in the ideals of liberty, democracy, and the rule of law, ideals that inspired America’s Founding Fathers and continue to give our partnership purpose.  Our expanding education and cultural exchanges carry this connection forward, allowing young Greeks and Americans to learn from one another and to build relationships of their own.   

Mr. Secretary, I look forward to our discussions today and to the practical results that we deliver.  We have a strong foundation and a clear sense of what we can achieve.  Today’s discussion will help us turn that shared ambition into practical results.  Our alliance draws strength – draws strength from all we have achieved together.  Its promise lies in what we choose to do next.  Thank you. 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, thank you.  Thank you for this opportunity to be here today for the sixth time a U.S. secretary of state gathers with their counterparts in Greece for this Strategic Dialogue.  And I’m happy to be here in Greece for that dialogue.  It’s my first trip to the country ever; I didn’t even have a chance to come as a senator.  And so I’m happy to be here and to be a part of this Strategic Dialogue.   

I want to begin by saying that I hope our presence here today and our work that we’re about to do – and continue to do together – highlights something very important, and that is how critical the historic alliance between Greece and the United States is.  And this is especially true now at a time of great global uncertainty, whether it’s the war between Russia and Ukraine, whether it’s what’s happening in the Middle East, whether it’s – meaning in the Straits of Hormuz and, increasingly now, in the Red Sea because of the Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

text:
NEBIUS $NBIS RAISED ITS CHIP-RENTAL PRICES ABOUT 20%. IT STILL BORROWS THE MONEY TO BUY THE CHIPS:

Nebius Group (NBIS) at $249.87, +$17.30 / +7.44% on Tuesday, and $244.50 premarket, -$5.37 / -2.15% from that close.

Among the six names below, the fuel and shipping stocks sit within 3% of their highs. The names that sell money - lenders, payments, advisers - sit 13% to 32% under theirs. Nebius straddles the line: it rents out something in short supply, chip time, and borrows to build it.

The Amsterdam company rents computing power, racks of AI chips, to AI model builders. It is #8 of 30 on the Hypergrowth Len5, and the June quarter reported August 12 is why: sales of $582M, +454%. Tuesday's jump came with the rest of AI infrastructure, and with news of its own:

- BNP Paribas raised its rating to Outperform from Neutral.
- An October 1 price list took its H200 chip rental from $4.50 to $5.40 an hour, +20%, the second increase since May.
- It bought Inferize, a startup that trims idle chip time.

The bill, at June 30 and for the first half:

- Cash $8.04B; long-term debt $8.50B.
- Capital spending $8.13B vs $4.50B of cash from operations. The 2026 plan is $20B-$25B.
- June-quarter net loss: $190M, or $0.68 a share.

Verdict: demand is proven, and funding is the test. Third-quarter report tentatively November 10.

MOMENTUM LEN5:

- Marathon Petroleum (MPC) at $432.36, -$1.11 / -0.26% on Tuesday, #9 of 30. The Ohio refiner makes gasoline and diesel. This Len5 tracks stocks climbing for months with short and long gains agreeing: past month +11.2%, three months +60.7%, six months +79.1%, and 1.2% under Monday's record. The driver is the refining margin, what a barrel earns after the crude cost: $36.33 in the June quarter vs $17.58 a year earlier. October 1 brought a 6.3% jump. The Energy Information Administration's count for the week ended September 25 had gasoline stocks down about 1.7M barrels and distillate, mostly diesel, down about 2.3M, and Chinese refiners paused October fuel exports. What would knock it off the Momentum Len5: a close under $395.42, September's last, which erases that jump. Verdict: the stock follows fuel margins, which report November 3.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:

- PayPal Holdings (PYPL) at $54.61, +$0.20 / +0.37% on Tuesday, #13 of 73. The San Jose payments company runs Venmo and Braintree. This Len5 wants a durable business at a discount; PayPal fits the discount half, at about 10 times past-year profit, and grades mid-tier on quality. Privately held Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International bid $60.50 a share on July 15 and walked away in late August; the stock fell 12.7% on August 28. Tuesday's close is still 15% above July 14's $47.37, with no offer on the table. June quarter, reported July 28: revenue $8.68B, +5%; transaction margin dollars, what it keeps per payment after processing costs, $3.9B, +1%. What would knock it off the Quality-Value Len5: that profit measure shrinking from a year ago on October 27. Verdict: cheap because sales grow five times faster than the profit it keeps.

DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:

- Raymond James (RJF) at $159.43, -$1.37 / -0.85% on Tuesday, #7 of 192. The Florida firm runs financial advisers, an investment bank and a bank. This Len5 waits for a top-quality business to trade well below a cautious value of its earnings; RJF sits 13% under its August 6 high at about 14 times past-year profit. June quarter, reported July 22: record revenue $3.93B, +16%; record profit $3.01 a share, +42%. What would knock it off the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5: losses in its $56.2B bank loan book, which would crack the quality half. Verdict: a record quarter at an ordinary price; analysts expect $3.33 a share on Wednesday, October 28, vs $3.11.

GROWTH LEN5:

- Enova International (ENVA) at $182.88, +$4.88 / +2.74% on Tuesday, #4 of 30. The Chicago online lender serves borrowers with weaker credit. This Len5 wants profit rising year after year at a price that has not caught up. On September 14 Enova withdrew its applications to buy New York digital bank Grasshopper Bancorp, a $369M deal. The stock fell 23.4% the next day. It sits 32% under August 14's high, at about 13 times past-year profit. The business did not slip. June quarter, reported July 23: loans made $2.3B, +27%; profit $4.00 a share, +40%. What would knock it off the Growth Len5: write-offs, loans given up as uncollectable, rising above June's 7.3% of loans. Verdict: a growth lender priced like a failed deal; analysts expect adjusted profit of $4.36 a share on Thursday, October 22 (tentative), vs $3.36.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:

- Nebius, #8 of 30. This Len5 hunts very fast sales growth with years of it behind. Annualized run-rate sales, the latest pace stretched over a year, reached $3B at June 30, +56% from March. The company targets $3.0B-$3.4B of 2026 sales and a $7B-$9B run rate by December, with contracted orders above $40B. What would knock it off the Hypergrowth Len5: a cut to that run-rate target, or sales growth fading well below June's pace. Verdict: growth is not the doubt; paying for it is.

INCOME LEN5:

- Global Ship Lease (GSL) at $45.50, -$0.36 / -0.78% on Tuesday, #1 of 30, and 2.3% under its September high. The Athens company owns containerships and leases them to shipping lines on fixed-rate contracts. This Len5 wants a payout the business covers with room to spare: the $0.625 quarterly dividend is a 5.5% yield and about a quarter of June-quarter profit, $2.48 a share. All of 2026 and 90% of 2027 is already under contract. What would knock it off the Income Len5: a dividend trimmed to help pay for 15 new ships ordered for $1.33B, or 2027's open ships re-renting at lower rates. Verdict: paid from contracts signed in advance; third-quarter report tentatively November 9.

The market is paying up for scarcity and marking down money. Nebius sells the first and rents the second, and its price sits between the two.

Not investment advice.

text:
Setting aside the particulars of this horrible and active case, it’s a grotesque and offensive generalisation to say that “the problem is, and has always been, men”.

How is such a sweeping statement fundamentally different, in its prejudicial nature, from saying the problem is, and has always been, immigrants, the Irish, or women, for that matter? All are sweeping statements devoid of nuance.

And even if you regard all men as potential killers, surely you must acknowledge that the arrival of tens of thousands of unvetted men from countries with deeply regressive cultures, where women have few or no rights, risks exacerbating violence against women and girls.

As a man, I’m completely in favour of safeguarding women on the basis of biological sex, and I readily acknowledge that a significant minority of men pose a threat to women. But I have no time for those who demonise men as a single cohort.

It helps no one. Worse, it risks driving more young men into the arms of bad actors who offer them belonging rather than condemning them simply on the grounds of their sex.

A GP. A mother of three. Dead in her own home in Dersingham, a mile from Sandringham, while she was hosting a sleepover for her children’s friends.

Police called at 2.20am. Children taken out of the house to safety. A man in his 40s arrested on suspicion of murder.

She had left a previous practice to spend more time with her young family. Neighbours say she was a lovely woman. They also say this is the sort of village where you can leave the car unlocked all night and nothing happens.

That Britain is gone.

Not in a city centre at closing time. In a detached house backing onto the King’s estate, during a kids’ sleepover. If a family doctor is not safe in her own home in a “crime-free” Norfolk village, stop telling people the danger is somewhere else.

The suspect has not been named. The investigation is at the start. None of that changes what those children were in the house for.

Rest in peace, Dr Hannah Terry.

Frank’s Attorneys Challenge Two Jurors and Raise 115 Grounds for a New Trial

On Wednesday, October 1, 1913, The Atlanta Journal reported Leo M. Frank’s attorneys had served Solicitor General Hugh M. Dorsey with an amended motion seeking a new trial. The motion raised 115 separate grounds and covered approximately 200 legal-cap pages. Attorney Luther Z. Rosser prepared the motion, which challenged evidentiary rulings, jury instructions, Dorsey’s courtroom conduct, and the impartiality of two jurors.

The defense alleged J. A. Henslee and Johenning had concluded Frank was guilty and expressed those opinions prior to their selection. Supporting affidavits were promised. The article reported the defense’s accusations without establishing their truth or describing a ruling on them.

The motion also attacked the admission of Jim Conley’s testimony and portions of the testimony of practically every State witness. Other objections concerned evidence about Frank’s character, Dr. Harris’s testimony, questions reflecting on defense witness Herbert Schiff’s honesty, and the exclusion of Rabbi Marx’s proposed explanation of B’nai B’rith’s activities.

Courtroom conditions occupied another substantial part of the defense’s argument. The attorneys alleged applause and hostility among spectators had threatened Frank’s opportunity for a fair trial. They challenged Judge Leonard S. Roan’s refusal to clear the courtroom or declare a mistrial and argued his warnings had been inadequate. The motion also objected to alleged misquotations of evidence in Dorsey’s argument and requested instructions concerning Conley as an alternative suspect and corroboration of testimony from a witness who had sworn falsely.

A separate portion of the report discussed who would hear the motion. Roan was expected to handle it despite his appointment to the Georgia Court of Appeals and Judge B. H. Hill’s transfer to the Fulton Superior Court. The hearing was scheduled for the following Saturday, but the newspaper anticipated a delay because Dorsey had received the papers only on Wednesday.

References

The Atlanta Journal. (1913, October 1, Wednesday). New trial asked on 115 counts by Frank’s attorneys. pp. 1, 16. Article text identifies page 1, column 7, and page 16, column 5. Based on the transcription provided, which contains incomplete passages.

Citing 115 separate counts and attacking two of the jurors, counsel for Leo M. Frank on Wednesday served on the solicitor general their amended motion for a new trial for the man convicted of Mary Phagan’s murder.

The motion recites that the court erred repeatedly, not only by refusing to rule out evidence introduced by the solicitor general, but by refusing to admit testimony offered by the defense; by refusing to incorporate certain points in his charge to the jury and for refusing to rebuke the solicitor general for statements made in the cross examination of witnesses and in his argument.

The petition alleges that two of the jurors, J. A. Henslee and Johenning were prejudiced against Frank before they were selected and both had arrived at the definite conclusion that he was guilty and had so expressed themselves.

Affidavit to support this contention will be introduced.

Every Witness Attacked

In fact portions of the testimony of practically every state’s witness were inadmissible, the motion declares, and the court erred in allowing them to go to the jury.

Portions of the testimony of Dr. Harris should have been stricken, it is argued.

Many of the several hundred pages of the amendment are devoted to an argument that the court erred in refusing to clear the court room and in refusing to declare a mistrial on the several occasions that the defense made such motions.

The court room should have been cleared, it is argued, because such a feeling against the defendant had been aroused among the spectators that it was a menace to the jury and a fair and impartial trial could not be given the defendant.

Despite the protest of counsel for the defense there was continuous applause, when the points were scored by the prosecution, it is argued.

Passion and Prejudice

Passion and prejudice had been so aroused in the court room that the defendant could not be given a fair trial and the court’s threats to clear the court were entirely inadequate.

The court erred, it is charged, in failing to clear the room, when the crowd laughed when Dr. Harris gave a tart answer to one of Mr. Arnold’s questions.

The court erred in failing to rebuke Solicitor Dorsey when by his question he cast reflections upon the honesty of Herbert Schiff, a defense witness.

The court erred; it is argued, in refusing to allow Rabbi Marx to testify that the B’nai B’rith, while a benevolent organization, does not assist people charged with violation of the criminal statutes.

The court erred in refusing to rebuke Dorsey when he declared that he was not “four-flushing” on his ability to damn Frank’s character.

That the court erred in not charging to the jury that if the hypothesis that Jim Conley could have committed the crime as well as Frank had not been eliminated that then they should discharge the defendant.

That the court erred in refusing to rebuke Solicitor Dorsey for many alleged misquotations of the evidence, which are all cited, in his argument.

That the court erred in not charging to the jury that if the hypothesis that Jim Conley could have committed the crime as well as Frank had not been eliminated that then they should discharge the defendant.

That the court erred in refusing to rebuke Solicitor Dorsey for many alleged misquotations of the evidence, which are all cited, in his argument.

That the court erred by admitting the testimony of several young women relative to Frank’s general relations with women, and by allowing Solicitor Dorsey to ask certain questions relative to alleged immorality of Frank before the time of the tragedy.

That the court erred in failing to charge that the jury need not believe that testimony of a witness, who admits that he was sworn falsely unless that testimony is corroborated.

Although Conley is not mentioned here it is clear that it is to him that the defense refers.

The motion for a new trial covers

(Continued on last, page, Col 5.)

New Trial Asked on 115 Counts by Frank’s Attorneys

about 200 legal cap pages.

It was served by the solicitor Wednesday together with the defense’s chief of the evidence, which is also several hundred pages long.

The motion was prepared by Attorney L. Z. Rosser.

Judge Roan Will Probably Hear Motion

It seems now to be indicated that Judge L. S. Roan, who presided over the trial of Leo M. Frank will hear the motion of the convicted man’s attorneys for a new trial of the charge.

It is regarded as certain that he will hear it unless the hearing is delayed beyond one week from next Monday.

The indication lies in the fact that on this approaching Monday begins the October term of the state court of appeals, to which Judge Roan has been appointed and from which Judge B. H. Hill has been transferred to the Fulton superior court.

But the call of the calendar of cases before the court of appeals is set for the following Monday.

In the interim the court will devote itself to cases already heard, in order that Judge Hill may complete his work in the court before he retired from it.

It is in that interim that the Frank motion very probably will be heard.

The hearing is set for next Saturday, but there is said to be little probability that Solicitor General H. M. Dorsey will be ready then to answer it, he not having been served with a copy of it before Wednesday.
