text:
Frank Seeks a New Trial on 115 Grounds

On Wednesday, October 1, 1913, The Atlanta Georgian reported Luther Z. Rosser had filed an amended motion seeking a new trial for Leo M. Frank, convicted of murdering Mary Phagan. The motion occupied nearly 200 typewritten pages and raised 115 grounds for challenging the trial. Twenty-five pages addressed objections to Solicitor Hugh Dorsey’s closing argument.

The defense accused jurors Marcus Johenning and J. A. Henslee of holding prejudiced opinions when selected and announced affidavits would support the accusation. It also alleged courtroom applause, jeering, and public demonstrations had intimidated the jury. The newspaper described these claims as grounds advanced by Frank’s attorneys, with their merits still awaiting the court’s decision.

Other objections concerned Jim Conley’s testimony, evidence about Frank’s character and alleged conduct with women, Dr. H. F. Harris’s examination of Mary Phagan’s stomach contents, streetcar schedules, factory clocks, and testimony describing Frank’s nervousness. The defense also challenged references to B’nai Brith, the Pinkerton investigation, and comparisons between Frank’s case and other criminal prosecutions. Requested jury instructions addressed reasonable doubt, the possibility of Conley’s guilt, and corroboration if the jury considered Conley an accomplice.

The hearing was scheduled for Saturday, October 4, although Dorsey was expected to seek additional time to investigate the motion and prepare his response. The Georgian reported Judge Leonard S. Roan intended to hear the motion and finish his work on the case prior to leaving the Superior Court bench.

Editorial note

The accompanying text consolidates the available October 1 reporting into one readable account. Repeated passages have been removed and unique details retained. It is an edited composite of several versions, rather than a verbatim transcription of a single newspaper page.

References

The Atlanta Georgian. (1913, October 1, Wednesday). Rosser ready, Roan will hear Frank argument and related coverage of Frank’s motion for a new trial. Mary Phagan Kean Legacy Project. https://t.co/Wawc0w71B2

TRANSCRIPT

The Atlanta Georgian

Wednesday, October 1, 1913

Leo Frank’s Motion for a New Trial: Consolidated Coverage

Editorial note

This consolidated text brings together the October 1, 1913 Frank new-trial coverage represented in the available transcriptions of The Atlanta Georgian. Repeated passages have been removed, overlapping accounts combined, and additional information retained. Where versions differ in detail, the fuller account has generally been used. The two related notices concerning the county jail and a juror’s mother appear separately at the end.

Period wording has been retained as closely as possible, with corrections to transcription errors, spelling, punctuation, and broken sentences. “Fourflushing” is retained without a hyphen. The allegations and legal arguments reported below are those attributed to Frank’s defense. Their inclusion does not establish their truth or indicate how the court ultimately ruled.

This is an edited composite, not a verbatim transcription of one newspaper page or edition. The supplied transcription contains damaged wording in the paragraph concerning corroboration of Conley’s testimony. The reading reproduced here removes a repeated phrase, but the exact wording of that sentence remains subject to verification against the newspaper image. Page and column labels have been omitted because this combined text does not follow the arrangement of any single printed version.

Rosser Ready, Roan Will Hear Frank Argument

The announcement that the papers in the motion for a new trial would be filed Wednesday was made Tuesday by Attorney Luther Rosser. “We have been hard at work on our evidence for weeks,” said Mr. Rosser, “and have now just about completed it. It is practically certain that we will file the papers Wednesday.”

Regardless of the success or failure of Solicitor Hugh Dorsey to prepare his answer by Saturday, the date set for the hearing, Judge L. S. Roan will hear the motion and dispose of the case before he retires from the Superior bench, according to authoritative information Tuesday.

This final decision is in deference to the expressed desire of Judge Roan, who was quoted exclusively in The Georgian last week to the effect that he felt it his duty to finish up the Frank case before retiring in accordance with the wishes of all other officials concerned. Solicitor Dorsey is anxious for Judge Roan to hear the motion in view of the fact that Judge Roan is familiar with every phase of the famous case.

Judge Roan, as trial judge, generally has been regarded as the logical man to dispose of the case. The Superior Court judges are said to be a unit in that opinion.

Dorsey Prepares Vigorous Fight on Frank Motion

Solicitor Hugh Dorsey Wednesday prepared to make a vigorous assault on the arguments set forth in the motion for a new trial for Leo M. Frank, sentenced to hang on October 10 for the murder of Mary Phagan. The papers were expected to be filed by attorneys for the defense probably early Wednesday afternoon.

Postponement of the hearing Saturday appeared certain Wednesday morning prior to the filing of the papers. Mr. Dorsey declared he would go into an investigation of the papers immediately in an effort to make his reply at the earliest possible moment.

It is hardly likely, however, that Mr. Dorsey will be able to prepare his answer by Saturday, as the papers are said to be quite lengthy and filled with evidence which probably will require the summoning of witnesses from various parts of the State. It is likely, therefore, that the Solicitor will request a postponement of the hearing until he can complete his side of the case.

In this event the motion probably will be heard within the next week or ten days before Judge Roan, who, according to every reliable indication, will dispose of the Frank case before he retires from the bench.

Ask New Frank Trial on 115 Counts

Citing 115 counts wherein the court is declared to have erred in the trial of Leo M. Frank, Luther Z. Rosser Wednesday filed with the criminal court an amended motion for a new trial for the pencil factory superintendent.

The motion, contained in nearly two hundred typewritten sheets, includes an exhaustive research of the trial and each count, as it is brought out, is dissected. Its effect is asserted and the whole combined to form the chain of the defense’s claims.

The two jurors named are Marcus Johenning and J. A. Henslee, both of whom, it is claimed in the motion, were prejudiced against Frank before they were selected. Affidavits will be introduced to support this contention.

The motion was placed in the hands of Solicitor Dorsey for his inspection and reply and the first hearing will be given on October 4.

Charge Made of Jury Intimidation

Principal among the objections offered in the motion is the conduct of the crowds which attended the trial. Frank’s attorneys openly declare the jury was intimidated, and despite their objections no effort was made to stop the applause which time and again rang out in the courtroom.

Threats to clear the room were made by the trial judge, the motion states, but they were absolutely disregarded and the threats were not enforced, despite the objections of counsel for the defense.

Hits at Conley Testimony

The motion struck also at the admission of the lascivious testimony of Jim Conley, the negro sweeper. The testimony referred to included that wherein the negro declared on the witness stand that Frank had entertained women in the factory on holidays while he stood watch at the front door.

Lasciviousness is not one of the character traits involved in a plea of murder and can not be held in a murder trial, even when the defendant has put his character in issue, the motion stated.

The testimony of Dr. H. F. Harris, County Physician, also was objected to. The motion declared that the physician’s testimony was argumentative and not a statement of fact, scientifically or otherwise. Dr. Harris had gone extensively into an analysis of the cabbage taken from the stomach of Mary Phagan, which she had eaten on the morning of her tragic death.

Objection was also made to the testimony of Newt Lee, the negro night watchman, who first found the Phagan girl’s body, wherein he testified as to Frank’s nervousness and his method of conversation when the two were brought together at the police station following the murder.

The testimony of Detective Black that Frank was excited, while Lee was composed, at this time also was made the point of an objection. Black’s statements of a conversation which he had had with Frank before the murder, when on a private investigation, were objected to when the detective compared them to the conversation which he held with the pencil factory superintendent after the girl was murdered.

Charge Errors to Court

The petition charges that the court erred in allowing the testimony of Miss Mary Pirk, who charged immoral conditions at the pencil factory, and in admitting other testimony hinting at the same thing over the protests of the defense.

Error is charged in the admission of Miss Irene Jackson’s evidence concerning a conversation with Detective Starnes about dressing-room conditions, and an incident in which Frank looked into the room when Miss Emily Mayfield was not dressed.

Another count is based on the admission of Scott’s testimony concerning a conversation he had with Mrs. Arthur White regarding her seeing a negro on the first floor of the factory. The State claimed this negro was Jim Conley.

Solicitor’s Conduct Attacked

The court is charged with error in allowing the Solicitor to declare that he was prepared to prove the charges of immorality against Frank. The petition charges specific error to the Solicitor’s declaration, “I am not fourflushing,” made in the presence of the jury. It is declared that this declaration had undue influence on the jurors’ minds, leading them to unfair inference.

Another error is laid to the court in allowing, over the defense’s objection, the Solicitor’s questions tending to show that Montag Brothers had attempted to influence the Pinkertons and had tried to make the detective agency shield the prisoner. The petition declares that none of the evidence concerning the employment of the Pinkertons was admissible.

The overruling of any evidence from Street Car Inspector Leach concerning the dismissal or punishment of employees for being ahead of schedule time is another count.

Error is charged in the questioning of J. N. Minar, a reporter for The Georgian. The defense claims that the questions concerning whether he went to interview the Epps family merely as a reporter should never have been allowed. The questions were asked, the petition says, to influence the jury and no attempt to prove the intimations ever was made.

In refusing to allow Miss Hall to testify to a telephone conversation in which Frank told her about work to be done that tragic day another error is charged, and another in the admission of Philip Chambers’ reference to Gantt, tending to show that Frank had tried to throw suspicion on Gantt and shield himself.

B’nai Brith Question Recalled

The court also errored, it is held, in declining to allow Dr. David Marx to give testimony as to the character of the Jewish organization known as the B’nai Brith.

Defendant’s counsel, it is said, stated at the time that Dr. Marx would testify that, while the B’nai Brith was an international Jewish charity organization, its charity did not extend to giving aid to persons charged with misdemeanors of criminal law.

The State objected to this, it is further stated, and the court sustained the objection and so the court errored in this respect, for the reason that the Solicitor General, in his insinuations to the jury and in his speech, strongly intimated that Frank was receiving moral and financial support by reason of his membership in B’nai Brith.

The court also errored, it is held, in permitting Mrs. J. J. Wardlaw to be asked certain questions in regard to Frank’s alleged conduct on a Hapeville car with Mary Phagan. She answered, it is said, “No,” to all questions. The defendant objected to the questions because while the witness denied any knowledge by hearsay or otherwise of the wrong asked about, the mere asking of such questions, the answer to which must have been irrelevant and prejudicial, was harmful to the defendant, and the court erred in permitting questions to be asked no matter what the answers might have been.

Character Ruling Attacked

The court further erred because, although the defendant had put his character in issue, admitting such testimony, the State could not reply by proof of improper or immoral conduct with women.

The court erred, it is said, in permitting the witness W. E. Turner, over the objection of the defendant, to tell of a conversation he overheard between Frank and Mary Phagan, in which Frank told her he was superintendent of the factory, and of Mary Phagan backing away from him, and of Frank walking toward her. This was prejudicial because it was a distinct transaction apart from the issues in the case intended to prejudice the jury.

The court erred in permitting W. P. Merck, over objection, to tell of an engagement he had with Daisy Hopkins, and to tell of her remarks that she had just been to the pencil factory.

The court erred in admitting the minutes of the State Board of Health showing the controversy of Dr. Harris and Dr. Westmoreland. This was prejudicial to the defendant, centering the minds of the jurymen on something different from the issues in the case. It erred in permitting E. H. Pickett to testify, over objections, about Minola McKnight’s statements.

Hit Car Evidence

The court erred in permitting J. C. McEwen, street car man, to testify as to the arrival of the Euclid avenue car, stating that it would have to be ahead of the White City car to cut it off. Objection also was cited to the testimony of Henry Hoffman, another street car man who testified about cars coming in ahead of time.

The court erred, over the objection of the defendant, in allowing the witness Lewis Ingram to testify as to the street car coming in ahead of time. The court erred for the same reason in permitting the witness W. D. Owens to testify as to the time.

Objections were cited to the testimony of J. M. Gantt, that the clocks of the pencil factory were not accurate, on the ground that the evidence was misleading, and against L. T. Kendrick’s testimony about the condition of the clocks while he was in the factory.

Another objection was against the testimony of Harry Scott, admitted over objection, that Frank did not inform him that Conley could write.

Attack Character Evidence

The court erred in allowing witnesses to testify that Frank’s character for lasciviousness was bad. To permit this evidence, states the petition, was highly prejudicial to the defendant. It attacked his moral character, and while such an attack would not tend to convict him of murder nor show him a person of such character as would likely commit murder, its introduction prejudiced the jury against him.

It charges that the court erred in permitting Dewey Hewell, who was brought to Atlanta from the Home of the Good Shepherd, in Cincinnati, to testify as to Frank’s character. It also charges error in admitting the testimony of Miss Cato that she saw Frank go into a private dressing room with Miss Rebecca Carson.

Requested Charge Concerning Conley

The petition charges that the court erred in refusing to give certain pertinent legal charges in the language requested by the defendant’s counsel. The petition states the judge was requested to make this charge:

“If the jury believed from the evidence that the theory or hypothesis that James Conley may have committed this crime is just as reasonable as the theory that the defendant may have committed this crime, then under the law, it would be your duty to acquit the defendant.”

Applause in Court Cited

It charges that the court erred in declining to grant a motion for a mistrial on account of the applause and in refusing to clear the courtroom. Says the petition:

“The passion and prejudice of those in the crowded courtroom was so much aroused against the defendant that he could not obtain a fair and impartial trial. The very presence of that crowd was a menace to the jury.”

It further charges that the court erred in permitting Attorney Hooper to argue to the jury that the failure of the defense to cross-examine the State’s female character witnesses was because a cross-examination would have brought out specific instance of immorality. A similar objection is made to Dorsey’s argument.

One objection to Dorsey’s speech was his reasons for Mrs. Frank’s failure to visit her husband. It charges that the court erred in permitting Dorsey to intimate that the defense called some of the expert witnesses because they were physicians of some of the jurors.

Other Points in Motion

Other interesting extracts from the petition concern public sentiment, which was greatly aroused against the defendant. The courtroom was quite a small room and during the argument of the case every seat was taken. The jury, in going to and fro, was dependent on the small passageways made by the officers of the court. The jurymen could hear the whispers of the crowd.

During the argument of the Solicitor, Mr. Arnold made an objection and the crowd laughingly jeered at him so that Mr. Arnold appealed to the court.

On Saturday, prior to the rendition of the verdict, excitement in and about the courtroom was so apparent as to cause apprehension in the mind of the court as to whether he could safely continue the trial Saturday afternoon.

Tells of Court Conference

In making up his mind his honor conferred with, while on the stand and in the presence of the jury, the chief of police of Atlanta and the colonel of the Fifth Georgia Regiment. The public press, apprehending trouble also, united in a request to the court that he not continue the court on Saturday.

So court was adjourned until Monday morning. But public excitement had not subsided Monday morning. When the Solicitor entered the courtroom he was vociferously cheered by the large crowd, ladies and gentlemen, present, by stamping their feet and clapping hands while the jury was not 20 feet away in their rooms.

While Mr. Arnold was making a motion for a mistrial and while taking testimony to support it the crowd applauded.

Cheers for Dorsey Recalled

When the jury was finally charged by the court and retired to consider their verdict, and when Mr. Dorsey left the courtroom, a large crowd on the outside of the courthouse and in the street cheered by yelling and clapping hands and yelling “Hurray for Dorsey.”

When it was announced that the jury had agreed upon a verdict the court felt constrained to clear the courtroom, but when the verdict was rendered a crowd of more than 1,000 people outside raised a mighty shout of approval.

Allege Technical Errors

The court erred in not leaving it to the jury to say whether or not, under the facts, the witness Conley was an accomplice.

The court further erred in not charging the jury that if, under the instructions given them, they found Conley was an accomplice of Frank, they could not convict Frank under the testimony of Conley alone, but that to do so there must be a witness other than Conley in circumstances corroborating the evidence of Conley.

The court erred in charging the jury as follows:

“Is Leo Frank guilty? Are you satisfied of that beyond a reasonable doubt from the evidence in this case or is his plea of not guilty the truth?”

Reason for Objection

The court erred in putting the proposition of the defendant’s guilt or innocence to the jury in this manner, because the effect of the same was to put the burden upon the defendant of establishing his plea of not guilty and the further effect was to impress upon the jury that, unless they believed that the defendant’s plea of not guilty was the truth, they could not acquit him, and even though they did not believe his plea of not guilty to be true, it left out entirely the consideration that if they still had a reasonable doubt in their minds of his guilt they should acquit him.

Twenty-five pages of the petition are devoted to objections to Solicitor Dorsey’s speech. The various objections to his arguments that were made in court are recited and urged as grounds for a new trial. The court is charged with having erred in permitting certain comparisons between the Durrant, Richeson and Wilde cases and the Frank case.

Mentions Vain Request

The petition says that a new trial should be granted because of the following grounds:

The Solicitor General having, in his concluding argument, made the various statements of fact about the Durrant case, as shown in the preceding grounds of this motion, the defendant requested the court, in writing, before the judge began his charge, to charge the jury as follows, which request the judge refused to grant and thereupon committed error:

“The jury was instructed that the facts in other cases read or stated in your hearing are to have no influence upon you in making your verdict. You are to try this case upon its own facts and upon the opinion you entertain of the evidence here introduced.”

Related Notice: Dorsey Tells Why Jail Is Crowded

That the overcrowded condition of the county jail, which has been made the subject of a letter from the Board of County Commissioners, can not be alleviated at the present time was the statement of Solicitor Dorsey Wednesday. Mr. Dorsey declared the conditions grew out of the Frank trial and the consequent absence of one judge from the criminal bench.

Related Notice: Mother of a Frank Juror Held Insane

An echo of the Frank trial was heard in the Fulton County Ordinary Court Wednesday when a jury declared Mrs. Eliza Bosshardt, 60 years of age, mother of Charles Bosshardt, one of the jurors in the case, a fit subject for the State sanitarium at Milledgeville.

Relatives testified Mrs. Bosshardt suffered from delusions during the Frank trial. She expressed fear that her son would be drowned.

References

He said this is the most expensive mistake on this entire list — because you're declining a 50–100% return on investment that requires zero skill.

"If your employer offers a 401(k) match — they'll match your contributions up to a certain percentage of your salary. A typical match: the employer matches 50% of your contributions up to 6% of your salary."

"What that means: if you earn $60,000 and contribute 6% ($3,600/year) — your employer adds $1,800. That's $1,800 in free money. An instant 50% return before the money is even invested."

"If you contribute less than 6% — you get a partial match. If you contribute 0% — you get $0. The employer keeps the money they were willing to give you."

"The compound math is devastating. $1,800/year in missed employer match, invested at a 7% average annual return, over 30 years: approximately $170,000. You didn't lose $1,800. You lost $170,000 — because the $1,800 per year compounds for 30 years."

"He said this is the only investment decision where the return is guaranteed before you make it. 'The stock market might go up or down. Real estate might appreciate or not. But the employer match is a guaranteed 50–100% return — on day one — with no risk. There is no investment on Earth that offers a guaranteed 50% return. Your employer is offering one. BREAKING🚨 DHS called Marimar Martinez a domestic terrorist after an ICE agent shot her five times in Chicago. Today she sued, and the evidence says she was shot while trying to get away.

On Monday, Martinez's lawyers announced the lawsuit and released a forensic reconstruction of the day she was shot in Chicago's Brighton Park. They say it shows Border Patrol agent Charles Exum fired three shots into the windshield of her Nissan Rogue, one into the front passenger side, and a fifth through the rear passenger window while she crouched against her steering wheel.

Martinez is a U.S. citizen, born and raised in Chicago. She works as a Montessori school assistant and has no criminal record. On October 4, 2025, during Operation Midway Blitz, she was on her way to drop off clothes at a church when she spotted agents. She honked her horn and yelled "la migra" to warn her neighbors.

Five bullets left seven wounds. Exum later texted fellow agents: "I fired 5 rounds and she had 7 holes."

Homeland Security called her a "domestic terrorist" and claimed she rammed agents with her car. Prosecutors charged her with assaulting a federal agent, then dropped the case 46 days later. Body-camera footage shows Exum turning his steering wheel left, toward her car, before they collided. She had a gun she was licensed to carry, and it stayed in a snapped-closed pink holster at the bottom of her purse the whole time.

In April, an Illinois commission concluded that Exum "shot an unarmed civilian without apparent justification" and that evidence was "deliberately tampered with and destroyed."

Exum's bosses rallied around him anyway. He texted that he had support from "Chief Bovino, Chief Banks, Sec Noem and El Jefe himself." Then-Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino offered to delay Exum's retirement because of his "excellent service in Chicago." Another supporter texted him: "you are a legend among agents."

A year later, no agent from Midway Blitz has been criminally charged for anything they did on duty. Chicago police detectives are now investigating the shooting and want to bring a case to Cook County prosecutors.

Her attorney Michael Gallagher said Monday that their experts have "objective proof that this was a bad shoot. That everything Exum said was a lie."

text:
PROSPERITY, Pa. — Jimmy Brock adjusts a device on his belt that provides oxygen in an emergency. It is the last piece of safety equipment he puts on before our descent into the Enlow Fork Mine for a tour. He silently goes through the hand motions of double-checking the rest: Hard hat is secure; cap lamp is over the top; respirator, mask, hearing protection, protective eye gear are securely in place over flame-resistant overalls and steel-toed boots.
“Are you ready for something amazing?” a smiling Brock asks McCormick, who gives two thumbs up. It marks the first time the freshman senator will go down a mine shaft.
The tour was my idea. I wanted to take you, the reader, down the mine and show you how much safety and technology are part of modern coal mining, how fast the coal goes from the longwall to the market, and how the industry is adapting to changing times.
Mining is embedded in our culture and politics. Washington County has its share of wealthier suburban neighborhoods, but voters have been more resistant to Democrats than they have in other white-collar areas, in part because the people have a profound sense of place. Residents who don’t work in coal often have a deeper connection to the industry’s legacy and work ethic than they do to the college degrees they earned far from here.
Brock, 69, is the first in his family to go into mining, a field where many workers are third- and fourth-generation. He was working as a tennis instructor nearly 50 years ago when a student whose husband worked in the coal business as a human resources supervisor tried to sell him on the pay and benefits. He accepted an offer for a summer job, then nearly quit after just one day of shoveling coal onto conveyor belts.
The ride down takes less than two minutes in a surprisingly pristine steel elevator — more like a hospital freight — and ends at a well-lit mine floor. From there, we jump into the mantrip, a rail vehicle that resembles the trams along the Jersey Shore boardwalk, and travel several miles through what feels like an interstate highway of tunnels, including yield and stop signs. Along the way, we pass miners with headlamps inspecting coal seams using technology that incorporates AI.

text:
EX POST!™ OCTOBER 7, 2026 | AFTERNOON EDITION COMMENTARY

A DEATH AT A RUSSIAN PLAGUE LAB—AND A TEST OF TRANSPARENCY

Will Trump demand the same openness from Moscow that he demanded from Beijing?

A young laboratory worker is dead. The cause remains unresolved. And Donald Trump says he plans to speak with Vladimir Putin.
The question is whether Trump will demand the same transparency from Russia that he demanded from China.
The case involves a 28-year-old worker who reportedly died October 2 of pneumonia of unknown origin. She worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.
The name matters. This institution was established in 1934 to control plague outbreaks and later expanded its work to other dangerous diseases, including cholera and anthrax. Plague is explicitly part of its name and its historical mission.
That connection helps explain why her unexplained death attracted scrutiny: Was this an ordinary infection, or something connected to her laboratory work?
That question deserves investigation. It does not establish that she died of plague.
The speculation grew from a regional governor’s suggestion that plague was a possibility and unverified accounts involving a broken laboratory test tube. Russian authorities rejected the laboratory-accident theory. Reuters reported that supporting evidence had not been made public.
Those distinctions matter. An unexplained death is not proof of a laboratory leak. A rumor repeated across social media is not a diagnosis.
Trump reportedly planned a telephone conversation with Putin about the case and offered American assistance. The reported contact was a call—not a confirmed meeting in Florida.
Offering assistance is appropriate. But assistance should accompany a demand for verifiable information: What tests were performed? What did they show? What organisms did the employee work with? Was there a documented exposure? What evidence supports the official explanation?
The World Health Organization assessed the risk outside Russia as very low and reported no symptoms among monitored contacts. That is reassuring. It does not settle the cause of the worker’s death.
During the COVID pandemic, Trump repeatedly blamed China and promoted claims about the virus’s origins. But a possible laboratory accident and a deliberate release are separate allegations, requiring separate evidence. Neither should be treated as established merely because a politician repeats it.
The same discipline must apply to Russia.
Trump’s relationship with Putin should neither soften legitimate scrutiny nor encourage unsupported accusations. Public health requires consistent standards, regardless of which government is being questioned.
If Washington demands openness from Beijing, it should demand openness from Moscow.
A real human being is dead. Given what we know about her workplace and the unresolved cause of her illness, the circumstances of her death demand a clear, evidence-based explanation. The public deserves verified facts—not assurances that outrun the evidence. American assistance and Russian accountability should go together. ❦

text:
On December 14, 1799, the day he died, George Washington was bled several times as treatment for a severe throat and airway infection.

He had been outdoors in cold, wet weather the day before and woke around 2 a.m. with difficulty breathing, a sore throat, and trouble speaking or swallowing. Before doctors arrived, he asked an overseer, George Rawlins, to bleed him. Rawlins removed about 12–14 ounces; Washington asked for more, and Martha Washington intervened to stop it.

Once physicians were present—primarily Dr. James Craik, with Drs. Elisha Cullen Dick and Gustavus Richard Brown—further bleedings followed through the day. 

Contemporary and later accounts commonly total the removals at more than 80 ounces (roughly 2.4 liters, often estimated at about 40 percent of his blood volume) over roughly 12 hours, in four sessions. 

Some medical reviews note that the exact total is not fully certain from the primary documents and place the clearly recorded amount lower (at least roughly 44–46 ounces), while still agreeing that the bleedings were large and repeated. Dick objected to the last major bleeding, arguing Washington needed his strength, but was overruled.

The doctors diagnosed “cynanche trachealis” (inflammation of the upper airway). Modern interpretations usually favor acute bacterial epiglottitis or a similar rapidly progressive throat infection. Other treatments included blistering agents, an enema, and purgatives such as calomel and tartar emetic. Washington died that evening, around 10–10:30 p.m., at Mount Vernon. 

Bloodletting was standard practice under the humoral medicine of the time; it did not help and almost certainly weakened him.

The biggest mistake people make when going to their doctors for treatment is that they truly believe that the years of classroom training and years of residency rounding in hospitals equates with a significant or vast amount of real world knowledge - the knowledge maybe there, but these programs offer little to no encouragement to actually think - they are merely seeing and memorizing in order to pass their board examinations - tests that require the ability to recall but never to think. 

So, if the mountain of “knowledge” was never based in true scientific investigation but rather something that was influenced by profit or correlation, the resultant product that we as physicians “sell” to our patients is suspect, and without a thinking mind, we may actually end up hurting our patients and blaming any resulting observations of adverse effects on something we are comfortable in assigning blame to - which is usually explained as part of the disease process itself and never an iatrogenic response because we are too narcissistic to understand or accept. 

When you hear someone talk about the science, just remember, doctors truly thought they were helping George Washington with their barbaric treatment. 

That was the an accepted science. 

I am sure, that our future generations will look back on our treatments of today and forever wonder why we believed in our “science.”

This is what I now know is the science of vaccines. A thinking logical mind knows that these treatments can be barbaric.

text:
Too Russian for the NHL? The tensions behind Ovechkin’s farewell
Political backlash and a coach’s rebuilding plans cast a shadow over the Capitals legend’s final chapter in Washington (FULL)
By Alan Moore, a Vilnius-based sports journalist and host of Capital Sports 3.0. A former athlete, he has over 30 years of professional sports and higher education experience across the globe.
https://t.co/xagy7Jjqud
There will be no doubt as to where the tomb of Alexander the Great II will be, or where he will see out the twilight of his career. But has one of the greatest modern Russian hockey stars been forced from the heady heights of the National Hockey League too soon?
When Alexander Ovechkin appeared in an election promo video for the United Russia party, I questioned his reasoning. I wasn’t alone. An NHL beat reporter posted in a WhatsApp group chat “Ovi’s about to quit Caps.” Of the other 30+ North American sports reporters in there with me, all speculated as to his next move, while also worrying about the backlash. There wasn’t long to wait.
The Ukraine troll farms ignited the fire that burned all the way into US media and Russophobic elements, and reached Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis. Leonsis, who also owns the Washington Wizards NBA franchise, refused to buckle to pressure from the US sports press corps, backing his star man to the hilt.
The Greek-origin billionaire has always been protective of Ovechkin and his other Russian players. In 2018, he told a popular English-language sports radio show in Moscow, called Capital Sports, that “we need to judge athletes on their performance and behavior, not color, country and so on.” However, the same cannot be said of the Capitals’ head coach, Spencer Carbery, who appears to have used the furor for his own ends.
“Spence wants a rebuild and he can’t do it with [Ovechkin] on board. He can’t blow up the team while [Ovechkin] is still on the roster,” a Capitals’ source told me on Tuesday morning. In the pre-season, Carbery said that he would play Ovechkin less and was, privately, against extending his contract.
When I questioned whether the political party video played any role in his ‘retirement’, the source said “definitely, but not from the club’s side. But there was a fallout with the coach.”
Igor Nazarenko, of St. Petersburg-based sports outlet Sport Day by Day warned of Ovechkin’s displacement in June after Washington signed American Alex Tuch from the Buffalo Sabres on an eight-year, $86 million contract. The sharpshooting winger’s arrival heralded, Nazarenko predicted, the replacement of the Russian as the on-ice leader.
Additionally, Carbery has focused on youth development, and has spoken about giving talents like Russia’s Ivan Miroshnichenko (22), Belarus’ Ilya Protas (20), and the US’ Ryan Leonard (21) more game time.
Scott MacPherson, former General Manager of Kunlun (now Shanghai) Red Star of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL) and personal friend of Alexander Ovechkin predicted this would happen last year.
In early-2025, he told Capital Sports that Ovechkin wouldn’t “linger” in the NHL and instead return to his roots in Russia. “Ovi’s got nothing to prove [in the NHL], but he wants to be back in the KHL.”
I asked why. He made his debut at the top of Russian hockey aged 16; now at 41, why bother?
“He’s Russian. He loves his country and he wants to give back to fans. One, two years more in the KHL and it will be memorable.”
Russian sports media is already speculating about who will land him. Dynamo Moscow, his original Russian club, are favorites, while the other two big Moscow clubs, Spartak and CSKA, are already ruled out. SKA St. Petersburg has been mooted as his retirement vehicle, though that has been ruled out by the local media.
A couple of years in the KHL, followed by a career in politics, or sports administration, or even coaching, lies ahead of Ovi. His exit from the NHL was not as simple as stepping aside to let youth have its fling. Neither was it only because he made a video that riled up the anti-Russian trolls, as hockey fans see past politics and want to watch the best perform for them.
Yet it cannot be ruled out that the offer made by his current NHL team, according to MacPherson, of $1.5 million for one-year extension until 2027-28, was beyond insulting. If Russian sports media is to be believed, for two last-hurrah seasons with Dynamo Moscow, he will earn ten times that per year, and put the KHL front and center on the global stage.
In any case, Alexander the Great II is coming home to where his heart is.

text:
"Vance says Iran must meaningfully reduce enrichment capacity to end war
US is in talks with President Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Araqchi, Vance says
Vance said he has not decided whether to pursue a White House run.

 US Vice President JD Vance said in an exclusive interview with Reuters that Iran ​must make a “meaningful” reduction in its nuclear enrichment capacity to satisfy US demands and end the countries’ seven-month war, even as Washington was unsure how ‌Tehran makes decisions in negotiations.
Vance, a longtime skeptic of US involvement in foreign wars, has taken a leading role in negotiating a settlement to the conflict and brokered a provisional peace agreement in June that quickly fell apart. 
The war has jolted global energy markets and become a political liability for President Donald Trump and fellow Republicans ahead of November midterm elections.
Speaking on Monday after a campaign trip in Alaska, Vance said ​any agreement would require Iran to reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity, rather than offer assurances of future nuclear drawdowns.

Iran and the US have exchanged proposals in recent weeks aimed at ending the war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route. Trump rejected Tehran's ​latest offer and has warned that military operations could intensify after the midterms.

Vance said the US remained open to an agreement but would require concrete Iranian nuclear concessions.

UNCLEAR HOW IRAN MAKES DECISIONS: VANCE
Complicating matters, Vance said Washington is uncertain who makes decisions in Tehran.
Vance said the US was in talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi. But ​it was unclear how much authority they wield within Iran's power structure, he said, after joint US-Israeli strikes at the start of the war killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Iran's ‌Foreign Ministry ⁠spokesperson said on Sunday that US officials are well aware of who their Iranian counterparts are and how Iran's decision-making system works.
"The problem is actually the opposite: it lies in the contradictory positions and mixed messaging from US officials," Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference.

Vance declined to say if he ​was leading peace talks, though he is ⁠frequently cited as the White House's top negotiator.
"We're certainly involved," he said. "Ultimately, the president of the United States is driving things."

The war — and its $3 billion monthly price tag — has become a key issue on the campaign trail. Higher energy prices have put Trump and Republicans on the ​defensive in competitive states that will decide control of Congress.

Vance has sought to temper criticism of Trump’s handling of the conflict, telling ​voters they should not ⁠let that issue keep them from backing Republicans in next month's elections.
Trump carried Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024, but rising everyday costs have put the state in play.
Before speaking with Reuters, Vance focused much of his speech on affordability concerns, especially around ⁠energy. Alaska's remote ​locale makes consumer goods more expensive, and energy production is a key industry.
Rally attendees roared when Sullivan nearly ​introduced Vance as the president of the US, rather than the vice president. Vance is seen as a leading Republican contender to succeed Trump in the White House.
Vance told Reuters afterward that he had not decided whether to ​seek the presidency in 2028."

text:
Here is my original  Google Pixel, which I bought around October 2016, and my latest phone, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold.
And I think the Fold might actually be my favourite phone to date.

I got a very good trade-in deal from Google, which made the price much easier to justify. I’m not sure I could have talked myself into paying the full amount, but at the price I paid, I’m very happy with it.

In fact, I’ve now sold my iPad because I simply wasn’t using it anymore. The Fold covers that middle ground between a phone and a tablet surprisingly well for me.
I completely understand why, for many people, the iPhone is the obvious choice. I’ve just never really been tied to Apple. My wife is completely Apple, although amusingly she mainly uses Google apps on all of it.

For what I actually do, Android works perfectly well. I use Krea through the browser, Photoshop, LumaFusion, ChatGPT, Gemini and Grok  and that covers most of what I want to do away from my desktop.

I built myself a Windows PC late last year, mainly so I could experiment with local AI, so I’m no longer really in the Apple universe anyway.

My history with PCs actually goes back to 1993, when I was doing a desktop-publishing course in Seattle, Washington. I’ve owned and used Macs over the years too, but I’ve never really loved them. I suppose a lot of it simply comes down to what you get used to.

I’ve developed a strange Pixel upgrade pattern
Pixel 1 → Pixel 4 → Pixel 7 → Pixel 11.
With a few iphones and samsungs scattered in between

I’ve never really considered myself a fanboy of any particular company. I just buy whatever I think will work best for me at a price I’m comfortable paying.

Having a SIM-only contract helps with that too. I’m not locked into waiting for an upgrade date, so if a decent trade-in offer appears, I can take advantage of it.

Ten years between the two Pixels in this photo. Technology has moved on just a bit but strangely not as fast as i would have thought. Have a good day

text:
You obviously didn't even watch my video because I have a whole section (Part 4) going over the Magisterium. Here, let me paste my script for you:

PART IV: THE MAGISTERIUM
The teaching of the Ordinary Magisterium on this point is consistent with the patristic and scholastic tradition.
The Roman Catechism (Catechismus Romanum, 1566)
The Catechism of the Council of Trent, composed under St. Pius V, in its treatment of the Creed's article on the Second Coming, reflects the traditional eschatological expectation that the Jews will be converted prior to the Last Judgment. It references the ministry of Elias in connection with the Last Things, placing this within the settled teaching of the Church. While the Roman Catechism does not develop a detailed exegesis of Romans 11:26 itself, it presupposes and embodies the patristic eschatological framework that the verse undergirds.
The Catechism of the Catholic Church (1992), paragraph 674
The most authoritative modern synthesis of Catholic teaching states explicitly:
“The glorious Messiah's coming is suspended at every moment of history until his recognition by 'all Israel,' for 'a hardening has come upon part of Israel' in their 'unbelief' toward Jesus... 'For if their rejection means the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance mean but life from the dead?' The 'full inclusion' of the Jews in the Messiah's salvation, in the wake of 'the full number of the Gentiles,' will enable the People of God to achieve 'the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,' in which 'God may be all in all.'”— Catechism of the Catholic Church, §674
This is a remarkable and authoritative affirmation of the ancient tradition. The Catechism does not speak of a 'dual covenant' by which Jews might be saved apart from Christ — it speaks of the 'full inclusion of the Jews in the Messiah's salvation.' It explicitly links Christ's glorious return to 'all Israel' recognizing Him. This is the dominant patristic teaching on Romans 11:26, firmly reaffirmed in the official Catechism of the Catholic Church.
A note of precision is worth making here: CCC 674 does not dogmatically define the precise manner, scale, or timeline of Israel's future conversion, nor does it formally define the role of Elias as a matter of faith. What it does clearly and authoritatively teach is threefold: (1) Christ's return is linked to Israel's recognition of Him; (2) there will be a 'full inclusion' of the Jews in the Messiah's salvation; and (3) this follows the fullness of the Gentiles. That is the secure, authoritative ground — and it is substantial, representing the formal reaffirmation of a consistent tradition.
Paragraph 674 also cites Romans 11:15, 11:12, Ephesians 4:13, and 1 Corinthians 15:28, weaving together the great Pauline vision of the final consummation in which Israel's acceptance of Christ triggers the full measure of the Body of Christ.
Nostra Aetate (Vatican II, 1965)
The Council's declaration on non-Christian religions, while primarily addressing the wrongness of blaming all Jews collectively for the death of Christ, also affirms: 'God holds the Jews most dear for the sake of their Fathers; He does not repent of the gifts He makes or of the calls He issues — such is the witness of the Apostle. In company with the Prophets and the same Apostle, the Church awaits that day, known to God alone, on which all peoples will address the Lord in a single voice and serve him shoulder to shoulder.'
While Nostra Aetate is sometimes cited to discourage direct evangelization of Jews, the text itself says nothing of the sort. It condemns unjust violence and collective guilt, not the proclamation of the Gospel. Indeed, paragraph 674 of the Catechism — promulgated after Vatican II — makes clear that 'full inclusion of the Jews in the Messiah's salvation' remains Catholic teaching.
The Good Friday Prayer (Traditional Latin Mass)
The traditional Good Friday prayer for the Jews, as used for centuries in the Roman Rite — in the pre-1955 form that preceded the modifications of 1959 (John XXIII), 1962, and the Benedictine revision of 2008 — reads:
“Let us pray also for the faithless Jews: that Almighty God may remove the veil from their hearts; so that they too may acknowledge Jesus Christ our Lord. Almighty and eternal God, who dost not exclude from thy mercy even Jewish faithlessness: hear our prayers, which we offer for the blindness of that people; that acknowledging the light of thy Truth, which is Christ, they may be delivered from their darkness.”— Traditional Good Friday Prayer for the Jews (Pre-1955 Traditional Latin Mass form; the 1962/2008 forms convey the same conversion petition in revised language)
This liturgical prayer, used for centuries in the Church, is a continuous act of hope and charity directed precisely at the eschatological conversion promised in Romans 11:26. It is the Church praying for the very event St. Paul prophesied.
A Note on the Theological Weight of This Teaching
Before proceeding, a clarification that will make this presentation academically unassailable: while the Church has not issued a formal solemn definition specifying that there must be a mass Jewish conversion, or fixing the exact role of Elias, or establishing a precise timeline, the consistent patristic and scholastic tradition — firmly reaffirmed in CCC 674 — teaches that a future, significant turning of the Jewish people to Christ forms part of God's providential design before the end of time. This teaching is reflected in the ordinary magisterium and the universal catechetical tradition of the Church, and enjoys the support of the common and constant teaching of the Fathers and Doctors. It is not a private theological speculation — it is as close to a certain theological conclusion as can be found outside a formally defined dogma.

Ukrainians: the new mercenaries, the new ISIS?

This is something I find very hard to understand.

Seven foreign nationals arrested in India in the Myanmar training-camp case have now been released from Tihar Jail.
One is American, Matthew Aaron VanDyke. Six are Ukrainian. The NIA had accused the group of involvement in a plot connected to training armed groups in Myanmar.
Yet they have now been granted default bail, their passports released, and permission to travel back to the US and Ukraine for a month.

So they can leave India.
That should raise some serious questions.

Ukraine has been a massive battlefield for years. Fighters have gained real experience with drones, weapons, reconnaissance, sabotage and irregular warfare.
What happens when those people leave the battlefield?

My concern is that Ukrainians are becoming a new generation of international mercenaries, carrying combat experience from the Ukraine war into other conflicts.

In that sense, they could become a new ISIS-type phenomenon — not ISIS literally, but a new pool of battle-hardened fighters whose expertise can be exported from one conflict to another.

India needs to know who these people were working for, who was paying them, where they were going and what exactly they were training for.

Because if people are arrested in connection with alleged terrorist activity, it is difficult to understand why they are then allowed to leave the country.

The Ukraine war may eventually end.

The fighters it has trained will not simply disappear.

Fratricide (from Latin fratricidium; from frater 'brother' and -cīdium 'killing' – the assimilated root of caedere 'to kill, cut down') is the act of killing one's own brother.

It can either be done directly or via the use of either a hired or an indoctrinated intermediary (an assassin). The victim need not be the perpetrator's biological brother. In a military context, fratricide refers to a service member killing a comrade.

The term is often used metaphorically to refer to civil wars.[2][3]

Religion and mythology
The Abrahamic religions recognize the biblical account of Cain and Abel as the first fratricidal murder. Esau swore to kill Jacob after Jacob stole his blessings, and later, Jacob's sons planned to kill Joseph, but instead sold him. Judge Gideon's son, Avimelech, killed his seventy brothers, except for the youngest, Jotham, who escaped.

In the mythology of ancient Rome, the city is founded as the result of a fratricide, with the twins Romulus and Remus quarreling over who has the favour of the gods and over each other's plans to build Rome, with Romulus becoming Rome's first king and namesake after killing his brother.[4]

In Greek mythology, Cassiphone, the daughter of Odysseus and Circe, killed her half-brother and husband Telemachus in revenge after he killed her mother Circe following a quarrel between the two.[5]

Osiris Myth
Main article: Osiris myth
In ancient Egyptian mythology, the god Osiris is murdered by his brother Set who usurps the throne.

The Mahabharata and the Ramayana
In the Hindu epic Mahābhārata, Karna was killed by Arjuna who was unaware that Karna was his eldest brother.

Roman Empire
The only known fratricides in the Roman Empire are Romulus killing REmus and the reasonably well-known murder of Geta on the orders of his brother Caracalla in 211. The brothers had a fraught relationship enduring many years; upon their father Septimius Severus's death in February 211, they succeeded him as co-emperors. Their joint rule was embittered and unsuccessful, with each of them conspiring to have the other one murdered. In December of that year, Caracalla pretended to be holding a reconciliation in their mother Julia Domna's apartment when Geta was lured to come unarmed and unguarded. A group of Centurions loyal to Caracalla ambushed him upon Geta's arrival, with Geta dying in his mother's arms.[6] It is said that the fratricide would often come back to haunt Caracalla.

In Roman mythology, Romulus and Remus (Latin: [ˈroːmʊlʊs], [ˈrɛmʊs]) are twin brothers whose story tells of the events that led to the founding of the city of Rome and the Roman Kingdom by Romulus, following his fratricide of Remus. The image of a she-wolf suckling the twins in their infancy has been a symbol of the city of Rome and the ancient Romans since at least the 3rd century BC. Although the tale takes place before the founding of Rome in 753 BC, the earliest known written account of the myth is from the late 3rd century BC. Possible historical bases for the story, and interpretations of its local variants, are subjects of ongoing debate.

Overview
Romulus and Remus were born in Alba Longa, one of the many ancient Latin cities near the seven hills of Rome. Their mother Rhea Silvia, also known as Ilia,[2] was a Vestal Virgin and the daughter of former king Numitor, who had been displaced by his brother Amulius. In some sources, Rhea Silvia conceived them when the god Mars visited her in a sacred grove dedicated to him.[3]

Seeing them as a possible threat to his rule, King Amulius ordered them to be killed and they were abandoned on the bank of the river Tiber to die. They were saved by the god Tiberinus, Father of the River, and survived with the care of others at the site of future Rome. In the best-known episode, the twins were suckled by a she-wolf in a cave now known as the Lupercal.[4] Eventually, they were adopted by Faustulus, a shepherd. They grew up tending flocks, unaware of their true identities. Over time, they became natural leaders and attracted a company of supporters from the community.

Romulus and Remus on the House of the She-wolf at the Grand-Place of Brussels
When they were young adults, they became involved in a dispute between supporters of Numitor and Amulius. As a result, Remus was taken prisoner and brought to Alba Longa. Both his grandfather and the king suspected his true identity. Romulus, meanwhile, had organized an effort to free his brother and set out with help for the city. During this time, they learned of their past and joined forces with their grandfather to restore him to the throne. Amulius was killed and Numitor was reinstated as king of Alba. The twins set out to build a city of their own.

After arriving back in the area of the seven hills, they disagreed about the hill upon which to build. Romulus preferred the Palatine Hill, above the Lupercal; Remus preferred the Aventine Hill. When they could not resolve the dispute, they agreed to seek the gods' approval through a contest of augury. Remus saw 6 auspicious birds first, but Romulus saw 12 and claimed to have won divine approval. They disputed the result; Remus insulted Romulus's new city and was killed, either by Romulus or by one of his supporters.[5] Romulus then went on to found the city of Rome, its institutions, government, military, and religious traditions. He reigned for many years as its first king.

Giovanni Battista Re (born 30 January 1934) is an Italian Catholic prelate who has served as Dean of the College of Cardinals since 2020. He was made a cardinal in 2001 and served as prefect of the Congregation for Bishops from 2000 to 2010. As the most senior cardinal bishop in attendance, he chaired the 2013 conclave that elected Pope Francis.

Early years
Born in Borno, Italy, the son of the carpenter Matteo Re (1908–2012),[1] Giovanni Battista RE was ordained a priest by Archbishop Giacinto Tredici in Brescia on 3 March 1957. He holds a doctorate in canon law from the Pontifical Gregorian University, Rome, and taught in the Brescia seminary.[citation needed] To prepare for a diplomatic career he entered the Pontifical Ecclesiastical Academy in 1961.[2]

Curial service
Re has been a member of the Roman Curia since 1963, where he served as personal secretary to Archbishop Giovanni Benelli. He was elevated to monsignor and served in various diplomatic positions before being named both bishop of the titular see of Forum Novum and secretary of the Congregation for Bishops on 9 October 1987.[3] Pope John Paul II administered the episcopal consecration on 7 November.

College of Cardinals
As Dean of the College of Cardinals, Re along with Pope Francis[33] presided over the funeral of Pope Benedict XVI on 5 January 2023.[34] It was the first funeral for a retired pope since Pope Gregory XII, who resigned in 1415 and died two years later. Two years later, on 26 April 2025, Re officiated at the funeral of Pope Francis.[35] He presided over the General Congregations of the College of Cardinals leading to the 2025 papal conclave[36] and presided at the Missa Pro Eligendo Romano Pontifice on the morning of 7 May 2025, before the conclave started later that afternoon.[37] He was too old to be an elector and therefore did not preside over the conclave.[c]

AI Overview
These three names share a deep linguistic and historical connection, primarily originating in Ancient Mesopotamia, the Middle East, and the Caucasus.
Sargon
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Greek and biblical translation of the Akkadian regnal name Šarru-kīn. It combines šarru (Akkadian for "king") and kīnu (meaning "true," "established," or "legitimate").
Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").
Sako
Origin & Etymology: Sako operates on a few different historical tracks depending on the region:
In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.
In the Balkans: In Albania, it functions as a standalone occupational surname for a "church servant" or as a nickname for the Muslim name Isak (Isaac).
In Asia: It is also an unrelated Japanese surname (written as 佐古) meaning "HELP" and "ancient".

(H) Pope Saint Innocent I

 “In seeking the things of God . . . you have acknowledged that judgment is to be referred to us [the pope], and have shown that you know that is owed to the Apostolic See [Rome], if all of us placed in this position are to desire to follow the apostle himself [Peter] from whom the episcopate itself and the total authority of this name have emerged” (Letters 29:1 [A.D. 408]).

(I) Saint Augustine

“Among these [apostles] Peter alone almost everywhere deserved to represent the whole Church. Because of that representation of the Church, which only he bore, he deserved to hear ‘I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven’” (Sermons 295:2 [A.D. 411]).

“Some things are said which seem to relate especially to the apostle Peter, and yet are not clear in their meaning unless referred to the Church, which he is acknowledged to have represented in a figure on account of the primacy which he bore among the disciples. Such is ‘I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven,’ and other similar passages” (Commentary on Psalm 108 1 [A.D. 415]).

“Who is ignorant that the first of the apostles is the most blessed Peter?” (Commentary on John 56:1 [A.D. 416]).

(J) Council of Ephesus 

“Philip, presbyter and legate of [Pope Celestine I] said: ‘We offer our thanks to the holy and venerable synod, that when the writings of our holy and blessed pope had been read to you . . . you joined yourselves to the holy head also by your holy acclamations. For your blessedness is not ignorant that the head of the whole faith, the head of the apostles, is blessed Peter the apostle’” (Acts of the Council, session 2 [A.D. 431]).
“Philip, the presbyter and legate of the Apostolic See [Rome] said: ‘There is no doubt, and in fact it has been known in all ages, that the holy and most blessed Peter, prince and head of the apostles, pillar of the faith, and foundation of the Catholic Church, received the keys of the kingdom from our Lord Jesus Christ, the Savior and Redeemer of the human race, and that to him was given the power of loosing and binding sins: who down even to today and forever both lives and judges in his successors’” (ibid., session 3).

(K) Pope Saint Leo I

“Our Lord Jesus Christ . . . has placed the principal charge on the blessed Peter, chief of all the apostles, and from him as from the head wishes his gifts to flow to all the body, so that anyone who dares to secede from Peter’s solid rock may understand that he has no part or lot in the divine mystery. He wished him who had been received into partnership in his undivided unity to be named what he himself was, when he said: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church’ [Matt. 16:18], that the building of the eternal temple might rest on Peter’s solid rock, strengthening his Church so surely that neither could human rashness assail it nor the gates of hell prevail against it” (Letters 10:1 [A.D. 445).

(L) Saint Hilary of Poitiers 

“Peter to whom previously He had given the keys of the kingdom of heaven, upon whom he was going to build His Church against which the gates of hell would not prevail, what he bound or loosed on carth would remain in heaven either bound or loosed... He was to suffer so much for the salvation of the human race that he named Peter, the first confessor of the Son of God, the foundation of the Church, the door-keeper of the heavenly kingdom and in earthly affairs the judge of heaven in triumph over Satan." (“Treatise on the Psalms,” [A.D. 360]).”

There is a growing concern that the persistent, lengthy queues in Tirumala may be artificially driven. 
The systemic friction in the free general queue leaves many pilgrims feeling coerced into opting for the ₹300 Special Darshan or other paid tiers simply to secure a reasonable waiting time. 

What should be a privilege feels increasingly like a necessity pushed by design.

A major underlying issue is the lack of administrative transparency. The TTD does not publish real-time or daily breakdowns showing the precise allocation of darshans across various categories, such as Break Darshan, SRIVANI, ₹300 Special Entry, and Sarva Darshan. 

Without clear, public-facing statistics on how many devotees from each category are processed daily, pilgrims are left in the dark. 

This operational opacity extends to accommodation, where finding available cottages remains a constant struggle for the average visitor.

When looking at other high-volume pilgrimage destinations, the operational contrast is stark:

**Golden Temple (Amritsar)** Handles a higher daily footfall than Tirupati, yet operates with continuous, seamless movement and dignified accessibility for every visitor without multi-tiered paywalls.

 **Kashi Vishwanath (Varanasi)**: Manages nearly double Tirupati’s footfall post-corridor expansion, yet completes general darshan in a fraction of the time.  

While TTD frequently highlights the adoption of modern technologies such as AI and Machine Learning for crowd management, technology alone cannot resolve structural inefficiencies. Deployment of advanced algorithms offers little benefit unless paired with genuine operational transformation, equitable access, and complete administrative transparency.

text:
HOW TO SETUP A BUSINESS ALTAR

A business altar is not a magic table that prints money. It is a chosen place and a chosen habit where you put your work in front of God on purpose and keep it there. In the Bible, an altar was a spot someone built so they could meet God, remember a promise, offer something costly, and say, “This part of my life is not mine alone.” People today took that old picture and applied it to shops, offices, and side hustles. 

No single person in the Bible started a “business altar.” Noah, Abraham, and others built altars for worship and covenant. Modern teachers, especially in some Pentecostal churches, began saying you can treat your business the same way: dedicate it, pray over it, and refuse to let money become the thing you actually worship. The idea is borrowed from Scripture. The exact phrase is newer.

Look at the old stories in plain language. After the flood, Noah built an altar and gave an offering. It was his way of saying the new start belonged to God, not just to his survival skills. Abraham built altars wherever he pitched his tent. He was a wealthy man with flocks and workers, and the altars marked the land and the promises as God’s, not only his. 

Jacob, running and afraid, used a stone as a pillow, dreamed, then set that stone up as a pillar and made a vow. The place became a reminder: if God kept him, God would get the honor. Elijah repaired a broken altar on Mount Carmel before fire ever fell. The prophets of Baal shouted for hours. Elijah prayed a short, clear prayer. The difference was not volume. It was whose altar was standing. 

Later, when the ark of God stayed in Obed-Edom’s house, the Bible says the Lord blessed that household and everything that belonged to him. David noticed. Presence, tended on purpose, touched the ordinary work around it.
That is the seed of the idea. You do not need a stone pile in the parking lot. You need a real decision that this business, this job, this small trade, sits under God. 

Then you need a rhythm that keeps the decision alive.
Here is a simple way to set it up. 
Pick a real spot: a corner of the shop before you open, the desk before emails, the kitchen table if you work from home. Clear it. You can use a Bible, a notebook, or nothing visible at all. What matters is that you and God both know this is the place you stop and tell the truth. 

Speak a short dedication out loud: “This work is Yours. The customers, the money, the mistakes, the next decision—I am not the final owner. Show me what to do, and I will do the part that is mine.” Write the date. If you have a partner or employees who share the faith, tell them the business is being run this way so the habit is not a secret. If they do not share it, you still keep the habit yourself. 

Dedication is not a performance for customers.
Activation is not a one-time speech. It is the first ordinary day you actually pause there. Before you chase sales, you ask for clean judgment. Before you hire, you ask for wisdom. Before you cut a corner to make the month look better, you stop. 

The Bible’s picture of living sacrifice in Romans 12 is useful here: you offer your actual body and schedule, not just a feeling. Proverbs keeps saying the same hard thing in simple words—the hand of the diligent makes rich, honest weights please God, plans fail without counsel. Prayer does not replace those. It aims them.

Keeping the fire burning means you do not let the altar become furniture. Fire in the old temple was not allowed to go out. For you, that looks small and repeatable. Same short time most days, even ten minutes. Thank God for what worked. Confess what you shaded or avoided. Ask for the next true step, then write it down and do it. 

Please continue reading in the next post 👇🏾

text:
Fact check thru Grok:

Partly true on the speaking role. The “Trump did none of the work” line is spin.
The clip is Maryland Gov. Wes Moore on Kaitlan Collins’s CNN show, talking about Tuesday’s Anduril event at Tradepoint Atlantic in Sparrows Point. Anduril is putting a roughly $3.7 billion private shipyard there to build components for Virginia-class submarines, with about 3,100 permanent jobs. The White House has described the package as $6.6 billion, which folds in related Navy contract value. CNN reported a $2.9 billion Navy award.
What holds up
Moore was on the program, then taken off it. CBS Baltimore reported he was initially scheduled to speak alongside Trump and was removed after the White House objected on Monday. His office says the same. He then skipped the event. The White House does not dispute that he was denied a speaking slot. Their line is that he was invited as a guest, staff and security were coordinated, and he boycotted because he would not be on stage. Deputy press secretary Anna Kelly called it a “diva” move. A White House statement said he was “throwing a tantrum over a federal initiative.”
So “blocked from speaking” matches the reporting. “Blocked from the event” does not. He was offered a seat in the audience and chose not to go.
What does not hold up cleanly
Moore’s claim that his team did the work and Trump only showed up for the credit overstates it. Maryland and Baltimore County worked the site for more than a year, including incentives. Anduril CEO Brian Schimpf publicly thanked Moore, County Executive Kathy Klausmeier, the congressional delegation, and other state and local officials. The Navy contract and the presidential announcement are federal. Both sides are claiming exclusive credit for a deal that had state recruitment and a federal buyer.

text:
I've had friends ask about the ballot measures that are up for vote this coming election in Arizona. Here is a breakdown for each measure. If you want to read the full wording for each you can visit the State web page. This is purely informational, kept to just the facts, to help everyone make the best informed decision they can. I hope it helps. 🥰

Arizona Statewide Ballot Measures – November 3, 2026

All eight were referred by the Legislature. A simple majority is required to pass. Below are the factual descriptions of what each measure does if approved (given a Yes vote).

*Proposition 141 (Constitutional amendment)

Prohibits the state and local governments from imposing any tax or fee based on vehicle miles traveled. Also prohibits rules that monitor or limit vehicle miles traveled without the vehicle owner’s consent. Limited exceptions apply to certain commercial and government vehicles.

*Proposition 142 (Constitutional amendment)

Prohibits government agencies and public education systems from requiring any applicant, student, or employee to endorse preferential treatment or discrimination on the basis of race or ethnicity. Also restricts public spending on offices or programs that promote such preferential treatment. Includes exceptions for academic coursework, research, and instruction about historical events.

*Proposition 144 (Constitutional amendment)

Amends election rules to:

Specify that only U.S. citizens may register and vote in Arizona elections.
Require every voter (including those voting by mail) to present government-issued identification.
Prohibit foreign nationals from contributing money or anything of value to influence Arizona elections, and prohibit knowingly accepting such contributions.
Require election officials to offer voters the option to have their ballot tabulated at their voting location on Election Day.

*Proposition 316 (Statute)

Prohibits local governments from imposing a new tax or increasing an existing tax on the sale of food for home consumption without voter approval. Caps the tax rate at 2%. Existing rates above 2% are frozen at their current level and cannot be raised without voter approval.

*Proposition 317 (Statute)

Declares drug cartels to be terrorist organizations under Arizona law. Defines a drug cartel as a formal or informal association engaged in human smuggling, drug trafficking, or acts defined as terrorism. Directs the Arizona Department of Homeland Security to use all authority available to address threats posed by drug cartels. States that the measure does not support an alien’s asylum claim.

*Proposition 318 (Statute)

Requires schools and athletic associations to restrict use of restrooms, locker rooms, shower rooms, and other private spaces to individuals of the sex recorded on their original birth certificate. Also restricts participation in sex-designated interscholastic and intramural athletic teams and sports based on biological sex as recorded on the original birth certificate.

*Proposition 319 (Statute)

Prohibits state agencies and local governments from installing or using new photo-enforcement systems (speed and red-light cameras) for traffic violations unless a contract for the system existed on or before December 31, 2026. Local governments with existing systems must obtain voter approval at the next regular general election (and every 10 years thereafter) to continue operating them.

*Proposition 320 (Statute)

Requires school districts with 7,500 or more students, or any district operating in a county with a population of 500,000 or more, to spend at least 60% of operational spending on direct instructional expenses. The Auditor General defines “operational spending” and “direct instructional expenses.” Non-compliant districts must increase instructional spending by at least 0.5% per year until they meet the threshold. The Department of Education may reduce certain state funding for continued non-compliance.

The Houston Texans haven’t had their ideal season, but quarterback C.J. Stroud is delivering strong performances. Veteran quarterback Russell Wilson offered encouragement, recounting a tough rebound season after a Super Bowl setback and stressing the importance of staying the course. He shared a personal reminder, writing on a note: “They’ll love you one day, and they’ll hate you the next,” and urged Stroud to keep pushing to reach the next level.

Stroud is on pace to set new personal bests in passing attempts and passing yards per game this season and has yet to turn the ball over. However, his completion percentage and touchdown rate are trending downward, and his sack rate has risen compared to the end of last season. Analysts attribute these trends more to the Texans’ surrounding play and team performance than to Stroud’s own abilities.

The Texans released a clip highlighting Stroud mic’d up from Week 4 against the Dallas Cowboys, following a touchdown pass to Nico Collins. In the footage, Stroud exclaimed that opponents wouldn’t mess with him after the score, praising Collins, who was returning from a hamstring injury. The clip was part of a broader team package released online.

In season-long evaluations, Stroud has faced higher-difficulty challenges, including games against tough defenses and some limited supporting personnel. Still, his early-season play has been described by several commentators as impressive for the level of difficulty and the expectations surrounding his contract negotiations. The prevailing question remains: can the Texans build around Stroud and improve their record to align with his proven performance?

text:
In 64 A.D. a fire broke out in the City of Rome that burned for nine days.  A rumor got out and spread throughout the city that the Emperor Nero had taken his lyre up to look over the scene to sing of the burning of Troy (it was well-known that Nero fancied himself as a singer).  This led to speculation that he had a part in starting the fire.  The Roman historian Tacitus picks up with the story [note that Tacitus was not sympathetic with Christians or their beliefs]:
"But all human efforts, all the lavish gifts of the emperor, and the propitiations of the gods, did not banish the sinister belief that the conflagration was the result of an order. Consequently, to get rid of the report, Nero fastened the guilt and inflicted the most exquisite tortures on a class hated for their abominations, called Christians by the populace. Christus, from whom the name had its origin, suffered the extreme penalty during the reign of Tiberius at the hands of one of our procurators, Pontius Pilatus, and a most mischievous superstition, thus checked for the moment, again broke out not only in Judaea, the first source of the evil, but even in Rome, where all things hideous and shameful from every part of the world find their center and become popular. Accordingly, an arrest was first made of all who pleaded guilty; then, upon their information, an immense multitude was convicted, not so much of the crime of firing the city, as of hatred against mankind. Mockery of every sort was added to their deaths. Covered with the skins of beasts, they were torn by dogs and perished, or were nailed to crosses, or were doomed to the flames and burnt, to serve as a nightly illumination, when daylight had expired. Nero offered his gardens for the spectacle, and was exhibiting a show in the circus, while he mingled with the people in the dress of a charioteer or stood aloft on a cart. Hence, even for criminals who deserved extreme and exemplary punishment, there arose a feeling of compassion; for it was not, as it seemed, for the public good, but to glut one man’s cruelty, that they were being destroyed." (Tacitus, Annals 15:33).

-Bible Archaeology
