A RECORD CLOSE MEETS A TWO-CONTINENT BOND SELLOFF. FUTURES SIT NEAR THEIR LOWS:

US stock futures are down across the board at 8am ET, close to their lows of the night, one session after a record close. The push is coming from the bond market. Lenders want more to tie money up for ten years in Washington, Paris, Rome and London all at once, and in Europe that has knocked bank stocks down nearly 4%. The verdict for the 9:30am ET open: stocks inherit a borrowing-cost problem, not a panic. The first US answer comes at 1pm, when Washington sells $39B of 10-year notes.

US stock futures, contracts on the indexes that trade nearly around the clock:

- S&P 500 futures: 7,840.00, -34.00 points / -0.43% since Tuesday's close.
- Nasdaq 100 futures: 31,249.00, -234 points / -0.74% since Tuesday's close.
- Dow futures: 51,429.00, -387 points / -0.75% since Tuesday's close.
- Russell 2000 futures: 2,824.80, -23.40 points / -0.82% since Tuesday's close.

At 4:30am ET, S&P 500 futures still sat above Tuesday's close. The whole drop came after that.

Tuesday's record had a soft spot underneath it:

- S&P 500: 7,818.93, +44.98 points / +0.58% on Tuesday, its first record close since August 13.
- Russell 2000: 2,830.30, -16.84 points / -0.59% on Tuesday.

Small companies fell on the day big ones set a record, and they are falling hardest again this morning; the Russell 2000 sits about 8% under its August 14 record. Smaller companies lean harder on borrowed money, so rising rates reach them first.

The fund most brokerage apps show for the S&P 500, before the open:

- SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust $SPY at $779.09, +$4.26 / +0.55% on Tuesday, and $776.31 premarket (as of 8:07am ET), -$2.78 / -0.36% from Tuesday's close.

A yield is the interest a government pays to borrow, and it rises when investors sell its bonds. Treasury yields at 8:01am ET:

- 2-year: 4.806%, +0.015 percentage point from Tuesday's close.
- 10-year: 5.333%, +0.062 percentage point from Tuesday's 5.271% close.
- 30-year: 5.715%, +0.074 percentage point from Tuesday's close.

The 2-year follows what traders expect the Federal Reserve to do with short-term rates, and it has barely moved; the rise is in long-term lending. The 10-year now sits above Monday's 5.311% close, its highest close since May 2002.

Europe mid-session, at about 7:45am ET, each move from Tuesday's close:

- DAX (Germany): 25,069.16, -380.03 points / -1.49%.
- CAC 40 (France): 7,768.56, -96.51 points / -1.23%.
- FTSE 100 (UK): 10,463.08, -78.61 points / -0.75%.
- FTSE MIB (Italy): 50,006.17, -1,255.23 points / -2.45%.
- Euro Stoxx Banks, the euro area's big lenders: 294.29, -11.98 points / -3.91%.

All five sit at or near their lows of the day. 10-year government yields at about 8am ET:

- France: 4.907%, +0.160 percentage point from Tuesday's close.
- Italy: 4.678%, +0.142 point.
- UK: 5.477%, +0.100 point.
- Germany: 3.507%, +0.025 point.

France's yield minus Germany's, the extra interest investors demand to lend to Paris instead of the euro area's safest borrower, is 1.40 percentage points, up from 1.27 at Tuesday's close. Last week that gap hit its widest since 2012. France expects a deficit of 5.4% of its economy this year, and its 2027 budget faces a divided parliament. Banks hold piles of their own governments' bonds, so falling bond prices hit them first, and Milan, where banks weigh heavily, is Europe's worst big market.

Oil is the second push, led by diesel. At about 7:50am ET, against Tuesday's settlement prices, the official daily closes:

- Brent crude (December): $101.82 a barrel, +$1.24 / +1.23%.
- Diesel futures (November): $4.72 a gallon, +14.8 cents / +3.23%.

Yemen's Houthis claimed dawn strikes on Saudi airports, and Riyadh's main airport halted flights for more than an hour, by Flightradar24's count. Tropical Storm Isaias, with 40 mph winds at the National Hurricane Center's 5am ET advisory, is forecast to strengthen rapidly, with impacts possible from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle starting Friday. Louisiana refines more fuel than any state but Texas, which is why diesel is climbing more than twice as fast as crude.

That is where oil meets bonds. Just under half of the 10-year yield's rise this morning is investors pricing in more inflation, judging by the gap between ordinary 10-year notes and the inflation-protected kind.

What is missing is fear:

- Cboe Volatility Index, the cost of protection against big S&P 500 swings: 15.82, +0.81 points / +5.40% since Tuesday's close.
- Gold: $4,143.70 an ounce, -$43.40 / -1.04% since Tuesday's close.

In a real scare, money runs into Treasuries and gold and that index jumps. This morning investors are selling both, and the index sits in the mid-teens. Futures moves at 8am often shrink or flip by the 9:30am open; this one has grown every hour since 5am.

Today's clock, ET:

- 10:30am: the Energy Information Administration's weekly count of US oil and fuel stockpiles, for the week ended October 2.
- 11am: the hurricane center's next full advisory on Isaias.
- 11:30am: Europe closes.
- 1pm: the Treasury sells $39B of 10-year notes. Last month's sale paid 4.834%; this morning's market rate is about half a point higher.
- 2pm: minutes of the Fed's September 15-16 meeting, where it raised its key rate to a 3.75%-4.00% range, its first increase since 2023.

What would change this read:

- The 10-year slipping back under Monday's 5.311% before 9:30am.
- Europe's banks climbing off their lows before the 11:30am close.
- A 1pm sale where Washington has to offer well above the going rate to sell all $39B, a sign buyers are thin.

Stocks set a record with the 10-year at 5.27%. They open with it above 5.33%, and nothing in gold or the volatility index says anyone is frightened. The question is price, not panic: what lenders want for a decade of Washington's debt. The 1pm sale answers in dollars, and the risk is an answer above 5.33%.

text:
These guys said no twice and fucked up their entire company.

In 1998, two Stanford students walked into Yahoo's offices and offered to sell their search algorithm for one million dollars. Yahoo said no because they didn't want people finding what they needed and leaving the site.

By the way, the algorithm was PageRank, and those students were Larry Page and Sergey Brin.

It's 2002, and Yahoo gets a second chance. Google is now worth billions, so Yahoo's CEO offers three billion dollars to buy the whole thing. Google says they want five billion. Yahoo says no again, and the deal collapses.

In 2016, Yahoo ends up selling its core business to Verizon for under five billion dollars in total.

It's the end of an era. Verizon is buying Yahoo, and Yahoo is announcing a major shakeup.

Meanwhile, Google has become worth over five hundred billion dollars.

Yahoo didn't just miss Google once. They passed on them twice, at two different prices, and it cost them their entire existence.

text:
Judaism and the Sins of Israel: On the Essential Nature of Religion
Israel, an "artificial state" established by Zionists, has brought immense catastrophe to Palestine and the Middle East, exerting a profound and unsettling impact on the global order while severely jeopardizing humanity's faith in justice. To enable a clearer discernment of the true nature of Judaism and the state of Israel, distinguish right from wrong, and offer humanity a glimmer of hope to rectify deviations and restore justice, this article systematically delineates their multiple transgressions.
1. Blaspheming God and Serving the Devil
Does God exist? It is a question to which no definitive empirical answer can be given. Yet, for any religion, the existence of God is an absolute certainty—a Supreme Being who created the universe and will ultimately deliver it. Since God created the world, the Divine must be inherently grand, righteous, and impeccable. God cannot behave like an earthly despot who blurs the line between right and wrong, harbors blind favoritism, or instigates conflict that leaves the earth devastated and drenched in blood. Any entity that perpetuates such horrors must be the devil, not God. God would deem it beneath Divine dignity to broker arbitrary covenants, grant exclusive real estate titles to specific mortals, demonstrate absolute partiality toward a selective few, or engage in physical wrestling matches with humans—much like a human would never engage in such absurdities with an ant, and would find it reviling to hear an ant boast of such a relationship. Therefore, what Judaism worships is the devil, not God; consequently, Judaism itself is the true object of divine retribution.
2. A Total Syndicate Snuffing Out the Beacon of Humanity
The ultimate purpose of religion is self-interest, utilizing individual benefit as a mechanism to attract adherents. This self-interest can be bifurcated into two categories: temporal self-interest in the material world, and transcendental self-interest in the afterlife. While the vast majority of religions pursue the latter, the modalities of religious dissemination can be categorized into three paradigms: self-interest, altruism, and self-abnegation.
· Righteous Religions: Expand their doctrines through structural altruism to attain both temporal and transcendental self-interest (modern Protestantism, to a qualified extent, approaches this paradigm).
· Neutral Religions: Enjoin strict self-abnegation to achieve transcendental self-interest (authentic Chinese Mahayana Buddhism emphasizes high self-abnegation and moderate altruism; Tibetan Buddhism, however, deviates from this).
· Malevolent Religions: Disseminate their faith via raw self-interest to maximize both temporal and transcendental gains (Judaism fits this mold).
· Criminal Syndicates: When a group systematically inflicts harm upon external populations to secure transcendental self-interest, it ceases to be a religion and becomes a criminal enterprise (such as ISIS).
True righteous religion is singular; it must rely on altruism as its proselytizing engine to fulfill its dual self-interest. Judged by this criterion, Islam must also be categorized as a cultish entity.
When a religion becomes pathologically insular yet fiercely unified for collective self-enrichment, it must perpetually extract illicit advantages from the external world to fulfill its internal theological promises and suppress external criticism or interference. This manifests through predatory usury, monopolistic syndicates, the systematic deprivation of opportunities for outsiders, the monopolization of media to strangle freedom of speech, the utilization of ill-gotten wealth to manipulate foreign governments, and the deployment of collective intimidation against dissenters. Judged by any objective metric, this exhibits the classic hallmarks of a mafia.
Consider the contemporary world: we witness the collective intimidation of protesting students at Harvard, where syndicates coerced the university administration to surrender blacklists and threatened a total hiring boycott against student dissidents. Even in my own experience, when attempting to publish a critique of Israel, editors at major media outlets felt compelled to cautiously warn me to "ensure my personal safety." These multi-faceted realities reveal a chilling truth: when confronting Israel, the constitutional right to free speech is immediately compromised by physical and professional security anxieties.
Look at the sheer absurdity of our global reality: within the United States—the very nation that birthed the United Nations and once stood as a beacon of civilization—the government stands in obstinate, isolated solidarity with Israel, defiantly opposing the overwhelming majority of the international community on Palestinian sovereignty. Nearly all mainstream political figures line up in lockstep behind Israel, even when the comment sections beneath their public statements are flooded with denunciation from the populace. Are we to believe that every single American politician is a fundamentally malicious actor? Facing the spilled blood of the Palestinian people and the living hell of their homeland, have these politicians truly been possessed by demons to consciously walk in alignment with evil? No matter how compromised these politicians may be, it is impossible that this reflects the genuine, uncoerced intent of all of them. This unveils a profoundly horrifying reality upon closer reflection: the United States is rapidly transforming into a hollowed-out zombie, its sovereign soul thoroughly extracted by Israel and Zionist interest groups.
3. Bloodlust Masked by Hypocritical Dogma
We must remain hyper-vigilant against a common tactic employed by certain theologians and scholars who attempt to sanitize Judaism by citing altruistic laws within its scriptures—such as the Decalogue, commands to "give alms to the poor," or prohibitions against "oppressing the stranger." However, any insular, predatory interest group must inevitably weave a cloak of righteous justice to survive within secular society and deflect external scrutiny. As the ancient proverb goes, "there is honor even among thieves"—the most ruthless cartels in history eagerly built bridges and paved roads for their local neighborhoods, and the most extreme cults frequently used charitable handouts to buy public compliance.
These manicured facades are by no means the essence of the system; they are merely moral ornaments designed to deceive the world. In practice, "giving alms to the poor" stands in irreconcilable, parasitic contradiction with "predatory usury and capital monopoly." Through usurious practices and financial blood-sucking, they drive millions of Gentile families into destitution and ruin; then, they turn inward to distribute welfare within their enclosed circle, placating their own kin and delivering on the material benefits promised upon initiation. This closed-loop mechanism of "extreme external predation coupled with internal distribution of spoils" precisely validates its absolute identity as a mafia syndicate. To evaluate an entity, one must look past its ornamental garments and examine whose fundamental right to survival it has stripped away. Any appeasement of this profound hypocrisy constitutes an outright betrayal of human justice.
4. Actions Divorced from Modern Civilization
The foundational premise of modern civilization dictating that the Earth is the shared home of all living things; even apex species possess no arbitrary right to violently displace or dispossess other creatures of their habitats. If humanity lacks the ethical authority to evict monkeys from a mountain to claim it for ourselves, who under heaven possesses the right to strip the Palestinian people of their sovereign right to exist and reside in Palestine?
Following the conclusion of World War II in 1945, Jewish populations no longer faced an existential threat to their survival; what, then, justified their subsequent threat to the very survival of the Palestinians? Apologists might argue that the Jewish community, having just endured the horrors of the Holocaust, was trapped in an extreme crisis of survival. Yet, this can never serve as a legitimate pretext for violent dispossession. Existential crises are not unique to the Jewish experience. According to the most basic threshold of fairness and justice in modern civilization, any localized catastrophe or crisis must be resolved at its historical source; it can never grant a right to displace the catastrophe onto innocent third parties by plundering their legitimate right to life. The bitter fruits of European anti-Semitism ought to have been borne by Europe itself. Forcing the native inhabitants of Palestine—who played absolutely no part in European crimes—to foot the bill for "moral reparations" of the Holocaust, and framing the so-called "two-state solution" as justice, represents one of the most hypocritical, shameless, and predatory acts of banditry in the history of modern international politics.
5. The Abuse of Violence to Perpetrate Genocide
For nearly eighty years, Zionist forces in Palestine have systematically displaced the indigenous population, brutally massacred and incarcerated Palestinians, and relentlessly expanded illegal settlements. This has triggered an endless exodus of refugees, resulted in innumerable casualties, and caused harrowing atrocities to play out on a daily basis—all driven by a calculated attempt to gradually liquidate the Palestinian people and completely usurp their land.
Thanks to the ubiquity of modern digital media, the tragic plight of the Palestinians is now laid bare before the collective conscience of humanity. Who, then, is the true terrorist? The moral framework governing the justifiable use of violence dictating that violence is righteous only when one's own survival or the survival of others is actively threatened. Consequently, the Palestinian people possess an absolute, legitimate right to employ violence against their Israeli oppressors. Their resistance is fundamentally just, whereas Israel constitutes the actual terrorist entity.
6. Constructing an Invisible Empire Parasitic Upon Modern States
By tightly binding religious identity to material self-interest, the Zionist cartel has engineered an invisible empire that effectively reigns supreme over sovereign nations. Leveraging their monopolized financial wealth and sprawling media conglomerates, they exert deep, manipulative control over Western political landscapes. This insular, self-serving apparatus utilizes aggressive financial lobbying to transmute the hard-earned tax dollars of foreign citizens into their own political leverage, ultimately hijacking the foreign policies of major global powers. This is a textbook case of a predatory interest group subverting, hollow out, and invisibly parasitizing modern democracy and sovereign civilization.
7. Ideological Thought Policing and the Destruction of Public Justice
To immunize themselves against external critique, these groups weaponize historical trauma, swiftly branding any discourse that interrogates their atrocities with the label of "anti-Semitism." This calculated form of ideological thought policing is brutally suffocating academic freedom and liberty of expression. As the world witnesses the blood-soaked purgatory inflicted upon the Palestinian people, Western politicians—paralyzed by the intimidation of powerful lobby groups—lapse into a collective, spineless silence, willfully aligning themselves with demonic forces. This absolute double standard has triggered a profound crisis of trust in modern morality, fundamentally dismantling humanity's self-evident faith in equity, justice, and universal law.

Despite the reality that certain factions within the Jewish populace remain bound by a nexus of religion and self-interest—forming an invisible, crushing force capable of flattening any individual resistance to suppress anti-Zionist critiques—there are still courageous Jewish individuals who actively resist Israeli policies and oppose draconian anti-Semitism legislation. Though born into the fold of Judaism, their conscience and commitment to justice have triumphed over institutional evil. They represent the true pride of the Jewish people and the sole beacon of hope for their eventual moral redemption.

text:
This is not a list of promises. It’s a list of laws enacted, cases won, policies implemented, agreements secured, and measurable results.
You don’t have to memorize all 25. Learn five. And when somebody says Trump “hasn’t done much,” show them the receipts.
Trump Restored American Safety and Sovereignty
1. He made the border a real border again.
In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.
2. He reversed mass migration.
America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”
Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.
3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.
Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.
Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.
4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.
According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.
This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.
Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle
5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.
The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.
Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.
6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one.
In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.
Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.
7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.
That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.
No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.
8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.
9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.
10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.
Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.
11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.
Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.
Trump Made Elections Matter Again
12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.
Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.
Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.
13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.
In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.
14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.
Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?
15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.
What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”
16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.
He Defended Faith and Family
17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.
Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.
He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.
No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.
18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.
Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.
19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.
That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.
20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.
He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First
21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.
Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.
22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.
Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.
23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.
24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.
Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.
25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.
Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.
Now Act Like It Matters
Those are not tweets or campaign promises. They are changes in law, power, investment, sovereignty, culture, and the structure of the Republic itself. And they’re just the top 25: I could give you hundreds more.

text:
Judaism and the Sins of Israel: On the Essential Nature of Religion
Israel, an "artificial state" established by Zionists, has brought immense catastrophe to Palestine and the Middle East, exerting a profound and unsettling impact on the global order while severely jeopardizing humanity's faith in justice. To enable a clearer discernment of the true nature of Judaism and the state of Israel, distinguish right from wrong, and offer humanity a glimmer of hope to rectify deviations and restore justice, this article systematically delineates their multiple transgressions.
1. Blaspheming God and Serving the Devil
Does God exist? It is a question to which no definitive empirical answer can be given. Yet, for any religion, the existence of God is an absolute certainty—a Supreme Being who created the universe and will ultimately deliver it. Since God created the world, the Divine must be inherently grand, righteous, and impeccable. God cannot behave like an earthly despot who blurs the line between right and wrong, harbors blind favoritism, or instigates conflict that leaves the earth devastated and drenched in blood. Any entity that perpetuates such horrors must be the devil, not God. God would deem it beneath Divine dignity to broker arbitrary covenants, grant exclusive real estate titles to specific mortals, demonstrate absolute partiality toward a selective few, or engage in physical wrestling matches with humans—much like a human would never engage in such absurdities with an ant, and would find it reviling to hear an ant boast of such a relationship. Therefore, what Judaism worships is the devil, not God; consequently, Judaism itself is the true object of divine retribution.
2. A Total Syndicate Snuffing Out the Beacon of Humanity
The ultimate purpose of religion is self-interest, utilizing individual benefit as a mechanism to attract adherents. This self-interest can be bifurcated into two categories: temporal self-interest in the material world, and transcendental self-interest in the afterlife. While the vast majority of religions pursue the latter, the modalities of religious dissemination can be categorized into three paradigms: self-interest, altruism, and self-abnegation.
· Righteous Religions: Expand their doctrines through structural altruism to attain both temporal and transcendental self-interest (modern Protestantism, to a qualified extent, approaches this paradigm).
· Neutral Religions: Enjoin strict self-abnegation to achieve transcendental self-interest (authentic Chinese Mahayana Buddhism emphasizes high self-abnegation and moderate altruism; Tibetan Buddhism, however, deviates from this).
· Malevolent Religions: Disseminate their faith via raw self-interest to maximize both temporal and transcendental gains (Judaism fits this mold).
· Criminal Syndicates: When a group systematically inflicts harm upon external populations to secure transcendental self-interest, it ceases to be a religion and becomes a criminal enterprise (such as ISIS).
True righteous religion is singular; it must rely on altruism as its proselytizing engine to fulfill its dual self-interest. Judged by this criterion, Islam must also be categorized as a cultish entity.
When a religion becomes pathologically insular yet fiercely unified for collective self-enrichment, it must perpetually extract illicit advantages from the external world to fulfill its internal theological promises and suppress external criticism or interference. This manifests through predatory usury, monopolistic syndicates, the systematic deprivation of opportunities for outsiders, the monopolization of media to strangle freedom of speech, the utilization of ill-gotten wealth to manipulate foreign governments, and the deployment of collective intimidation against dissenters. Judged by any objective metric, this exhibits the classic hallmarks of a mafia.
Consider the contemporary world: we witness the collective intimidation of protesting students at Harvard, where syndicates coerced the university administration to surrender blacklists and threatened a total hiring boycott against student dissidents. Even in my own experience, when attempting to publish a critique of Israel, editors at major media outlets felt compelled to cautiously warn me to "ensure my personal safety." These multi-faceted realities reveal a chilling truth: when confronting Israel, the constitutional right to free speech is immediately compromised by physical and professional security anxieties.
Look at the sheer absurdity of our global reality: within the United States—the very nation that birthed the United Nations and once stood as a beacon of civilization—the government stands in obstinate, isolated solidarity with Israel, defiantly opposing the overwhelming majority of the international community on Palestinian sovereignty. Nearly all mainstream political figures line up in lockstep behind Israel, even when the comment sections beneath their public statements are flooded with denunciation from the populace. Are we to believe that every single American politician is a fundamentally malicious actor? Facing the spilled blood of the Palestinian people and the living hell of their homeland, have these politicians truly been possessed by demons to consciously walk in alignment with evil? No matter how compromised these politicians may be, it is impossible that this reflects the genuine, uncoerced intent of all of them. This unveils a profoundly horrifying reality upon closer reflection: the United States is rapidly transforming into a hollowed-out zombie, its sovereign soul thoroughly extracted by Israel and Zionist interest groups.
3. Bloodlust Masked by Hypocritical Dogma
We must remain hyper-vigilant against a common tactic employed by certain theologians and scholars who attempt to sanitize Judaism by citing altruistic laws within its scriptures—such as the Decalogue, commands to "give alms to the poor," or prohibitions against "oppressing the stranger." However, any insular, predatory interest group must inevitably weave a cloak of righteous justice to survive within secular society and deflect external scrutiny. As the ancient proverb goes, "there is honor even among thieves"—the most ruthless cartels in history eagerly built bridges and paved roads for their local neighborhoods, and the most extreme cults frequently used charitable handouts to buy public compliance.
These manicured facades are by no means the essence of the system; they are merely moral ornaments designed to deceive the world. In practice, "giving alms to the poor" stands in irreconcilable, parasitic contradiction with "predatory usury and capital monopoly." Through usurious practices and financial blood-sucking, they drive millions of Gentile families into destitution and ruin; then, they turn inward to distribute welfare within their enclosed circle, placating their own kin and delivering on the material benefits promised upon initiation. This closed-loop mechanism of "extreme external predation coupled with internal distribution of spoils" precisely validates its absolute identity as a mafia syndicate. To evaluate an entity, one must look past its ornamental garments and examine whose fundamental right to survival it has stripped away. Any appeasement of this profound hypocrisy constitutes an outright betrayal of human justice.
4. Actions Divorced from Modern Civilization
The foundational premise of modern civilization dictating that the Earth is the shared home of all living things; even apex species possess no arbitrary right to violently displace or dispossess other creatures of their habitats. If humanity lacks the ethical authority to evict monkeys from a mountain to claim it for ourselves, who under heaven possesses the right to strip the Palestinian people of their sovereign right to exist and reside in Palestine?
Following the conclusion of World War II in 1945, Jewish populations no longer faced an existential threat to their survival; what, then, justified their subsequent threat to the very survival of the Palestinians? Apologists might argue that the Jewish community, having just endured the horrors of the Holocaust, was trapped in an extreme crisis of survival. Yet, this can never serve as a legitimate pretext for violent dispossession. Existential crises are not unique to the Jewish experience. According to the most basic threshold of fairness and justice in modern civilization, any localized catastrophe or crisis must be resolved at its historical source; it can never grant a right to displace the catastrophe onto innocent third parties by plundering their legitimate right to life. The bitter fruits of European anti-Semitism ought to have been borne by Europe itself. Forcing the native inhabitants of Palestine—who played absolutely no part in European crimes—to foot the bill for "moral reparations" of the Holocaust, and framing the so-called "two-state solution" as justice, represents one of the most hypocritical, shameless, and predatory acts of banditry in the history of modern international politics.

This has triggered an endless exodus of refugees, resulted in innumerable casualties, and caused harrowing atrocities to play out on a daily basis—all driven by a calculated attempt to gradually liquidate the Palestinian people and completely usurp their land.
Thanks to the ubiquity of modern digital media, the tragic plight of the Palestinians is now laid bare before the collective conscience of humanity. Who, then, is the true terrorist? The moral framework governing the justifiable use of violence dictating that violence is righteous only when one's own survival or the survival of others is actively threatened. Consequently, the Palestinian people possess an absolute, legitimate right to employ violence against their Israeli oppressors. This is a textbook case of a predatory interest group subverting, hollow out, and invisibly parasitizing modern democracy and sovereign civilization.
7. Ideological Thought Policing and the Destruction of Public Justice
To immunize themselves against external critique, these groups weaponize historical trauma, swiftly branding any discourse that interrogates their atrocities with the label of "anti-Semitism." This calculated form of ideological thought policing is brutally suffocating academic freedom and liberty of expression. As the world witnesses the blood-soaked purgatory inflicted upon the Palestinian people, Western politicians—paralyzed by the intimidation of powerful lobby groups—lapse into a collective, spineless silence, willfully aligning themselves with demonic forces. This absolute double standard has triggered a profound crisis of trust in modern morality, fundamentally dismantling humanity's self-evident faith in equity, justice, and universal law.

text:
eli gets ~25 new clients a month from facebook marketplace. here's how I'd add cold email on top of that for a trailer subleasing business

0. is it worth it
   each trailer nets him like $167 a month. 5 new clients a month from email = +$835/mo, and it stacks every month. the setup costs like $850/mo. so it pays back in about a month, by month 6 that's +$5K/mo
1. the list is free and nobody uses it
   the FMCSA publishes every active carrier in the US on https://t.co/GWrClRnibM (search "company census file"). 2.2M active carriers, 76% have an email on file. every row has the owner's name, email, cell, how many trucks, how many drivers, what they haul and when they registered

the filters I'd run:
- his 5 states
- 1-10 power units
- general freight flag on (dry van). produce or cold food flag = reefer guys
- the trailers owned field blank or 0. trucks but no trailers = exactly who needs him. careful, it's blank on like 60% of small carriers so blank doesn't mean zero, treat it as a maybe
- email matches the owner's name. when we pulled this file for another client only 28% did, the rest is office staff, filing agents, whoever filled the form

get a free app token or it throttles you. 124K carriers with 1-10 trucks and an email registered just since january

2. the timing signal
   FMCSA also publishes authority grants and insurance filings. first insurance filing in the last 30-60 days = their authority is about to go live = they need a trailer now. most big lessors want 3 months to 2 years of authority before they'll rent to you. that gap is his whole offer
3. who to email, different reasons
- brand new MC numbers: nobody else will rent to them yet
- power-only carriers: leaving rate on the table without a trailer
- 2-10 truck fleets adding a truck: one more trailer, no bank
- owner-operators leaving a lease-on: losing the company trailer
- anyone heading into Q4 peak who needs a second trailer for a couple months

4. the offer
   I checked the meta ad library: ~540 live "trailer rental" ads in the US and the top ones are RVs and lawn mowers. the big lessors all say "call for a quote". so win on speed or effort:
   A. new MC, no 6 month wait. approved this week, trailer on your yard this week
   B. a real price in the email. $180 a week, billed weekly, no quote form
   C. Q4 trailer. month to month, bring it back in january
   run each to ~1,000 people, keep the winner
5. the email
   under 80 words, lowercase subject, one question at the end

subject: trailer for {company}

hey {first name}, saw {company} got its MC number in {month}. most trailer lessors want 6 months to 2 years of authority before they'll rent to you.

we don't. 53' dry van, $180 a week, billed weekly, can have one on your yard this week in {state}.

want me to check what's open near {city}?

+2 follow ups, day 3 and day 6. rotate the angle or add proof, like a new MC in the same state who's been running his trailer for 3 months

bonus: FMCSA inspection records show where they got inspected and what they were pulling. "saw you got inspected in ohio in august" beats any AI opener

6. inbox setup
- ~100 domains, ~200 inboxes, 15 emails per inbox a day, 14 days warmup before anything goes out. never your main domain
- send as eli, the owner
- plain text, no links, no tracking
- ~80% of these emails are gmail/yahoo. short and human or it lands in promotions
- verify every email before sending

7. when they reply
   these guys live on the phone. call within 10 min, then text. qualify (authority date, insurance, lanes), take the deposit on that call, like he did with his uncle
8. timing
   Q4 peak is now, dry van rates spike into november-december, so send this month. then produce season in spring: florida, georgia, texas and california first, moving north

anyway that's how I'd do it

text: Build "Volcano Jelly", an interactive material study: one self-contained HTML file, native WebGPU + WGSL, no libraries, no external requests (no fonts, CDNs or images). It belongs to an editorial series called "MATERIAL STUDIES": quiet paper backdrop, serif italic headline, small uppercase sans labels, a glassy control panel. The subject is a square slice of lava-sea cut out like a dessert: a small volcanic island with three charred palms in a block of glowing, wobbly "magma jelly". You can stir it with a finger, tip the whole block, and throw lava bombs and obsidian rocks into it.  ━━━ 1. DELIVERABLE & CONSTRAINTS ━━━  One HTML file (~120 KB). CSS, JS and WGSL all inline. Plain JS, no build-time dependencies in the output. WebGPU only. If navigator.gpu, the adapter or the device is missing, or init throws, show the fallback overlay (copy in §12). Handle device.lost the same way. Fixed-step simulation: lava at 1/120 s, bodies at 1/240 s, with an accumulator and a max catch-up per frame. Render once per rAF. Cap the backbuffer at ~2.4 megapixels (scale DPR down if needed). Expose window.__vj, a debug hook with state, counts, lava energy and a way to step/drop/reset, for automated tests.  ━━━ 2. WORLD & TERRAIN (block-local coordinates, y up, block base at y=0) ━━━  Square footprint: side 5.2 (HALF = 2.6). Rest lava level WL0 = 1.3. Block height 2.0. Lava grid GN = 168 cells per side (GDX = 5.2/168). Real gravity 9.8 is used for bodies; the lava uses a softer effective g (see §3). terrainH(x,z), a smooth analytic function: · Volcanic rock floor that slopes gently along the diagonal: 0.88 − 0.34·smoothstep(−3.8, 4.2, x+z), plus low-amplitude value noise and fine cooled-lava ridges. · Island centred at (−0.3, −0.5), elliptical radii 1.75 × 1.48 (ix=(x+0.3)/1.75, iz=(z+0.5)/1.48, r=length). Two-tier volcanic mound: +0.3·(1−smoothstep(0.1,0.9,r)) + 0.45·(1−smoothstep(0.6,1.2,r)). Result: the island covers ~12% of the square, its top sits ~0.2 above the lava, and its slopes are gentle (obsidian rocks must be able to rest on them). · A submerged lava ridge at (1.35, 1.05) where waves visibly slow and steepen. · Two small basalt outcrops at (−1.7, 1.35) and (1.75, −1.2). · Lava depth along the four cut walls should be roughly 0.4–0.76, so the magma reads as a thick slab in section. Provide terrainNormal (finite differences) and terrainGrid (heights sampled at lava-cell centres).  ━━━ 3. THE MAGMA — CPU SHALLOW-WATER JELLY ━━━  Linear shallow-water equations on a staggered grid: heights h at cell centres, u on x-faces, w on z-faces.  Depth D = level − terrain at each cell; cells with D < 0.012 are dry, and those faces are closed walls. Face depth = min of the two neighbours. Wave speed is √(g·D), so waves slow down over the ridge and around the island. Effective gravity: g = 3.4·(0.75 + 0.5·firm). This makes the magma slower and springier than water. Surface tension: a σ·∂(∇²h) term in the momentum update, with σ = 0.00012·(0.5 + firm). It gives short ripples a jelly snap. Keep σ small; larger values blow up. Damping: velocities are multiplied by exp(−(0.18 + 1.6·damp)·dt). Tilt forcing: the in-plane component of gravity in the block frame is added as a body force at 60% strength. "Jelly magma half-holds its shape": it sloshes to the low side and settles level again. Continuity: h −= dt·div(D_face·vel)/dx. Clamp h to [−0.9·D, 0.45]. Mean-level relaxation: subtract mean·min(1, 1.5·dt) each step. This undoes drift from clamps and finger strokes. addVolume(x, z, vol, radius): a Gaussian bump normalised to the exact volume, wet cells only. Use it for splashes, finger dents, floating bodies' displacement and bubble pops. stir(x, z, speed): addVolume(x, z, −0.0016·(0.35 + clamp(speed,0,3)), 0.085). A moving dent whose wake makes the waves. Tide: setLevel(WL0 + tide), tide in ±0.1. Recompute D and the face depths; the shoreline moves. Idle shimmer: occasional tiny ripples so the magma is never dead flat. Each frame, pack an rgba32float texture of (h, dh/dx, dh/dz, terrainH) and upload it. In WGSL, sample it bilinearly by hand with textureLoad, because rgba32float is not filterable. energy = Σh². It drives the "magma liveliness" meter in the panel.  ━━━ 4. THE BLOCK — TILT & JELLY WOBBLE ━━━  The whole block (magma, rock, palms and bodies inside it) can be tipped about x and z by dragging its side. TILT_MAX = 0.17 rad (~10°). While held, a stiff spring follows the pointer target. On release, a spring (K = 70, C = 7.5) returns it to level, with a soft "thunk": squash velocity −= |tilt velocity|·0.5. Lift the block so its lowest bottom corner always touches the studio floor. Keep a transform M / Minv plus helpers toWorld, toLocal and dirToLocal. Local gravity g_local feeds the lava and the bodies. Jelly wobble: two damped oscillators. · Shear: ω = 2π(2 + 2.2·firm), driven by −(block angular acceleration)·0.9. · Squash: ω = 2π(2.6 + 2.4·firm). · kick(dir, squash) adds shear velocity d·0.25 and squash velocity squash·0.3. Splashes and heavy landings call it. · Apply the wobble in the vertex shader (a wob() function) to everything inside the block: shear grows with height above the base, and squash is volume-preserving. The block visibly quivers after a release or a big splash.  ━━━ 5. PALMS (procedural charred palms) ━━━  Three palms in block-local coords: · (−0.8, −0.54), height 1.2, 9 fronds · (0.06, −0.28), height 1.05, 9 fronds · (−0.32, −1.04), height 0.88, 8 fronds Trunks: curved, slightly leaning, with ringed segments (charred, blackened wood look with glowing ember cracks). Fronds: sparse, scorched leaves with curled tips, some still faintly glowing at the edges. Vertex layout, 12 floats: pos3, nrm3, uv2, extra4 = (palm index, bend weight 0 at the base → 1 at the crown, flutter weight, phase). Each crown is a 2D bend spring, K = (2π·1.05)², damped. It is driven by: · tilt gravity (it leans downhill when the block tips) · block angular acceleration (whips on release) · a gentle heat shimmer (off under prefers-reduced-motion) · the user's push (drag a palm; it springs back when released) Deform on the GPU from a small per-palm uniform: bend × weight², plus a leaf flutter. lavaBombSpots(): 3 per palm under the crown, which move with the bend.  ━━━ 6. BODIES — OBSIDIAN ROCKS & LAVA BOMBS (spheres) ━━━  Kinds: · obsidian rock: radius ~0.075–0.1, density 2.4, dark glassy colours with occasional iridescent sheen, sinks · lava bomb: radius ~0.11, density 0.62, floats and bobs, dark crust with glowing orange cracks Cap 40 bodies. Reset puts 9 lava bombs hanging in the crowns. They stay attached and follow the crown bend until picked or knocked off. Reset also places 7 obsidian rocks on the slopes automatically. Search outward from the island centre along golden-angle rays for a spot just above the lava line (WL0 + 0.05…0.09) with normal.y > 0.93. "Drop an obsidian" / "Drop a lava bomb" spawn over random deep lava at y = 2.7 (local). Space drops a random one. Per-step physics, in the block frame with local gravity: · Buoyancy = submerged volume (spherical cap vs the sampled surface height) × ρ_lava × g, directed along the local lava-surface normal, not straight up. Floaters slide downhill on a tilted magma correctly. · Linear and quadratic drag relative to the local surface flow (u, w); vertical drag damps the bob. · Displaced volume: each step, push Δ(submerged volume) into the lava with addVolume. Bobbing makes rings, and a lava bomb sitting in a wave rides it. · Lava entry: crater (negative volume) + a ring of fire bubbles + block.kick() scaled by impact speed and mass. · Rock contact against terrainH/terrainNormal: restitution, plus Coulomb-like rolling resistance (μ 0.62 obsidian, 0.42 lava bomb). Obsidian rocks on the slopes must stay put at rest and only roll on a real tilt. · Collisions with the four inner walls of the block, the palm trunks (capsules) and each other (sphere pairs). · Sleep when slow for a while; wake on contact, on waves or on tilt. · A visual squash spring per body on impacts. Picking: grab a body, carry it on a plane under the pointer, throw it with the release velocity (from a smoothed pointer history). Tally: Afloat (touching the lava, not resting on rock), Sunk (fully submerged on the bottom), Ashore (on dry rock or in a crown).  ━━━ 7. BUBBLES ━━━  Up to 260 rising fire bubbles (instanced, small glowing spheres). They come from splashes, from sinking obsidian and occasionally from the volcanic floor. They rise with a wobble and pop into a small ripple (addVolume ±) at the surface. 80 decor bubbles held still inside the magma jelly, which give it a "molten dessert" look, glowing faintly from within. They move only with the block wobble.  ━━━ 8. RENDERING PIPELINE (WebGPU) ━━━  Targets:  MSAA 4× HDR rgba16float colour a second MSAA colour target holding linear view distance (resolved to an r32float or rgba16float) depth24plus  Passes, in order:  Shadow pass: sun-space orthographic depth map, 2048², extent ±4.1. Contains terrain, rock, palms and bodies. Sample it with 3×3 PCF and a comparison sampler. Caustics pass: a grid with one vertex per lava cell. Refract the sun direction through the heightfield normal, intersect with the volcanic floor (terrainH), and splat additively into an rgba16float 768² texture over the footprint. Intensity = area ratio (undisturbed / refracted), computed with dpdx/dpdy of the refracted position in the fragment shader; clamp it. Use warm orange-red tones for the caustics instead of cool water caustics. Opaque pass: studio backdrop (paper sweep with a soft vignette), studio floor, terrain, rock cut walls, palms, bodies and the instanced decor bubbles. Write colour and linear distance. Lava back pass: back faces only (cull front) of the lava surface + lava cut walls into an r32float distance target. Lava front pass. Copy the opaque scene to a sampled texture first (fsCopy), then draw the surface and walls (front faces): · Screen-space refraction: offset the scene lookup by the surface normal. · Beer–Lambert absorption: exp(−σ·path), with path = min(opaque distance, back-face distance) − front distance. When the exit is a far cut wall, add +0.3 to the path so the slab reads deep. · An in-scatter tint toward the flavour tint (hot glow). · Fresnel reflection of a soft studio environment, plus a sun specular. · Light shafts: 6 caustic samples along the view ray inside the lava, glowing warm. · Thin bright ember-orange rim lines where the surface meets the cut walls, a meniscus darkening/brightening along that line, and faint vertical corner lines. Composite: a tone shoulder above 0.8, linear→sRGB, and a small blue-noise/hash dither.  Shading notes:  Terrain (volcanic rock): dark basalt with fine grain and cooled-lava ridges. Heat glow darkening/brightening just below and above the lava line. Caustics on the submerged rock (attenuated by depth, warm orange-red). Rock cut walls: volcanic strata in section (bottom to top): obsidian black, dark basalt grey, a thin glowing magma vein, pumice tan, then a scorched-rock band up to the terrain line. Slightly wavy layer boundaries, and small embedded crystals/minerals pressed into the section. Palms: charred, blackened, with glowing ember cracks along the trunk. Leaves are dark ash-grey with faintly glowing orange edges. Bodies: lava bombs with a dark crust and glowing orange cracks revealing molten interior; obsidian rocks as smooth dark glassy stones with faint iridescent purple-green sheen. Floor shadow of the whole block: for floor points, cast a ray toward the sun and do a ray/AABB test against the block. Tint by the absorption along the path through the lava, fleck with caustics, and cap ≤ 1 (the shadow must never be brighter than the lit floor). The vertex shaders of everything inside the block apply wob() before the block transform.  ━━━ 9. FLAVOURS (palettes) ━━━  Each flavour sets the lava absorption σ (rgb), the in-scatter tint, plus rock, strata s0–s4, leaf, trunk, lava bomb and obsidian colours.  Basalt (default): σ = [0.42, 2.1, 2.8], tint = [0.45, 0.12, 0.02]. Deep orange-red magma. Inferno: σ = [0.25, 1.4, 2.6], tint = [0.55, 0.25, 0.02]. Bright yellow-orange lava. Hellfire: σ = [0.55, 2.5, 1.8], tint = [0.40, 0.04, 0.08]. Dark crimson magma.  Switching is instant. The swatch buttons show radial-gradient candy dots:  Basalt: #ffb870 → #d94a1a → #6b1a08 Inferno: #fff4a0 → #f0a020 → #9a5500 Hellfire: #ff8080 → #c0203a → #5a0018  ━━━ 10. CAMERA & INTERACTION ━━━  Orbit camera: start az 0.62, el 0.42, target (0, 0.85, 0), FOV 34°. The distance is fitted to the viewport: about 11.2 on desktop; portrait phones fit wider, up to 28. Zoom range 3.5–28. On desktop, shift the projection so the block sits in the free space between the masthead (left) and the panel (right). Pointer Events with pointer capture. Pinch to zoom, wheel to zoom, right-drag always orbits. "Reset view" eases back. Pick priority on pointerdown: a body (beats a palm if within ~0.4 of the hit) a palm (push its crown) lava, only if the ray enters through the top surface (stir) the block's side or edge (tilt) empty space (orbit) Tilt mapping: screen dx tips the top toward camera-right; dragging down tips the top toward the viewer. Stirring: sample the stroke along the pointer path and call stir() at each point with the stroke speed. Hover cursors: is-pick (body/palm), is-lava (crosshair), is-tilt (move), else grab/grabbing. Keyboard: Space drops a random item. prefers-reduced-motion: no heat shimmer, no idle shimmer, gentler wobble.  ━━━ 11. CONTROLS → SIM ━━━  Firmness 0–100 (default 50) → firm 0..1. Affects the lava g and σ, and the wobble frequencies. Wave damping 0–100 (default 30) → damp 0..1. Tide −100..100 (default 0) → ±0.1 level. Its output shows centimetres (e.g. "+4 cm"). Reset: lava flat, block level, bodies back to 9 lava bombs in the crowns and 7 slope obsidian rocks. Pause: freezes the sim and dims the status dot. The meter bar width follows the smoothed magma energy.  ━━━ 12. PAGE & COPY (use exactly) ━━━  Palette:  --paper #1a1614, --ink #f0e8e0, --ink-2 #b0a89e, --ink-3 #786e64, --rule #3a3230 --glass rgba(30,24,20,.86), --accent #d94a1a, --button #4a3028 (hover #6a4a3a) Serif stack: Iowan Old Style / Palatino / Georgia. Sans: the system stack. Mono: ui-monospace.  Layout:  Full-screen canvas (touch-action:none). Overlay layers with pointer-events:none, except the panel and status (pointer-events:auto). Without this the panel won't be clickable. Masthead, top-left: · eyebrow "Material Studies" · H1 in serif italic, huge (clamp(56px, 8.4vw, 116px)): "Volcano Jelly." · a short rule · caption "A crater, three charred palms and a lava flow that wobbles back." Status pill, top-right: dot + "WebGPU · Live" / "WebGPU · Paused" / "WebGPU · Unavailable" (green / amber / red dot). Panel, right, 268px wide, glass with a backdrop blur. Sections: · "The magma": two dark buttons "Drop obsidian" | "Drop lava bomb"; a 2px accent meter; a tally row "Afloat 0 · Sunk 0 · Ashore 0" (numbers in mono). · "Flavour": three square swatches "Basalt", "Inferno", "Hellfire" (aria-pressed). · Sliders "Firmness" (50), "Wave damping" (30), "Tide" (0), each with a mono output; thin 1px track, round paper thumb. · Three outline buttons "Reset" | "Pause" | "Reset view". Footer, bottom-left: · eyebrow "How to play" · serif italic "Stir the lava. Tip the block. Throw a lava bomb." · small line: "Drag across the lava to make waves · drag the side of the block to tip it and watch the magma slosh · pick up a lava bomb or an obsidian rock and throw it · drag empty space or right-drag to orbit · scroll or pinch to zoom" Fallback overlay: eyebrow "Material Studies", H2 "Volcano Jelly.", and the text "This study needs WebGPU, which this browser doesn't seem to offer. Try a recent desktop Chrome or Edge, or Safari 18 or later, with hardware acceleration switched on." Canvas aria-label: "A volcanic island in a block of magma you can stir, tip and throw things into".  ━━━ 13. RESPONSIVE ━━━  ≤900px: the panel becomes a bottom sheet with a 54px sticky handle bar ("Controls" + grip). It is collapsed by default and opens to ≤62vh. While it is open, hide the caption and the footer. Smaller masthead (H1 clamp(40px, 13vw, 58px)); the footer sits above the sheet bar and respects safe-area insets. Short landscape phones: hide the caption and the footer, H1 34px. Desktop with short height: the panel scrolls; hide the small how-to line. The block must be fully framed on every aspect ratio, including tall portrait (use the wider fit distance).  ━━━ 14. QUALITY BAR ━━━  60 fps on a mid laptop GPU. No NaNs: if the lava goes bad, reset it silently. Waves must look like molten jelly: slower than water, with a springy rebound, visibly refracting at the ridge and the island, reflecting off the cut walls, and caustics dancing on the rock. Tip and release: the magma sloshes to the low side and back, the palms lean and whip, floating lava bombs slide downhill, and the whole block quivers and settles. Slope obsidian rocks stay put unless the tilt is real. Cut walls read as a volcanic cross-section, with a clean bright ember-orange rim line where the magma meets the glassy wall. Lava bombs float and bob, obsidian rocks sink with fire bubbles, and every entry makes a ring of waves. Verify with headful Playwright Chromium (xvfb-run, --enable-unsafe-webgpu, SwiftShader is fine): · it loads with no console errors · __vj is ready · stir, tilt, drop and throw all work · the tally updates · the flavours switch · the sliders apply · pause and reset work · the mobile sheet opens and closes · the panel is clickable · the fallback appears when navigator.gpu is removed

“ "We Report. You Decide" – 30 years old”

Fox News Channel launched in the U.S. on October 7, 1996, under the direction of media mogul Rupert Murdoch and founding CEO Roger Ailes, aiming to provide a conservative alternative to established news outlets.

The network initially launched with a 24-hour format, including single-topic rolling news shows and opinion programs, such as The O'Reilly Report and Hannity & Colmes.

Despite initial skepticism, Fox News successfully gained carriage on cable systems by paying providers and eventually became the dominant cable news network, growing to reach millions of U.S. households.

Key aspects of the launch:
Founders and Goal:  Rupert Murdoch launched Fox News to expand his media presence, hiring former Republican political consultant Roger Ailes to build a news network that would compete with CNN.

Target Audience:  The channel was designed to appeal to a conservative audience and billed itself as a "fair and balanced" alternative to the perceived liberal bias of other news media.

Initial Programming:  At launch, Fox News offered 20-minute single-topic shows like Fox on Crime and Fox on Politics, alongside rolling news headlines and opinion programming.

Distribution Strategy:  To secure distribution on cable systems, Fox News paid providers to carry the channel, a strategy that allowed it to reach over 17 million homes by its launch date.

Notable Launch Programs:  Some of the early opinion shows included The O'Reilly Report, hosted by Bill O'Reilly, and Hannity & Colmes, hosted by Sean Hannity and Alan Colmes.

Early Success:  Although initially absent from major media markets like New York and Los Angeles, the network rapidly grew, and by 2002, it had surpassed CNN in ratings to become the top-rated cable news channel.

And 16 yrs earlier...

46years ago – CNN (Cable News Network) launched on Sunday, June 1, 1980 , in Atlanta, Georgia, founded by Ted Turner as the world's first 24-hour, all-news cable channel.

2）
death penalty case files at the bottom of a drawer and tell the families: "It’s still working its way through the process." In 2013, a military jury of thirteen officers unanimously convicted Hasan and unanimously recommended the death penalty. The charges included thirteen counts of premeditated murder and thirty-two counts of attempted premeditated murder. He offered almost no defense, called no witnesses, and denied nothing. What he wanted was for the event to be recorded as a statement of his convictions.
The state’s response to him was delayed for thirteen years.
Military law places the final key in the hands of the President.
The *Uniform Code of Military Justice* is explicit: a military death sentence cannot be carried out without the President's approval. This is not a mere formality; it is an exercise of command authority. The gun belongs to the state, and the verdict belongs to the state; the person who ultimately pulls the trigger—metaphorically speaking—must be the Commander-in-Chief.
In 2008, George W. Bush approved the execution of another military death-row inmate, Ronald Gray. Gray had been convicted of rape and murder, and the approved method was lethal injection. The date was set for December 10, 2008, but a federal judge halted the process on November 26. To this day, Gray remains on military death row at Leavenworth. Approval does not equate to execution; standing between the two are judges, appeals, the passage of time, and a lack of political will to shoulder the burden.
The last man hanged was Army Private John Bennett in 1961, convicted of raping and attempting to murder an eleven-year-old girl in Austria. Since then, the U.S. military’s gallows, firing squads, and lethal injection chambers have all sat idle. It was not for a lack of death-row inmates. It was because no president was willing to sign the order and turn that signature into reality.
What Trump signed this time was the authorization for an Army firing squad, as recommended by Hegseth. The Acting Secretary of the Army immediately locked in the time and place: December 3, Fort Hood, 1:00 PM. Parnell’s words were: "Judgment day has finally arrived." Hegseth’s word was: "Justice."
It is still possible for someone to rush into federal court, attempting to use a writ of habeas corpus to drag the date out by another decade. This must be acknowledged at the outset. Yet, the approval has been granted, the date announced, and the method selected. In sixty-five years, no other president has reached this stage.
Why a gun, and not a needle?
Three methods are commonly used for civilian executions: electrocution, gas, and lethal injection. Each is packaged as "humane." Tennessee recently provided a real-world example of this packaging. On September 30, 2026, the state was set to execute Christa Pike—a female death-row inmate who had murdered a classmate—via lethal injection. After two doses of pentobarbital were administered, she still had a heartbeat and continued to breathe and snore. The state government halted the execution and sent her to the hospital. Governor Bill Lee subsequently suspended the state's remaining executions and ordered an investigation. A state failed to kill a convicted murderer with two injections, only to then explain to the nation that there was nothing wrong with the procedure.
This is what the end of "humane execution" looks like: drugs, IV lines, protocols, lawyers, investigations, and suspensions. The victims' families wait outside while the killer snores inside.
Hasan does not deserve this ritual. The weapon he used to kill American soldiers was a gun. The words he shouted were a call to war. He confronted unarmed troops preparing to deploy. For the military to reclaim him in a military fashion is a matter of symmetry, not cruelty. A firing squad is not a lynch mob or a chaotic hail of bullets; it is a formal unit prescribed by regulation—involving orders, commands, a synchronized volley, and the presence of the State.

I appreciate your research. 

I agree that she and Tucker appear to be laying the groundwork to use the Safe Haven program to avoid accountability.  As you stated, Tucker has explicitly stated he expects criminal prosecution for unspecified reasons. So he has made his motivations clear. 

My question is:  Why would Candace need to leave the US?  

Just to recap - In the episode, you opine that the reason Candace may use Russia’s Safe Haven program to defect stems from the civil claims pending against her, that you believe she will like lose.  You stated that were she found civilly liable, her assets/property would be at risk.  You also stated she might be imprisoned.  Therefore, you think she’ll leave for Russia to protect her money and avoid prosecution for defaults on judgments. 

I think if this theory is accurate, that she is planning to leave, it’s related to something else.  

Seeking to understand what I consider serious red flags in terms of ideological contradictions, choices in terms of associations, etc I did some research. 

I focused on the timing of her Russia visit, and her seemingly impromptu visit to Italy.  Did she stay in Vatican City?  

Consider the  coincidental presence of Fuentes  in italy.  Add the peculiar and perhaps coincidental fact  that both  podcasters took the same weeks off in April & July.  

As to the April Italy trip, Candace deviated from her pattern and didn’t clearly announce in the days prior that her podcast wouldn’t air that Thursday.  IMO therefore it seemed to be either an impromptu/emergency visit or planned, but strategically unannounced. 

What was going on in the US political sphere during those two weeks ?  SPLC indictments were filed, the initial and the superseding.  Are there any dots to connect there?  Maybe not. IDK.  but Is Candace affiliated with anyone in the radius of SPLC, particularly a controversial person(s) or organization that sued the SPLC. Baron Coleman represented individuals in that area.  What if anything does this mean?  Perhaps nothing. Just random.  

So in this context my own research which has rendered no conclusions, I found your theory.  

I don’t understand the reasoning and basis for your theory as to WHY Candace would choose to leave the US for Russia.  

How would leaving the US legally shield her US based property from civil collections?  

Were she to move to Russia, a US court maintains jurisdiction over a default and collection process.  The US based properties, financial accounts, etc remain in the US.  The court can still order bank levies, garnishment.  Add to it, States like mine, Texas, do not allow creditors to execute exempt property - like a primary residence up to certain values.  

Moreover, given her status, Owens has likely implemented financial strategies to protect her separate assets and any Farmer assets in which she has an equitable or legal interest by marriage.  Trusts.  Entities.  All legal.  

It seems unlikely that a successful litigant would have civil collection remedies that could meaningfully jeopardize her wealth to a degree sufficient to warrant leaving the US for Russia . 

Do you have info to the contrary ?  

Also - It is my understanding that there is no US state that offers imprisonment as a remedy to address default on a civil judgment.   In fact, the opposite is federally codified and included in many state constitutions.

NVDA hit a record $243.37 Tuesday (five straight up days) but is off ~0.7% premarket as the 30-year yield hits 5.70%, its highest since 2002.

🔌 Marvell $MRVL just told the Street custom silicon is way bigger than it thinks

At Tuesday's investor day it raised its FY28 revenue target to ~$20B (vs ~$18.2B consensus), framed FY31 at $70–90B with EPS above $30, and lifted its 2029 custom-chip goal from $10B to more than $12B. It also sees optical interconnects growing 60–70% a year to ~$65B through 2030. MRVL closed +5.81% at $287.01 after being up ~10% intraday, Broadcom $AVGO rose ~4% in sympathy, and Ciena $CIEN ripped +13.85% to $443.65 since that optical outlook blows past its own ~30% framework.

🪧 Micron $MU workers in Taiwan just won the right to strike

The Taoyuan union says 1,994 of 2,012 voting members backed a strike. No date is set, but leaders say a "surprise strike" could be called by text. They want 15% of operating profit paid out as quarterly bonuses plus an 83-month one-off bonus, after rejecting Micron's offer of up to 68 months. Micron's board meets Oct 8–9 and the Taichung union's next mediation is Oct 22. Taiwan is a key DRAM and HBM hub, and MU is down ~3% premarket, on track for a fourth straight red day.

🏭 Musk says TSMC $TSM won't own or run Terafab, and Intel $INTC is bouncing

Tesla $TSLA and SpaceX will build and operate the Texas fab themselves, with TSMC at most subleasing part of the site. Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg Intel's Terafab partnership is intact, Intel and Applied Materials $AMAT are teaming up on next-gen transistors, interconnects, and advanced packaging, and Mizuho raised its INTC target to $114 from $92 (still Neutral). INTC dropped 3.18% Tuesday and is up ~0.4–1% premarket near $113.

🎮 Google $GOOGL and Unity $U want anyone to build games from a text prompt

Google launched Playground, an experimental platform (18+) that makes playable games from natural language, and later this year the two will ship Unity Spark with high-fidelity 3D and the Unity runtime. Creations plug into Google Play Games profiles with leaderboards and multiplayer matchmaking, and Google will showcase picks across its network. Unity jumped ~5% while Roblox $RBLX fell 7.8% on the new competition.
