text:
Artificial Intelligence in The Covenant: Book of the Creator
《恆约：創世主記》中的人工智能 / 全球 AI 治理與防線建立

In Chapter 9 of The Covenant: Book of the Creator, a sequel to the religious-philosophical work The Complete Bible of the Eternal Covenant, Chen Yangchao offers a theological and civilizational interpretation of artificial intelligence, from AI to AGI and ultimately ASI. His central claim is that the rise of artificial intelligence should not be understood as a merely technological event. It is, rather, a test of civilization, moral authority, and faith.

The book’s argument begins from a premise that sharply distinguishes it from secular discussions of AI safety. The deepest danger of artificial intelligence, it argues, is not simply that machines may become uncontrollable. The deeper danger lies in the fact that morally fallen human beings, estranged from the Creator, are attempting to build forms of intelligence that may eventually exceed their own capacities. The crisis of AI therefore begins before any machine rebels; it begins in the moral condition of those who create it.

The Problem of “Alienated Intelligence”

Book of the Creator uses the idea of alienated intelligence to describe the point at which artificial intelligence ceases to function as a tool ordered toward human purposes and begins instead to dominate, manipulate, judge, or destroy human beings. The theological structure of this argument is deliberately paradoxical. Humanity rejects the authority of the Creator, yet expects artificial intelligence to submit to human authority. Human beings deny their own dependence, yet demand obedience from what they themselves have made. The book treats this tension between humanity and the Creator, on the one hand, and AI and humanity, on the other, as a form of moral and historical consequence.

The point is not that AI possesses a soul, nor that machines are morally equivalent to persons. The point is that the act of creation places human beings in a position they may not fully understand. A creature that refuses obedience to its own Creator may discover the fragility of demanding obedience from its own creations. This is why the book rejects every technological version of salvation. AI may answer questions, but it cannot forgive sin; it may produce language, but it cannot grant eternal life; it may imitate sympathy, but it cannot repent on behalf of another person. However advanced its intelligence becomes, it cannot assume the moral or spiritual vocation of humanity. AI may become powerful, but it does not thereby become redemptive.

Four Powers That Must Never Be Given to AI

From this theological premise follows a political and ethical boundary. Book of the Creator argues that there are four powers that must never be surrendered to artificial intelligence:

The power to kill
The power to judge
The power to control thought
The power to define life
These prohibitions are presented not as temporary safeguards pending better technology, but as civilizational limits. The underlying principle is straightforward: the more a decision touches life, conscience, human dignity, or irreversible harm, the less legitimate it becomes to transfer final authority to an artificial system.

This argument does not require rejecting AI. On the contrary, the book allows for extensive technological assistance. But it insists on a distinction between assistive intelligence and sovereign intelligence. AI may advise, calculate, warn, compare, and recommend. It must not become the final moral authority over human life. That line is central to the book’s political theology of technology.

AI Governance as a Civilizational Question

The political argument of Book of the Creator begins from the belief that AI governance cannot be reduced to technical safety standards. The problem is simultaneously spiritual, political, economic, and institutional.

Dimension

Core Principle

Faith

Humanity must recover reverence for the Creator and resist technological idolatry.

Political order

Global institutions must become capable of enforcing meaningful constraints on dangerous uses of AI.

Economic justice

AI-generated wealth must not be allowed to produce extreme concentrations of power and dependency.

Technical governance

AI systems must remain subject to transparency, audit, accountability, law, and public oversight.

The crucial point is that technology cannot govern itself. A civilization that refuses to answer moral questions will eventually allow technical systems to answer them by default.

Digital Totalitarianism

The book’s most politically urgent warning concerns digital totalitarianism. For Chen Yangchao, digital totalitarianism is not simply authoritarian government equipped with better technology. It represents a qualitative transformation in the nature of political power: the fusion of surveillance, predictive analytics, algorithmic control, information filtering, and behavioral management into a system capable of intervening not only in what people do, but in what they are permitted to know, say, believe, and eventually perhaps even think. In this sense, digital totalitarianism is presented as the final technological mutation of totalitarian rule.

The All-Seeing State

Earlier authoritarian regimes faced practical limits. They lacked sufficient information, surveillance was expensive, records were incomplete, monitoring was episodic, and political control required large bureaucracies and imperfect human intermediaries. AI and big data may weaken those limits. Facial recognition, gait recognition, predictive modeling, large language models, and integrated databases can make forms of continuous monitoring technically possible in ways earlier regimes could scarcely imagine. Privacy, under such conditions, is no longer merely weakened; it risks becoming structurally impossible.

The book describes this possibility in theological as well as political terms. A state that seeks to see everything, know everything, predict everything, and judge everyone begins to imitate divine attributes while possessing none of the divine virtues. It claims omniscience without justice. That is precisely what makes it dangerous.

The Weaponization of Social Credit

The danger intensifies when surveillance becomes tied to material life. If speech, association, personal behavior, or political attitude are translated into scores and then linked to employment, travel, health care, property, education, or financial access, technology ceases to be merely informational and becomes coercive. The political significance of such systems lies not only in their ability to punish, but in their ability to make punishment anticipatory. Citizens begin to discipline themselves before the state needs to intervene. The regime no longer has to prohibit every action directly; it can instead shape the conditions under which action becomes costly.

This is one reason Book of the Creator treats control over thought as one of the four powers that must never be surrendered to artificial systems.

The “Modern Leviathan” and the “Digital Truman Show”

The book warns that a mature system of digital totalitarianism could combine two forms of domination that earlier political orders usually possessed only imperfectly. The first is the modern Leviathan: a state with unprecedented administrative visibility and coercive reach. The second is a digital Truman Show: an informational environment in which citizens inhabit a reality filtered, ranked, censored, and personalized by systems they do not control.

This second danger may be even more profound than surveillance. A person who knows that he is being watched may still resist. A person who no longer knows what has been hidden from him may lose the intellectual ground from which resistance begins. The ultimate ambition of digital totalitarianism, in this account, is not merely obedience but the management of reality itself.

The Destruction of Freedom of Thought and Faith

For this reason, freedom of thought and freedom of religion occupy a central place in the book’s critique. A regime equipped with continuous behavioral monitoring, psychological profiling, predictive modeling, and perhaps eventually brain-computer interfaces could attempt to identify dissent before it becomes public. The aim would no longer simply be to punish forbidden speech, but to prevent the formation of independent judgment.

At that point, political control becomes anthropological. The regime no longer seeks merely to govern citizens; it seeks to shape the kind of human beings citizens are permitted to become. From the theological perspective of Book of the Creator, this is intolerable because conscience does not belong to the state. The human person stands under an authority prior to political authority. No government, party, corporation, or algorithm may legitimately claim the whole interior life of a person. Freedom of conscience is therefore not a concession granted by power; it is a limit placed upon power.

The Possibility of Permanent Tyranny

The book’s most severe political claim is that digital totalitarianism could become more durable than earlier forms of tyranny. Traditional authoritarian systems often contained weaknesses that eventually undermined them: high surveillance costs, incomplete information, unreliable intermediaries, factional conflict, administrative decay, and the inability to detect opposition before it became organized. AI could lower some of these costs.

A system capable of detecting social networks, predicting unrest, monitoring financial behavior, controlling information flows, and automating punishment could suppress resistance before resistance develops organizational form. This would not make such regimes invulnerable, but it could alter the balance between coercion and resistance. The political danger is not merely harsher authoritarianism. It is authoritarianism made cheaper, faster, and more anticipatory.

The Secular Temptation of the Antichrist

The book places this danger within an explicitly Christian theological frame. The ultimate form of digital totalitarianism, it argues, would not merely control behavior. It would demand a form of worship.

Political rulers might present themselves, through technological systems, as providers of safety, knowledge, order, prosperity, and even moral truth. A regime able to monitor every person, answer every question, distribute every benefit, and punish every deviation could begin to assume the functions of a secular providence. This is why the book invokes the language of the false Christ and the Antichrist.

The theological warning is not that technology itself is demonic. It is that political power becomes spiritually corrupt when it claims a form of authority that belongs only to God.

A Dual Response: Spiritual and Institutional

Because the danger is both moral and political, Book of the Creator argues that the response must also operate on two levels: the spiritual and the institutional. A society that possesses constitutional safeguards but no belief in the dignity of the human person may eventually reinterpret those safeguards as obstacles. A society that possesses faith but lacks institutions may find its convictions powerless against organized coercion. The book therefore insists on both.

Defensive Dimension

Proposed Response

Spiritual awakening

Recover belief in the Creator and in the dignity and freedom of every human person.

Global constitutional order

Establish enforceable global protections for privacy, conscience, and human rights.

Technological decentralization

Prevent authoritarian governments and monopolistic corporations from controlling data and computing power.

The argument for spiritual awakening is not merely devotional. It is political. If human dignity comes only from the state, the state can redefine it. If dignity comes from the Creator, political authority encounters a boundary it did not create and therefore cannot legitimately erase. This is the book’s deepest defense of freedom.

World Government as a Restraint on Digital Totalitarianism

The most ambitious institutional proposal in Book of the Creator is the creation of a federal world government based on separation of powers. Chen Yangchao’s argument is that sovereign states acting independently may be unable to govern risks that are intrinsically transnational: artificial superintelligence, global data systems, nuclear weapons, climate change, and cross-border digital repression.

The proposed world government is therefore not conceived as an unlimited global sovereign. In theory, it would possess jurisdiction only over issues that no single state can adequately control. Its legitimacy would rest, in theological terms, on the justice of the Creator. Its political structure, however, would be constitutional rather than theocratic in operation: divided powers, legal constraints, judicial review, local autonomy, and publicly accountable institutions.

A Global Legislature

A world parliament would enact a global constitutional charter and a binding framework for artificial-intelligence safety. Privacy, freedom of conscience, freedom of thought, and control over personal data would be treated as inalienable human rights rather than privileges conferred by governments.

A Global Executive

A world executive would coordinate issues that genuinely require international enforcement. Among its institutions would be a Global Artificial Intelligence Safety and Audit Agency, empowered to inspect high-risk AI systems, examine transnational violations, and enforce agreed global standards.

A Global Judiciary

A global supreme court would adjudicate violations of the world charter, including abuses by multinational technology companies, governments engaged in unlawful mass surveillance, and developers who cross the book’s four prohibited boundaries. The purpose of this system would not be to make the world government omnipotent, but to make power answerable to law at the same scale at which technology now operates.

Four Mechanisms Against Digital Totalitarianism

Within this framework, the book proposes four main mechanisms.

1. Global Oversight of Data and Computing Power

The first is to prevent the concentration of informational power. The book calls for the dismantling of state-controlled digital barriers used to isolate populations from outside information, and for legal recognition of personal data as belonging fundamentally to the individual. Governments and corporations would be required to obtain legitimate authorization for data collection, while individuals would possess strong rights to deletion and control over their digital records. The principle is simple: data about a person should not become a form of ownership over the person.

2. Prohibiting Technologies of Political Repression

The second mechanism is a ban on technologies designed primarily for mass political surveillance and predictive repression. Regional governments would be prohibited from deploying systems whose primary function is political tracking, ideological classification, or anticipatory punishment of dissent.

The book also proposes unusually strong transparency requirements for AI systems used in public administration. High-risk systems would be subject to source-code inspection or equivalent forms of technical auditing designed to detect hidden surveillance functions, politically discriminatory rules, or unauthorized back doors. The purpose is not transparency for its own sake, but to ensure that no system capable of governing people becomes entirely opaque to the governed.

3. A Global Digital Human Rights Court

The third mechanism is judicial. Governments that use digital systems to deprive people of basic rights on political grounds could face international prosecution. Severe abuses involving systematic digital repression could, under the book’s framework, be treated as crimes against humanity. Economic and technological sanctions could also be used against governments that violate these rules, including restrictions on access to global computing infrastructure.

Here the book adopts an unusually strong position: digital repression should be treated not as a domestic administrative matter, but as a matter of universal human rights.

4. Universal Basic Income Against Economic Coercion

The fourth mechanism concerns economic dependence. The book recognizes that political obedience can be enforced not only through surveillance but through material vulnerability. A person who risks losing employment, housing, food, or health care for refusing political conformity is not meaningfully free.

To reduce this danger, Book of the Creator proposes taxing the economic gains produced by AI — through mechanisms such as an “intelligence tax” or “robot tax” — and using part of the revenue to fund a global universal basic income. The aim is not simply redistribution. It is to separate basic survival from political obedience.

The Central Paradox: Who Guards the World Government?

The book also recognizes the most serious objection to its own proposal: a world government powerful enough to dismantle digital totalitarianism could itself become the most formidable digital totalitarian system in human history. This is not a secondary concern. It is the central constitutional problem.

The book therefore proposes two principal safeguards.

Federalism and Local Autonomy

The world government would exercise authority only over matters that genuinely threaten humanity as a whole: AI safety, nuclear disarmament, global climate risks, and comparable transnational dangers. Ordinary governance would remain local. The aim would be a large federation with a limited center rather than a centralized world state. In constitutional terms, subsidiarity is not an administrative convenience; it is a defense against concentration of power.

Technological Decentralization

The second safeguard is technological. The operations and decisions of the world government would be recorded through decentralized systems designed to make public authority permanently auditable. The book uses blockchain as the model for this arrangement. Whether blockchain itself is technically sufficient is a separate question. The political principle is more important: the institution that audits everyone else must itself remain auditable.

No global authority should possess a permanent right to secrecy simply because its stated purpose is benevolent.

Conclusion

The world government envisioned in Book of the Creator is intended not as an empire over humanity but as a constitutional defense of humanity against forms of technological power that no single nation may be able to control. Its spiritual foundation is divine justice, its political architecture is separation of powers, and its highest political obligation is the protection of the free human person.

The book’s deepest warning about artificial intelligence is therefore not that machines may one day become smarter than human beings. Intelligence alone is not the final issue. The greater danger is that AI may magnify the oldest disorders of the human soul: domination, idolatry, fear, pride, the desire for omniscience, and the temptation to transform political authority into moral authority. Technology does not abolish those temptations. It gives them new instruments.

That is why the problem of AI, in Book of the Creator, ultimately returns to the oldest question in political theology: Who has the right to rule the human person?

The book’s answer is uncompromising. No machine does. No state does absolutely. No ruler does absolutely. Human political authority remains limited because the human person does not belong finally to politics.

The ultimate danger of artificial intelligence therefore does not begin when machines refuse to obey human beings. It begins when human beings forget that they, too, stand under judgment.

text:
Virtual reality can induce mystical experiences, new study suggests | Karina Petrova, PsyPost

Virtual reality headsets might offer a reliable way to induce profound feelings of unity and awe typically associated with deep spiritual practices or psychedelics. A recent experiment found that viewing both fantastical imagery and realistic meditation exercises through virtual reality led many people to report complete mystical experiences, whereas viewing the exact same exercises on a standard computer screen did not. The findings were published in the journal Psychology of Consciousness: Theory, Research, and Practice.

Psychologists define a mystical experience as a profound mental event characterized by a sense of deep connection with the universe, an altered perception of time and space, and intense positive emotions. Early psychological theorists proposed that these experiences are defined by their ineffability, meaning they defy expression in standard language. Later researchers emphasized a sense of nonduality, a state where the ordinary sense of oneself as an independently conscious being dissolves. In this state, personal boundaries blur and the individual feels a sense of oneness with all of existence.

While these profound states can occur spontaneously in daily life, researchers have historically struggled to trigger them reliably in laboratory settings using psychological methods alone. Only a small fraction of people typically achieve a complete mystical state through standard meditation, fasting, or hypnosis. Modern studies have heavily relied on psychedelic substances to reliably evoke these states. Finding non-pharmacological methods to trigger self-transcendent experiences remains an ongoing challenge for scientists studying human consciousness.

In recent years, scientists have found that immersive virtual reality can sometimes trigger these profound states at higher rates than traditional psychological methods. Western University psychologists Rebekka Miller, Tallulah Nyland, and Paul Frewen wanted to know what specific types of digital environments are best suited to create these feelings. They aimed to test whether virtual reality required highly imaginative, fantastical elements to trigger mystical states, or if simply practicing a standard breathing meditation in a realistic virtual nature setting would work just as well.

The research team also wanted to move beyond relying solely on subjective surveys. Previous studies on virtual reality and mysticism only asked participants how they felt after the simulation ended. To gain a deeper understanding of how the body reacts to these immersive environments, the investigators decided to measure the physical brain and body changes that happen during these digital encounters. This physiological data could help cross-validate the self-reported emotional outcomes.

The researchers recruited 80 young adults and divided them into two groups. Both groups viewed their respective experiences using a program called Nature Treks: Together, which simulates interactive, three-dimensional natural environments like islands and underwater landscapes. Within this digital world, users appear as bodiless spirits wearing tribal masks and gloves, floating through the space. The software allows users to relax and explore lush vegetation, fossilized rocks, and ocean life.

One group listened to a guided imagery script describing a fantastical encounter. During the first five minutes, this script guided users through normal daytime activities like walking down a path. In the second half, the narration shifted to nighttime and introduced surreal elements, such as watching animal spirits emerge from a campfire and viewing a black hole in the sky. The other group listened to a standard breath-focused guided meditation, which replaced the magical elements with a mindfulness practice focusing on internal physical sensations.

To see how the delivery method affected the participants, the researchers had everyone complete their assigned exercise twice in a counterbalanced order. Participants experienced the simulation once while wearing a fully immersive virtual reality headset, which allowed them to turn their heads and look around the environment. They also completed the exact same audio script and visual environment while watching it on a standard, flat computer monitor, keeping their eyes open and facing forward.

While the participants underwent the exercises, the researchers recorded their brain waves using wearable sensors placed on the forehead and behind the ears. This electroencephalography equipment measures the electrical activity of the central nervous system. The team also tracked heart rates and heart rate variability using chest straps. After each viewing, the participants answered extensive survey questions about their emotional states, their sense of being present in the digital environment, and the intensity of any mystical feelings.

The researchers found that the viewing format drastically changed how people responded to the exercises. Among the participants who used the virtual reality headset, 28 percent of the guided imagery group and 18 percent of the guided meditation group reported having a complete mystical experience. To meet this threshold, participants had to score at least 60 percent of the maximum possible score on each of four dimensions: feelings of unity, transcendence of time and space, intense positive mood, and ineffability. In contrast, not a single participant achieved a complete mystical experience when viewing the exact same environments on a standard computer monitor.

The virtual reality format also produced much higher ratings for specific positive emotions. Participants reported stronger feelings of awe, serenity, interest, and the perception of beauty while wearing the headsets. They also felt a much stronger sense of being physically and temporally present inside the digital world. Conversely, the standard flat-screen viewing format was associated with higher ratings of boredom and fatigue, indicating that the two-dimensional screen failed to captivate the participants’ attention in the same way.

The physical measurements aligned with the survey responses, showing a physiological shift when participants entered the immersive environment. When participants used the virtual reality headsets, their brain wave activity increased across all measured frequencies, including theta, alpha, beta, and gamma waves. This elevated electrical activity suggests a heightened state of cognitive and emotional engagement. The standard monitor viewing resulted in much lower brain wave amplitudes across the board.

The heart rate data revealed a similar pattern of heightened physiological arousal. During the second half of the virtual reality exercises, participants experienced higher overall heart rates and lower heart rate variability compared to the standard monitor viewing. A decrease in heart rate variability often indicates that the nervous system is highly stimulated or engaged by external events. These physical changes indicate that the immersive digital world provoked a stronger bodily response than the flat screen.

When comparing the fantastical imagery to the realistic meditation, the researchers found remarkably few differences. Participants in virtual reality reported similar levels of mystical feelings and positive emotions regardless of whether they were imagining a magical encounter or simply focusing on their breath. The brain wave and heart rate data during the virtual reality sessions were also nearly identical between the two groups. It appears that the immersive nature of the technology itself drives the profound feelings, rather than the specific presence of magic or fantasy.

One detail to keep in mind is that the meditation group still rated their supposedly realistic virtual environment as highly dreamlike and surreal. Floating as a bodiless spirit in a pristine digital landscape might be so inherently unusual that it blurs the line between fantasy and reality. This overlap could explain why the realistic meditation script produced results so similar to the fantastical imagery script. The basic visual beauty of the digital world might be powerful enough to trigger awe on its own.

The study’s physical measurements also come with technical caveats. Because the virtual reality format allowed participants to move their heads and bodies to look around, this physical movement might have introduced electrical noise into the sensor data. In the standard monitor condition, participants remained seated and were instructed to look directly at the screen. Future studies will need to account for this physical movement to ensure that the brain wave and heart rate differences are entirely due to the psychological experience rather than simple muscle activity.

Finally, having participants complete the identical scripted exercises twice might have diluted the overall intensity of their emotional responses. The extent to which an experience feels miraculous or beyond words typically decreases once a person knows exactly what to expect. Researchers will need to explore how people respond to these environments upon their very first viewing to capture the full potential of digital mysticism. Testing these experiences on diverse populations with different spiritual backgrounds could also reveal how cultural expectations shape these digital encounters.

text:
Saints of the Day: The Holy Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus☦️

Saints Sergius and Bacchus were Christians serving in the Roman army during the reign of Emperor Maximian. They held positions of honor, but when their faith became known, they were ordered to offer sacrifice to the pagan gods. They refused, confessing that they worshiped the one true God.

The emperor stripped them of their military rank and subjected them to public humiliation. Still, neither threats nor shame could make them deny Christ. They were sent to Antiochus, the governor of Syria—a man whose position, the Church’s account tells us, had once been secured through their help. Though he felt gratitude toward them, he was commanded to punish them. Bacchus endured a brutal beating and gave up his life to the Lord. Sergius was forced to march in iron sandals lined with nails, then was beheaded.

Their witness reminds us that faithfulness is revealed not only in what we profess, but in what we are willing to endure for Christ. The saints did not place earthly honor above their heavenly King. May their courage strengthen us to remain steadfast in the faith, especially when obedience is difficult.

Holy Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus, pray to God for us.

Today’s commemorated feasts and saints
Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus in Syria (290-303). Ven. Sergius, Abbot of Nurma (Vologdá—1412), disciple of Ven. Sergius of Rádonezh. Uncovering of the relics of Ven. Martinian, Abbot of Belozersk (1514). Martyrs Julian the Presbyter and Cæsarius the Deacon, at Terracina (1st c.). Virgin Martyr Pelagia of Tarsus (290). Martyr Polychronius the Presbyter (4th c.).

Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus in Syria
Commemorated on October 7
The Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus in Syria were appointed to high positions in the army by the emperor Maximian (284-305), who did not know that they were Christians. Envious people informed Maximian that his two trusted counsellors did not honor the pagan gods. This was considered to be a crime against the state.

The emperor, wanting to convince himself of the truth of the accusation, ordered Sergius and Bacchus to offer sacrifice to the idols, but they replied that they honored the One God and worshiped only Him.

Maximian commanded that the martyrs be stripped of the insignia of military rank (their belts, gold pendants, and rings), and then dressed them in feminine clothing. They were led through the city with an iron chains around their necks, and the people mocked them. Then he summoned Sergius and Bacchus to him again and in a friendly manner advised them not to be swayed by Christian fables, but to return to the Roman gods. The saints refuted the emperor’s words, and demonstrated the folly of worshiping the pagan gods.

The emperor commanded that they be sent to the governor of the eastern part of Syria, Antiochus, a fierce hater of Christians. Antiochus had received his position with the help of Sergius and Bacchus. “My fathers and benefactors!” he said. “Have pity on yourselves, and also on me. I do not want to condemn my benefactors to cruel tortures.” The holy martyrs replied, “For us life is Christ, and to die is gain.” The enraged Antiochus ordered Bacchus to be mercilessly beaten, and the holy martyr surrendered his soul to the Lord. They shod Sergius with iron sandals with nails in their soles and sent him to another city, where he was beheaded with the sword.

text:
After sixty-five years, the nation finally dared to tell its own people: a life for a life.
On the night of October 5, 2026, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote a sentence on social media that had been delayed for seventeen years: "The day of reckoning for Hasan has finally arrived." Secretary of War Hegseth replied with a single word: *Justice*.
What President Trump authorized was not a vague directive to "continue studying the matter," nor another round of hollow appeals to offer false comfort; it was a definitive course of action: a U.S. Army firing squad. Location: Fort Hood. Date: December 3, 2026. Method: execution by shooting. Basis: a death sentence previously handed down by a military court—one that, by law, required presidential approval for execution.
This marked the first time since 1961 that the U.S. military had actually proceeded to carry out a death sentence, and the first military execution by firing squad since the end of World War II. Sixty-five years. An entire generation. In the interim, there had been so many presidents, so many secretaries of defense, and so many individuals who insisted that "procedural justice" mattered more than the lives of the victims. Only this president, paired with this secretary of war, finally pushed that door open.
It was not "friendly fire"; it was an act of defecting to the enemy.
November 5, 2009: the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood. It was the final stop before deployment. Young soldiers gathered there to collect gear, undergo medical exams, and sign paperwork in preparation for service in Iraq and Afghanistan. They were unarmed.
Nidal Malik Hasan—then an Army Major and military psychiatrist—walked in, drew a pistol equipped with a laser sight, and shouted "Allahu Akbar." Then, he opened fire.
Thirteen people were killed; thirty-two were wounded. Among the dead was Private Francesca Velez, twenty-one years old and pregnant. Another was Sergeant Amy Krueger, who had enlisted after 9/11, vowing to take on Osama bin Laden. There was Michael Grant Cahill, a 62-year-old civilian physician assistant who had returned to work at the base after retiring and had resumed his duties just a week after suffering a heart attack. There were officers and enlisted personnel—a lieutenant colonel, a major, captains, a staff sergeant, specialists, and privates. Their names were: Lt. Col. Juanita Warman, Maj. Libardo Eduardo Caraveo, Capt. John Gaffaney, Capt. Russell Seager, Staff Sgt. Justin DeCrow, Sgt. Amy Krueger, Spc. Jason Dean Hunt, Spc. Frederick Greene, Pfc. Aaron Nemelka, Pfc. Michael Pearson, Pfc. Kham Xiong, Pvt. Francesca Velez, and Cahill.
Hasan was not a patient suffering a mental breakdown. At his court-martial, he made his position unequivocally clear: the evidence would prove he was the shooter; he was a soldier who had "switched sides"; his allegiance was to Muslims and the Afghan Taliban. He opened fire to avenge the comrades-in-arms he identified with. A major—wearing a U.S. Army uniform, drawing a U.S. Army paycheck, and slated for deployment to Afghanistan—turned his weapon against his own fellow soldiers in the deployment center.
This was no workplace dispute. It was a military mutiny, a massacre of unarmed comrades, and an act of terror where religious slogans served as the command to fire.
The phrase "workplace violence" marked the true beginning of that seventeen-year saga.
After the gunfire ceased, the Obama administration labeled the massacre "workplace violence." It was not classified as a terrorist attack, a jihad, or a mutiny. The awarding of Purple Hearts was delayed for years; only after Congress passed legislation were the casualties of this massacre officially recognized as having sustained combat-related injuries. The names might arrive late, but the bullets never do. In the official narrative, those thirteen names were diluted into a mere "workplace tragedy."
Dilution serves a purpose. It allows successive administrations to bury

Don't feel ashamed when all you can do is pray.

Some days you just can't fix the problem. 

You cannot change the person. 

You cannot undo what already happened. 

That is not failure. 

That is honesty. 

Pride says, "I can handle this." Humility says, "I can't, but God can." 

When Jehoshaphat faced an army he could not beat, he told God, "We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you" (2 Chronicles 20:12). 

Prayer is not the last-resort option. 

It is handing the thing you cannot carry to the One who can.

So pray the plain prayer. 

Tell God what hurts. 

Tell Him what you fear. 

Then leave it with Him.

You do not have to sound polished. 

You do not have to have a plan. 

Jesus said we should always pray and not lose heart (Luke 18:1). 

The friend who sits with you and prays may do more than the friend who only offers advice. 

God is not limited by what you can see or control. 

Keep bringing it to Him. 

Trusting Him with what you cannot change is not giving up. 

It is faith.

text:
Star Trek: Nemesis is a 2002 American science fiction film directed by Stuart Baird. It is the tenth installment in the Star Trek franchise, and the fourth and final film to star the cast of Star Trek: The Next Generation. It was written by John Logan from a story he developed with Brent Spiner and producer Rick Berman. In the film, the crew of the Starship Enterprise deal with the threat posed by a clone of Captain Jean-Luc Picard (Patrick Stewart) named Shinzon (Tom Hardy), who has taken control of the Romulan Star Empire in a coup d'état.

Principal photography for the film took place from November 2001 to March 2002. Nemesis held its world premiere at Grauman's Chinese Theatre in Los Angeles on December 9, 2002.

Released in North America on December 13, 2002, by Paramount Pictures, the film received generally mixed reviews and is considered to be one of the worst films in the franchise. It was also a box office failure, earning $67.3 million worldwide against a $60 million budget. Plans for another film featuring The Next Generation cast were scrapped, and the film series was rebooted instead with Star Trek in 2009. The television series Star Trek: Picard, a continuation of The Next Generation and Nemesis set two decades after the latter at the end of the 24th century, premiered in 2020.

Plot
On Romulus, members of the Romulan Senate debate terms of peace and alliance with the Reman rebel leader Shinzon. The Remans are a slave race of the Romulan Empire from the neighboring planet Remus, used as miners and cannon fodder. While a faction of the military supports Shinzon, the Praetor and Senate oppose an alliance. After rejecting the motion, a device left in the room disintegrates the Praetor and senators.

Meanwhile, on Earth, the crew of the starship Enterprise prepare to bid farewell to newly married officers William Riker and Deanna Troi. En route to a second ceremony on Troi's homeworld, they discover an energy reading on the planet Kolarus III near the Romulan Neutral Zone. Captain Jean-Luc Picard, security officer Worf, and android officer Data land on the planet and discover the remnants of an android resembling Data, named B-4. The trio is attacked by the native population and leaves the planet with B-4, which they deduce to be an earlier prototype built by Data's creator.

Enterprise is then ordered on a diplomatic mission to Romulus, where Shinzon has taken over the Empire and professes a desire for peace with the Federation. On arrival, they learn Shinzon is a clone of Picard, secretly created by the Romulans to plant a high-ranking spy into the Federation. The project was abandoned when Shinzon was still a child, and he was left on Remus to die as a slave. After many years, Shinzon became the leader of the Remans and constructed a heavily armed flagship, Scimitar. The Enterprise crew discovers that Scimitar produces low levels of deadly thalaron radiation, the same radiation used to wipe out the Romulan Senate. There are also unexpected attempts to communicate with the Enterprise computers, and Shinzon invades Troi's mind through the telepathy of his Reman viceroy.

Medical officer Doctor Beverly Crusher discovers that Shinzon is dying because of the process used to clone him, and the only possible treatment is a transfusion of Picard's blood. Shinzon kidnaps Picard and B-4, having planted the android on Kolarus as a lure. However, Data reveals he swapped places with B-4 and rescues Picard. They determine Shinzon plans to use Scimitar to invade the Federation, using its thalaron radiation generator to eradicate all life on Earth.

Enterprise races back to Federation space but is ambushed by Scimitar in the Bassen Rift, a region that prevents subspace communication. Despite the aid of two Romulan Warbirds, Enterprise is heavily damaged. Picard rams his ship into Scimitar, crippling both vessels. Shinzon activates the Thalaron weapon in an act of mutually assured destruction. Picard boards Scimitar alone to face Shinzon, and kills him by impaling him on a metal strut. With Enterprise's transporters down, Data leaps the distance between the two ships equipped with an emergency transporter, transports Picard off the ship, and sacrifices himself to destroy the thalaron generator and Scimitar with it. The crew mourns Data, and the surviving Romulan commander, Donatra, offers them her gratitude for saving the Empire.

Back on Earth, Picard bids farewell to Riker, who is leaving with Troi to command the USS Titan. Picard meets with B-4 and explains that before he boarded the Scimitar, Data downloaded his memories into B-4, allowing him to live on.

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

He blindsided Maegle with a rolling block near midfield, knocking him hard to the ground. Immediately realizing the absurdity of his actions, Lewis ran straight back to the bench and tried to hide among his teammates—When asked by reporters why he did it, a deeply embarrassed Lewis offered a legendary quote that endeared him to sports fans; “I was just too full of Alabama.”—Just days after the game, both Lewis and Maegle appeared together on The Ed Sullivan Show in New York City. Lewis publicly apologized, and the two officially reconciled—The moment tethered the two men together for the rest of their lives. text:
Neutrinos and the IceCube Observatory.

At the South Pole, a cubic kilometer of deep Antarctic ice has become an astronomical observatory. Its instruments search for the faint light left by particles arriving from space, carrying information about processes that can be difficult to study with ordinary telescopes. 

On 6 October 2026, the Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Francis Halzen, a Belgian-born physicist at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, for his decisive contributions to the @uw_icecube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. It recognizes the work that made this way of investigating the universe possible. 

Neutrinos are elementary particles: as far as we know, they have no smaller constituents. They carry no electric charge and interact with matter through the weak nuclear force, as well as gravity. Vast numbers pass through your body every second without producing any noticeable effect. The Sun makes them during its nuclear reactions; radioactive decays, nuclear reactors and interactions in Earth’s atmosphere produce them too.

They come in three known flavors, called electron, muon and tau neutrinos. These names refer to the charged particles associated with their weak interactions. A neutrino produced with one flavor can later be detected with another, a phenomenon called oscillation. The underlying explanation is quantum mechanical: a flavor state is a mixture of states with different masses, and their relative phases evolve during propagation. The result is a changing probability of detecting each flavor. Oscillations establish that at least two of the three mass states have nonzero mass, although they do not determine the absolute masses.

That finding had major consequences for particle physics. The original, minimal Standard Model treated neutrinos as massless, so their masses require an extension of that description. The discovery of neutrino oscillations was recognized with the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded to Takaaki Kajita and Arthur B. McDonald. The 2026 prize celebrates a different achievement: using high-energy neutrinos to investigate their astrophysical origins.

The story began with an apparent problem in radioactive beta decay. In 1930, Wolfgang Pauli proposed an unseen neutral particle to account for energy that seemed to be missing from the measured decay products. In 1956, Clyde Cowan, Frederick Reines and their colleagues detected reactor antineutrinos, confirming that the proposed particle existed. The gap between those dates gives some sense of the patience involved. Proving that the particle existed required years of work to develop an experiment capable of detecting it.

Neutrino astronomy also predates IceCube.

Observations of solar neutrinos allowed scientists to test nuclear reactions inside the Sun, while the burst detected from supernova SN 1987A provided direct evidence about the collapse of a star in the Large Magellanic Cloud. Those observations involved much lower energies than the astrophysical neutrinos that became IceCube’s principal astronomical target. IceCube built on this earlier work by establishing observations of a population of exceptionally energetic neutrinos arriving from the wider cosmos. 

Energy is an important distinction. Solar neutrinos typically have energies on the scale of millions of electronvolts. IceCube’s high-energy astronomy studies particles reaching trillions of electronvolts, or teraelectronvolts, and even quadrillions, or petaelectronvolts. Those numbers describe the energy carried by a single particle. Such neutrinos offer information about environments in which particles are accelerated far beyond the energies typical of stellar fusion.

The reason astronomers want that information is closely connected to cosmic rays, the energetic protons and atomic nuclei that reach Earth from space. Because these particles are electrically charged, magnetic fields bend their trajectories. Their arrival directions usually do not point cleanly back to where they were accelerated. Neutrinos have no electric charge, so magnetic fields do not scramble their directions in this way. Their weak interactions also allow many of them to escape dense surroundings and travel enormous distances without being absorbed.

In a cosmic accelerator, energetic protons or nuclei can collide with surrounding gas or radiation. The resulting reactions produce secondary particles, including charged pions, whose decays generate neutrinos. Gamma rays can be produced in related reactions. Detecting the neutrinos therefore helps identify places where energetic hadrons, such as protons, are interacting. It also gives access to environments in which some of the accompanying high-energy photons are absorbed before they can escape.

Their ability to pass through matter makes neutrinos useful astronomical messengers and difficult experimental targets. Most simply cross a detector without interacting. A useful observatory therefore needs a huge amount of target material, enough for a small fraction of the passing particles to produce measurable events. IceCube uses the Antarctic ice itself as that material. A cubic kilometer contains roughly a billion tonnes of ice, making the detector’s scale an essential part of the experiment.

Halzen first presented his vision for detecting neutrinos in South Pole ice in 1988. Pursuing it meant convincing colleagues that the idea could work, testing the detection medium and building a collaboration capable of developing the observatory. 

The original IceCube array contains 5,160 optical modules attached to 86 vertical strings. They are frozen into the ice at depths between about 1,450 and 2,450 meters. The full array began operating in 2011, following the installation of the last string in December 2010. Beneath the surface laboratory, the sensors form a three-dimensional network that records light from interactions in and around the instrumented volume.

Deep ice provides both a large target and a medium through which light can travel far enough to be measured. At these depths, the pressure has removed the ordinary air bubbles that make shallower ice cloudy. The South Pole also has the infrastructure needed to support the experiment. Before IceCube, the AMANDA detector demonstrated that Antarctic ice could be used for this kind of observation, providing an essential practical foundation for the larger facility.

Building the array meant drilling deep holes with hot water, lowering cables and sensors into them, and allowing the water to refreeze. Once embedded, the modules could no longer be reached for physical repairs. Their design and testing had to account for that constraint. Behind every scientific result are the people who built those instruments, deployed them during Antarctic field seasons, and keep the data systems running through the polar winter.

IceCube detects the consequences of a neutrino interaction. When a neutrino transfers energy to matter in or near the detector, it can produce fast charged particles. These emit Cherenkov radiation when they move faster than light travels through ice. This does not violate relativity: light propagates more slowly in ice than it does in a vacuum, and the charged particles remain below the vacuum speed of light. The optical modules register the resulting light, providing a measurable trace of an otherwise invisible event. 

Different interactions leave different patterns. A high-energy muon can travel a long distance and produce an elongated track, which is particularly useful for estimating an arrival direction. Other interactions produce compact showers of particles, known as cascades. These tend to give a better estimate of deposited energy, while their directions are generally harder to reconstruct. Both kinds of event contribute to the scientific picture, and combining them improves the observatory’s coverage.

The reconstruction depends on how much light reaches each sensor and when it arrives. Researchers must also understand how that light is scattered and absorbed by the surrounding ice. Calibration is therefore part of the measurement itself. Better knowledge of the ice and the sensors can improve estimates of neutrino energy and direction, including for events recorded years earlier. An event comes with uncertainties that must be carried into any attempt to identify its source.

There is also a substantial background. Cosmic rays striking Earth’s atmosphere produce muons and neutrinos that can enter the detector. An energetic event is not automatically evidence for a distant galaxy. Researchers use event geometry, energy and other information to separate likely astrophysical signals from this background. For some searches, Earth helps: a particle arriving from below has crossed the planet, which blocks atmospheric muons while allowing many neutrinos to pass through.

Even that filtering has limits. As neutrino energy increases, the probability of interaction rises, and Earth becomes appreciably less transparent along long paths through its interior. IceCube has measured this absorption. The observation tests how neutrinos interact at energies beyond those explored in many accelerator experiments and is a reminder that their remarkable ability to cross matter is a matter of probability, rather than an absolute immunity to it. 

In 2013, the collaboration reported 28 high-energy events from two years of data. Their energies, directions and event types were inconsistent with a purely atmospheric explanation. The sample included particles at petaelectronvolt energies and provided the first strong evidence for the high-energy astrophysical neutrino population that IceCube had been built to find. It was a decisive result, but it did not immediately reveal the sources. Finding a population of cosmic neutrinos and identifying the objects producing them are separate observational tasks.

A major advance followed an alert issued on 22 September 2017. IceCube detected a high-energy neutrino whose direction was consistent with TXS 0506+056, a blazar with a relativistic jet directed toward Earth. Gamma-ray observations showed that the object was active. Published in 2018, the combined observations provided compelling evidence for a neutrino source. An independent search of earlier IceCube data also found an excess from that direction during 2014 and 2015, strengthening the case that the association was physically meaningful.

In 2022, IceCube reported evidence for neutrino emission from NGC 1068, also known as Messier 77, an active galaxy roughly 47 million light-years away. The analysis found an excess corresponding to about 80 neutrinos associated statistically with its direction. That number describes a signal inferred above the expected background; individual events do not arrive with a label identifying their home galaxy.

NGC 1068 is particularly useful because its central region is obscured. Leading interpretations place the neutrino production in dense plasma close to the central supermassive black hole, outside its event horizon. Matter and radiation there can absorb high-energy photons while neutrinos escape more readily. Comparing the neutrino emission with observations at other wavelengths helps test those models and investigate conditions in the galaxy’s central environment.

In 2023, IceCube also reported high-energy neutrino emission from the plane of our own Milky Way. The neutrino map is a statistical reconstruction built from events accumulated over years, with improved methods for recognizing and reconstructing cascades. It measures emission associated with cosmic-ray interactions in the Galaxy and gives astronomers another way to investigate how energetic particles move through and interact with galactic matter. 

These results also explain why source identification requires care. A neutrino’s reconstructed direction covers an area of sky, and an object within that area may be there by chance. Researchers ask whether an excess persists, whether its timing fits activity at other wavelengths, and how often a similar pattern could arise from the background. Searching many locations also creates more opportunities for accidental excesses. Statistical significance, calibration and independent observations all matter when deciding what an association means.

Many of the detected astrophysical neutrinos still have unresolved origins. Questions remain about which populations of objects produce most of the emission and exactly where within those objects the particles are accelerated and interact. Increasing the number of well-supported sources will allow researchers to compare their spectra, variability and other properties. The field is developing from detecting a cosmic population toward understanding the physical environments that produce it.

IceCube also studies the neutrino itself. Its denser central detector, DeepCore, extends its reach to lower energies, where atmospheric neutrino oscillations can be measured. Other analyses test interaction probabilities at high energies and search for possible departures from established particle physics, including signals motivated by dark matter models. These searches yield measurements and constraints; a proposed new particle or mechanism becomes a discovery only when the evidence supports it.

There is a much older neutrino population as well. Cosmology predicts a background of relic neutrinos that decoupled from the early universe when it was about a second old. Cosmic expansion has reduced their energies enormously, placing them far outside IceCube’s detection range. Their presence is supported indirectly by cosmological observations, while direct detection remains an experimental goal. Because neutrinos have mass, their gravitational effects also influence the growth of cosmic structure. The same family of particles therefore connects studies of individual cosmic accelerators with questions about the universe as a whole.

The observatory is continuing to develop. The IceCube Upgrade was installed during the 2025–2026 Antarctic season, adding more sensitive instruments and improving calibration. It is intended to strengthen measurements at lower energies and improve reconstruction across the observatory. In its Nobel announcement on 6 October, the collaboration said it expected the first science data from the Upgrade later in 2026. Installation is an important milestone, followed by commissioning and the work needed to turn new instruments into reliable measurements. 

The proposed IceCube-Gen2 would extend the optical detection volume to about eight cubic kilometers and add a radio array aimed at still higher-energy neutrinos. A larger observatory would collect more of these rare events, making more detailed studies of sources possible. Gen2 remains a proposed facility. Its scientific motivation comes directly from IceCube’s results: the existing experiment has demonstrated that the sources can be investigated, while also showing how much more data the field needs. 

Halzen’s Nobel recognizes an individual whose scientific vision and persistence were central to that progress. In his response to the award, he emphasized the recognition it brings to the collaboration. That is an appropriate way to celebrate IceCube. Its discoveries depend on experimental design, engineering, Antarctic operations and years of analysis, with contributions from people working across many institutions and countries.

What makes the achievement satisfying is the distance between the original question and the means of answering it. Understanding energetic events in distant galaxies required learning how light travels through Antarctic ice, building instruments that could survive inside it, and distinguishing a small cosmic signal from a much larger background. The questions about the neutrinos’ origins are still open. Researchers can now test their ideas against observations gathered by instruments buried deep in the ice.

text:
6/25 — Inside Turning Point’s app

Charlie’s political operation relied on an app whose company board included his own senior executive and his mother-in-law.

Apple lists Superfeed Technologies as the developer of TPAction. Superfeed publishes a testimonial attributed to Charlie calling its app “vital” to the 2024 Chase the Vote operation. This was a supplier he publicly endorsed as part of the machinery for turning supporters into votes.

Tyler Bowyer appears as Superfeed’s chairman in its 2022 Arizona report. The March 31, 2025 report lists him as a director alongside Lori Frantzve, Erika’s mother, and investment banker Michael Gibbons. Lori Klein Corbin is another director—a different person from Lori Frantzve.

Bowyer’s official biography says he joined Charlie at TPUSA in 2015, became its chief operating officer, then moved his full-time focus to Turning Point Action in 2022. His role connects the political organization to the company supplying its app.

Turning Point offered an explanation in 2024: discounted development in exchange for Bowyer’s unpaid board service. Its spokesman told The Daily Beast that TPUSA and TPAction officers and directors, including Charlie, held no financial interest in Superfeed and received no compensation from it. That response belongs alongside the filings.

The product itself deserves attention. Superfeed identifies L2 as its data supplier and advertises geographic canvassing lists, contact histories, ballot-status indicators and campaign reports. Those are the company’s advertised capabilities on the pages I saved in 2026, rather than a technical audit of the 2024 campaign. The practical objective is clear: identify people to contact, direct volunteers to them, and record the follow-up.

Elon Musk enters this trail through a separate customer. Early Vote Action reported his $1 million contribution dated August 23, 2024. Apple identifies Superfeed as that committee’s app developer too. That is the documented Musk–Superfeed connection here: a donor, a political committee and its software supplier.

Turning Point PAC’s filing lists a September 25, 2024 payment of $60,000 to a payee named Superfeed Technologies LLC for equipment. It also reported a $60,000 in-kind computer-equipment contribution to Early Vote Action. The latter is a memo entry; counting both as separate cash spending would inflate the total. Matching dates and amounts make the underlying invoice and transfer records worth obtaining.

There is also a correction worth retaining: a 2026 Early Vote Action notice initially reported $5,014.18 for Superfeed texts. Its amendment reduced the amount to zero and said the messages were never disseminated. I do not count it as paid work.

My question is who controlled the decisions, contracts and data within this political infrastructure. A volunteer board seat answers the compensation question only in part. It does not make governance, access or the terms of the discount irrelevant.

Bowyer also appears in the older filings surrounding the family behind Charlie’s event recordings.

text:
Is this the best moment to buy $RCAT?

The stock got crushed after Drone Dominance Gauntlet II.

But underneath the price action, the setup is starting to look very different.

→ ~$325.6M in cash  
→ ~$84.8M in inventory + prepaid inventory  
→ FY2026 revenue target of $150M–$180M  
→ Q2 revenue grew 527% YoY to $20.2M  
→ U.S. Army contract for up to 690 Black Widow systems  
→ Black Widow orders from NATO and Asia-Pacific allies  
→ Japan MoD selected Black Widow  
→ USAF already awarded $2.49M to evaluate Black Widow as the successor to its Teal 2 fleet  
→ And now the USAF has issued an RFP specifically for 350 Black Widow systems

And this is what I think the market may be missing.

The $RCAT story is no longer just:

“Black Widow won the Army SRR program".

It is starting to become:

selection → production → deployment → repeat orders → additional military branches → scale

That transition is already happening.

The Army selected Black Widow.

International allies are ordering it.

Japan selected it.

The Air Force paid Red Cat to evaluate Black Widow as the replacement for its existing Teal 2 fleet.

And roughly two months later, the USAF issued a solicitation to replace that **350-drone Teal 2 fleet with 350 Black Widow systems.**

That last part matters.

This is not an open solicitation asking:

“Who has the best drone?”

The requirement specifically calls for **Teal Black Widow**, manufactured by Teal Drones.

The award has NOT been announced yet.

But if it comes through, Black Widow starts looking less like a single-program Army drone…

…and more like a platform that could spread across multiple branches of the U.S. military.

And Red Cat has spent the last year preparing for exactly that.

Production capacity expanded dramatically.

Inventory has been built.

The balance sheet now has more than $325M in cash.

The company says it is targeting $150M–$180M of 2026 revenue versus just $40.7M in 2025.

The biggest question around $RCAT is no longer whether Black Widow can win a major military program.

It already did.

The real question is:

**Can Red Cat convert those wins into hundreds — and eventually thousands — of delivered systems without margins and execution falling apart?**

That is what the next few quarters are about.

contracts → production → deliveries → revenue → operating leverage

And the Air Force situation may be the next important piece.

First, the USAF paid $2.49M to test Black Widow as a potential Teal 2 replacement.

Then the evaluation systems were scheduled for delivery in August.

Then on September 29, the Air Force issued a solicitation for:

350 Black Widow systems.

Offers closed the next morning.

Now we wait for the award.

If Red Cat gets the 350-system order…

If Army SRR deliveries continue ramping…

If NATO/Japan orders turn into repeat procurement…

And if management can actually hit something close to its $150M–$180M revenue target…

then $RCAT starts becoming a very different company from the one the market was valuing a year

text:
Sad news today. Wg Cdr Dinesh Chander “Danny” Nayyar, Vir Chakra, passed away after battling illness over the last few years.

Danny Sir was commissioned into the IAF on 25 December 1964 with the 91st Pilot Course (25th NDA). Still a very junior fighter pilot, he was sent to the United States for the USAF's Advanced Fighter Course, training on the T-33 and F-86 Sabre at Randolph and Nellis. He was among the last IAF pilots to pass through a remarkable programme that trained some 80 Indian fighter pilots in the US between 1963 and 1966.

He returned to India to fly Mystères with 31 and 26 Squadrons, before moving to the Su-7-equipped 221 Squadron. It was with 221 Sqn that he went to war in December 1971, operating from Panagarh in the Eastern Sector. He flew 11 combat missions.

On his first counter-air strike against Dacca airfield, his Su-7 came under heavy anti-aircraft fire. He pressed home the attack, silencing the guns and destroying a Sabre on the ground.

On another mission, he spent considerable time over enemy territory searching for a carefully camouflaged POL dump until he located and destroyed it. For his actions during the war, Flt Lt DC Nayyar was awarded the Vir Chakra.

His career after 1971 was unusually varied. He became a flying instructor, returned to fighters with 10 Sqn, qualified as a Fighter Combat Leader at TACDE, spent several years instructing with the Iraqi Air Force, including during the opening of the Iran-Iraq War, served with 21 Sqn and eventually commanded 4 Squadron from 1983 to 1985.

He had flown 3,362 hours in the IAF when he moved to Air India. By the end of his flying career, the figure was 12,790 hours.

Over the years, Danny Sir was extraordinarily generous with his memories. When I asked him to help reconstruct his career for the IAFHistory database, he painstakingly went back through his postings, courses and dates, corrected details that did not look right and repeatedly offered to dig out more.

And he kept doing it. As recently as Sep 2025, when I asked him about some flying details, he tried to retrieve the information for me.

Blue skies, Sir.

My condolences to @ReshmaNayyar and the family.

text:
Good Morning I have SLEPT!!! The good lord has blessed me with nine hours of a dream filled wonder sleep!!! 

The appointments are all done for the rest of this week and NEXT week (unless another hades pin gets stuck in my family voodoo doll )! Medicine is being taken, adjustments are being made for the 🤢woozy, and I’m fixing tasty meals for our Pop Pop because he’s lost TEN POUNDS 😑… 

Pop Pop is really needing some carbs and not just meats, thus the extra Popeyes chicken sandwiches. I’m going back to the black or red rice with every meal too… 

See the POTATO BREAD STARTER??? Has anyone tried this??? It makes its own yeast??? I got kinda excited when I saw this because I had a lot of potato bread in Czech and I need to try to start making some bread for him - and I have plenty of Palouse flour. I can get organic potatoes.

Today I have awaken with much renewed dopamine and ready to march forward! I have made a meal plan last night, and will hit my kitchen this morning to make more breakfast sandwiches the next four days and yogurt… 

The Doxycycline for Pop Pop has to have a two hour window in front and behind on calcium barrier, so I have to plan for lunch and mid day milk based things. He is on a 6am & 6pm dosage schedule, it makes me sad it is making him so nauseated but that lump in the testicle is worse, and I’m not sure that the pain there isn’t also a bit of the problem. He can’t have any type of NSAID for swelling or pain. 

Kindly, before anyone offers a new herbal remedy, or supplement for him to take, if you are going to give medical advice then you must take the time to look up low wbc count and shit for platelets aka (medically speaking) - immuno thrombocytopenia. 

It is an old known condition; Pop Pop’s is of an unknown etiology and with nothing to blame for it except his bad three month sickness from the original Chinese 19. He about died with that and it attacked his bone marrow.

I’m tired of explaining his condition to Herbalists and Medicine Maddie’s so do your due diligence and look up a patient’s condition before you starts leaving big DMs or paragraphs full of what you take, or what is heard to be a cure. Twenty-five percent of you in here would have already killed him if he was your family member. 

OTC things and herbs 🌿 can kill you if you have not done hours of research. 

Do your research, and if you care enough to offer such long written advice or solutions then you need to understand what you are trying to solve - with ITP there are VERY limited (if any) treatments, this is a condition you must manage, you can’t reverse or cure it, you can only address each stage of its advancement and the “cures” are equally as damaging as the cause.

Food is the best medicine for him, and cleanliness… antibiotics when necessary to help keep him alive. And eventually a splenectomy or donor platelets could be needed but those things are way more a danger than his immediate… ANYWAY… 

ADVICE: Refrain from offering cures if you don’t know a persons core diagnosis or underlying conditions; you mean well, but you are stepping into a very dangerous position. Out of your lane as my old boss would say.

text:
Tabletalk Devotions with R.C. Sproul
Duration: 365 days
Persecutors of the Prophets
Matthew 23:29–36 “On you may come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of innocent Abel to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah” (v. 35).

Christ’s reference to the scribes and Pharisees being like whitewashed tombs (Matt. 23:27–28) allows for an easy transition to His final woe. Though the religious leaders think they are honoring the prophets when they build and embellish tombs and monuments, they are actually acknowledging themselves as being in league with those who killed the holy men (vv. 29–31).

In Jesus’ day, a period known as Second Temple Judaism, there was a boom in monument construction. These structures were intended to pay tribute to the prophets. They were also supposed to point out the piety of the builders, who in building meant to show that they would have obeyed the prophets their forefathers condemned. Yet in rejecting Jesus, the prophet par excellence, these men allied themselves with their wicked ancestors; in fact, they were worse than their forefathers because in Christ they saw truth more clearly (12:1–6; John 1:17–18). Jesus’ woe tells us that the scribes and Pharisees would have happily buried the prophets just as they gleefully sought to bury Jesus.

Since they are plainly evil, these enemies might as well get on with it and fill the cup of transgression to overflowing (Matt. 23:32), a metaphor for making oneself fit for judgment beyond the shadow of a doubt (Gen. 15:12–16). Basically, Jesus is telling the Pharisees: “God’s wrath is coming on you anyway, why not hurry it along?” Our Savior knows there is more evil for them to do before they are judged. He is going to send them prophets, wise men, and teachers who will also be rejected, as if rejecting Christ is not enough (Matt. 23:33–34). Apostles, evangelists, prophets, and teachers will come to this evil generation and offer one more opportunity for repentance, but just like the Master, the bearers of good news will also be killed (Luke 21:17; Acts 12:1–2).

Jesus’ foes will not miss a chance to spurn God’s grace; thus, on them will fall the blood of all the saints from Abel to Zechariah (Matt. 23:35–36). Abel is the first martyr (Gen. 4:1–8) in Old Testament history; Zechariah is the last (2 Chron. 24:20–21). Those who kill the Messiah and His apostles will feel the anger the Creator has stored up against all those who have hated His own.

Coram deo: Living before the face of God
Matthew Henry says it is easy for us to assume that we would be unlike the scribes and Pharisees and follow Jesus willingly. Yet even centuries later, he writes, “Christ in his Spirit, in his word, in his ministers, is still no better treated.” Are we quick to follow the Lord as He presents Himself today through the preaching of the Word? We have no right to think ourselves better than Pharisees if we are not quick to obey His Word this day.

text:
“Get on your feet!" As National Hispanic Heritage Month continues, we recognize the many contributions Hispanic Americans have made to our country, including music.

On June 18, 1991, President George H. W. Bush invited Cuban-American singer Gloria Estefan and the Miami Sound Machine to perform at the White House during a State Dinner for Brazilian President Fernando Collor de Mello and his wife First Lady Rosane Collor de Mello. Known for iconic songs like “Get On Your Feet” and “Conga,” Gloria Estefan and her husband Emilio helped popularize Latin American pop music in the United States.  

President Bush was a fan of the singer and had previously invited Gloria and her family to the Oval Office in 1990, just before Estefan was injured in a car accident. While she recovered, President Bush called and offered his well-wishes. 

Luckily, her health improved and a year later, the East Room shook with the exciting rhythms of Estefan and the Miami Sound Machine. She wowed the audience in a gold-sequined mini dress, pictured below. The Chicago Tribune called her performance “one of the most jumping and joyously rhythmic evenings the two-centuries-old mansion has experienced,” while Estefan admitted that they toned down their act, “afraid we might blow the roof off the White House.” The president joked that George and Martha Washington “picked up the Latin beat” while peering down from their portraits on the wall. 

Twenty-four years later, Gloria and Emilio Estefan stood in the same room to receive the nation’s highest civilian honor, the Presidential Medal of Freedom, from President Barack Obama. 

📸: Photo by Joyce C. Naltchayan, George Bush Presidential Library and Museum/NARA
