text:
Podcast Summary | The Joe Rogan Experience: #2561 - LL Cool J

Overview
LL Cool J frames a five-decade career as the product of blue-collar discipline, timing, and an environment that put him close to hip-hop at its birth, not celebrity ambition. He calls himself a celebrity by consequence, and argues that arrogance blocks learning while learning is the most fulfilling part of success. The conversation moves from Def Jam's formation and early hip-hop culture to jiu-jitsu, Bruce Lee, combat sports as a soul test, relentless ambition, mastery, and the difference between harmony and balance. A second throughline is the speaker's own framework for ambition: Clausewitzian friction, thriving over surviving, and the idea that dreams do not carry deadlines.

Key Themes
- Fame is best treated as a byproduct of the work, not the goal; staying blue-collar and treating industry events lightly helps sustain longevity.
- Jiu-jitsu is uniquely humbling for famous people because charm, charisma, and status are removed from the equation; results are undeniable.
- Arrogance blocks learning, and learning, especially through hard skills, is described as the most fulfilling part of success rather than a stepping stone to status.
- Early hip-hop was empowering because marginalized kids heard people like themselves sounding powerful; early displays of wealth signaled survival and toughness, not portfolio status.
- Discipline, drive, and perseverance are under-embraced; giving up is framed as harmful, while empathy is distinguished from weakness and comfort is framed as the enemy of progress.
- Combat sports expose character: two people's souls get tested, and a fighter's rank, meaning who they are, can be seen in their eyes.
- Relentlessness is necessary for success but explicitly not the same as ease or constant comfort; being yourself beats imitating others.
- Mastery is transferable; starting over as a beginner in a new discipline renews creativity and builds a beginner's mindset.
- Harmony is preferred over balance: things fit in their place like an orchestra rather than being distributed equally.

Detailed Summary
LL Cool J said he was 16 when he got his first contract. He describes Def Jam's early formation as a production company started by Rick Rubin, with Rubin and Russell Simmons later forming the label. He says he was Def Jam's first act. The first song on Def Jam Productions was It's Yours by T La Rock. Ad Rock from the Beastie Boys programmed the beat, Rick Rubin produced it, and LL Cool J did the mic.

His exposure to hip-hop came around ages 8, through tapes circulating out of the Bronx while he was in Queens and North Babylon. He cites Grandmaster Flash and the Furious 4 before they were the Five, the Treacherous Three, and Cold Crush. He notes Sugar Hill's Rapper's Delight was 1979 but says he was into hip-hop before that, around 1975 to 1977.

Before jiu-jitsu, he did martial arts including aikido, karate, wing chun, and jeet kune do. He recently started jiu-jitsu and has been doing it around a year. His teacher is Brian Glick in Brooklyn, who trained under Renzo Gracie; Scott Khan connected them. Rogan and LL Cool J first met briefly around 1994 at an NBC event, and Rogan remembered LL Cool J making fun of the event.

Rogan argues jiu-jitsu is good for famous people because results are undeniable and cannot be charmed or charisma'd through. The discussion touches Hunter S. Thompson as someone who could pull off a cigarette holder. Framing fame as a consequence of the work, not the goal, keeps an artist grounded. Sustained learning, especially difficult skills, is presented as a way to stop obsessing over oneself; jiu-jitsu is cited as an example where you are focused only on survival.

Discipline, drive, and perseverance are framed as under-embraced virtues. Giving up is framed as harmful, while empathy is distinguished from weakness. Being comfortable with discomfort and continuing despite setbacks is framed as necessary, using the idea that you do not crash the plane over one or two burning engines; you keep flying and look to land. Progress stalls when people cling to comfort and become defensive. Advice should be judged on its content, not the messenger; even unlikely sources can offer useful guidance, and ideas should be contextualized to one's own life. Ambitious people can trigger resentment in those afraid to commit, but dreams do not have deadlines and three years will pass regardless.

The Clausewitz concept of friction and the Clausewitzian trinity are described as three forces: probability, chance, and luck; logic and reason; and passion, enmity, and hatred. The speaker says society currently operates in a place of emotions and passions rather than logic and reason. His mother showed him books depicting drug addicts to warn him what that world leads to, and told him girls do not like dummies. Intelligence without willpower still fails; intelligence, health, and inner emotional strength are cited as needed together.

One spark can set a prairie on fire is cited to warn against spiraling from one bad thought. Attitude determines your altitude and get comfortable being uncomfortable are offered as principles no one teaches in school; you need wise people or must figure it out yourself. Bruce Lee is quoted through the idea of absorbing what is useful. The speaker credits Bruce Lee for getting him into acting.

Bruce Lee's Dao of Kung Fu is called the original book of mixed martial arts. He combined American boxing, Chinese boxing, kung fu, karate, judo, and other styles, which was considered heretical at the time. Martial arts were previously siloed, and instructors could be upset if students practiced other styles. A rumor persists that Bruce Lee's death involved the Triads and a dispute after he left Raymond Chow's movies for Hollywood. The official conclusion focused on a hypersensitivity reaction to ingredients in the prescription painkiller Equagesic, which he took for a headache. The autopsy reportedly found severe brain swelling and no external injuries; later retrospective hypotheses include heat-related illness and hyponatremia. Bruce Lee was described as lightning quick and unprecedentedly skilled for his time, and karate schools opened all over the world after his impact.

The speaker first heard Sugar Hill Gang in a lunchroom in Jamaica Plain, Massachusetts. He describes coming up around kids who were 17 years old and still in eighth grade. Early hip-hop made invisible kids feel empowered, in contrast to seeing Black people on the news mainly in handcuffs. Early hip-hop bravado came from being an underdog, not from being on top. Biggie is cited as an example: footage of him at 17 on a street corner rhyming, already with spectacular flow. Jewelry in early hip-hop is described as a message of toughness and survival, being able to wear it in any neighborhood. Early hustlers, including the Supreme Team, AZ, Rich, and Alpo, were cues for hip-hop culture.

Earlier displays of money were not about open ostentatious wealth or portfolio-level status, but about proving personal accomplishment after having nothing. The achievement was framed as I did this in spite of difficult circumstances, comparable to coming from behind in Monopoly and feeling proud. Financial responsibility and wealth planning were not part of the mindset at the time; the focus was on immediate desires like getting a Benz. Examples of wealth display included having 50 grand in a dresser drawer, a gold chain, a nice car, and doing better than before. The speaker says he never lost the mindset of where he really comes from.

Fame and extreme success can isolate people, making it hard to stay relatable, learn, handle problems, or avoid being surrounded by yes-men. The conversation notes the risk of being in a bubble, forgetting humanity, and going crazy or isolated like Howard Hughes. The speaker says he is an introvert despite doing public-facing work; he needs to read, relax, and recharge. He avoids being surrounded by many people because it brings problems and because he cannot manage everyone's behavior. A Public Enemy logo detail: Chuck D took a picture of the speaker's friend E Love standing next to him on stage and put him in silhouette. Run-DMC took him on tour around the world. He did Dick Clark in 1985, and went to London around age 17 where the reception was incredible. When he put out a love song, some people were upset that he was willing to be that vulnerable; he says he got booed or people were mad. He argues that balance is real life and that having both hard and vulnerable sides is valid.

He frames his own art as reflecting the real, saying others keep it 50 and call it 100 and may privately enjoy what they publicly reject. Hip-hop's global reach is presented as real and culturally formative: fans worldwide engaged with it early, sometimes rapping English lyrics verbatim without speaking English. He names France, Germany, and Japan as places with early hip-hop engagement and pioneers. He recorded a track in Germany with an artist rapping in German while he rapped in English; the song was not known in America. French hip-hop is repeatedly praised, and Brazilian hip-hop is mentioned as enjoyable despite not understanding Portuguese. Exposure to hip-hop scenes abroad changed his mindset and reduced a myopic, U.S.-centered view of Black and hip-hop culture.

A major sports argument follows: basketball footwork, constant direction changes, misdirection, and hand-eye coordination can be a strong base for MMA striking. The heavyweight champion is said to be from France, and France is described as a hub for elite fighters. A fighter described as a former Muay Thai fighter who played basketball is cited as an example of unusual mobility for a large athlete. Soccer is also cited as a strong MMA base because of cardio and constant leg movement. Floyd Mayweather is praised for intellect, traps, elusiveness, and fighting right in front of opponents. Sugar Ray Robinson is referenced and described as elusive, able to stand in front and move out. Willie Pep is mentioned as having won an entire round without throwing. The speaker says his grand-uncle was John Henry Lewis, a light heavyweight champion later knocked out by Joe Lewis after moving up to heavyweight; he discovered this through DNA research and a Finding Your Roots episode. His mother was adopted, explaining why he did not know these family connections earlier. Boxing is described as definitive and understandable even to non-fans; combat sports generally are framed as revealing character.

Combat sports are framed as a soul test, watching two people's souls get exposed; you can see a person's rank, meaning who they are, in their eyes. Trainers can often tell early whether someone has it inside them; some people lack it, others have it if they can keep the fire burning. The preference is to thrive over survive; living defensively means missing opportunities to act. Self-awareness matters: even with innate traits, people can decide to improve, though it is not easy. The amateur-versus-pro framing: amateurs say that is easy for you to say to pros, which translates to that is too hard for me or not wanting to be uncomfortable. The internet is compared to a script, while real life is on its feet; skills that work behind a keyboard do not necessarily work in person, and the internet rewards instant validation unlike real life.

You can look at a man's eyes and tell his rank, not arrogant rank but who they are. An analogy of looking into a puppy's eyes is used to know what you are dealing with. Success is framed as difficult by nature: dreaming of roses means you get thorns, and climbing Mount Everest involves weather, slippery slopes, and burning legs. Living the dream often sounds like people are upset but trying to keep themselves happy. The internet rewards chopping down trees in the wrong forest; real life requires putting your ladder against the right wall. Ambition is framed as asking what you would do if you were not afraid, and living as if a documentary crew were filming your journey to success. Being relentless is emphasized as necessary in life.

Relentlessness is framed as necessary for success, but explicitly not the same as ease or constant comfort. A core argument is to be yourself rather than imitating others; people often know what they want but fear judgment. Rick Rubin is credited with great taste and a reductive production approach, stripping things down rather than piling on. Trusting intuition and making taste adjustments is presented as central to creative decision-making and collaboration.

LL Cool J says his first album Radio credits reduced by Rick Rubin, not produced by. Rick Rubin stripped down early hip-hop records, contrasting them with longer, more instrumental and disco-influenced records. LL Cool J sent demo tapes to multiple labels and received standard rejection letters. His mother used a tax return to buy him a Korg drum machine. He and Frankie and Spin Master Finesse made a pause tape: LL played the beat, Frankie scratched, then LL rapped over it. LL called Rick Rubin repeatedly after sending a tape; Ad Rock heard the demo and played it for Rick. Rubin called LL to come to the studio; LL recalls commuting excitedly by subway. They made a demo called Catch This Break, then played it for Russell Simmons. After further studio work with Ad Rock programming, Rick producing, and Jazzy Jay scratching, they made I Need a Beat. Russell Simmons and Rick Rubin started Def Jam as a label, not just a production company; LL and Ad Rock did two independent singles. Rubin suggested shortening Ladies Love Cool James to LL Cool J. LL initially disliked Going Back to Cali in demo form before coming around.

He describes trusting Rick Rubin's ear even when he initially disliked a song, using Going Back to Cali as an example: he hated the demo at first, then came around as it sounded different and became a thing. He frames songwriting around feeling over lyrical complexity, saying he aimed for the James Brown zone: how does it feel, rather than hyperfocused lyricism or cleverness. Simplicity is a central theme: simple, emotionally direct ideas are underrated and hard to achieve, using Jesse's Girl as an example of a simple sentiment many people feel. He compares overthinking a song to overthinking a martial arts kick, saying that once technique is internalized it becomes fluid rather than conscious. Becoming famous at 16 is described as immersive and enjoyable, with no sense of missing out on normal teenage experiences like prom. He emphasizes being completely consumed by the work and wanting success with every fiber of your being, refusing to take no even from yourself.

At 16, LL Cool J was traveling by bus and subway while making records and often loved Rick Rubin's ideas. He recalls playing Rock the Bells for a friend who listened on a Walkman and asked to hear it again. Quincy Jones told him he had to forget two-thirds of what he knew before he could get a hit. LL says his approach was to go after feelings with lyrics and make songs people can feel, rather than make listeners analyze an album like an audiobook. He describes introducing hip-hop in Maine in a small gymnasium, with maybe 15 kids and 20 parents or around 100 people, explaining what a DJ does and how hip-hop works. He says there was no hip-hop industry or road map at the time; Russell Simmons and publicist Bill Adler are mentioned as exceptions, but there were no established managers, platforms, branding, or strategic partners. He views hip-hop as a new art form emerging from grassroots belief and love, and calls being present for it a blessing and stroke of luck.

Being completely consumed by your pursuit is presented as necessary for success. Dreams have no deadline; people should not give up due to age. Colonel Sanders started Kentucky Fried Chicken around age 65. Cornelius Vanderbilt was doing business into his 80s. George Foreman returned to the sporting world later in life. Sam Jackson is cited as an example of someone who kept going. The man in the arena poem is referenced as motivation to stay in the arena. The limitation is in your mind; fear of failure holds people back. Creativity matters more than competition; teaching kids to create is more valuable than teaching them to compete. Even if a goal is not achieved, the process improves character and evolves the soul. People can be black belts in parts of life without recognizing it due to lack of self-awareness.

Martial arts are described as a vehicle for developing human potential; early training taught humility, respect, and manners. Belt progression marks milestones and reinforces hard work and focus. Black belts traditionally became black from heavy use, dirt, and grit, not dye. Old black belts can wear down and turn almost white again. Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belts can reach coral belt status for upholding the art form and contribution to the craft. Joseph Campbell's hero's journey is referenced regarding returning to the beginning. A personal red pill metaphor is offered: decide not to give up and see what life looks like in five years; if not there, five more years may be needed.

Starting over as a beginner in a new discipline is valuable: it builds a beginner's mindset, renewed excitement, and new avenues for creativity and thought. Mastery is transferable; once you understand the stages of success in one domain, you can apply that mindset to other missions. The speaker prefers harmony over balance: things fit in their place like an orchestra, where certain instruments lead, rather than equal distribution. There is a distinction between being nice and being kind: nice is seeking to be liked; kind sets and protects boundaries, and no status excuses stepping over them. Mastery of self, vision, and steps taken, plus the mindset of winning, are framed as the core pursuit being encouraged. Hearing from someone with lived experience is valued over theory for managing thoughts and getting through challenges.

The speaker says he will read one book for three or four years. Books are likened to martial arts belts: reading a book once is like taking a few lessons, not becoming a black belt; endless information means you can keep earning degrees. The Book of Five Rings by Miyamoto Musashi was cited as one of the most impactful books, read many times, starting at a young age. Musashi was described as having killed 60 or 61 men in one-on-one combat with swords. His philosophy was framed as requiring complete harmony across art, creativity, and poetry alongside ruthlessness with a sword. Specific Musashi concepts mentioned include being sticky on your opponent, keeping the sun at your back, using the threshold, positioning within a room's corners, holding and positioning the sword, and using both long and short swords. Musashi reportedly made opponents wait for hours, and died in a cave where he went after writing the book. The book is said to be from the 1400s.

Anthony Robbins' early work was mentioned as an influence for inspiration and for psychology around time management, mind management, and managing expectations. Education was said to derive from a Latin root meaning to bring out, bringing out what is already inside a person, as a good teacher or martial arts instructor does. Aspiration was framed as common among young people in America, where the idea that you can go from the bottom to the top is promoted, but people often get beaten down by life, circumstances, and poor choices. The speaker suggested the other person should write a book on these ideas, because people want to hear it from someone successful speaking from experience rather than theory. Anecdotes about a famous person entering a studio with a white belt illustrate that it is different when a known person trains, since someone gets to choke out a famous rapper.

🔴ANTISEMITISM: @X🔴/Haaretz/

Trump's Envoy Credits Elon Musk for 'Very Large' Reduction in Antisemitism on X. Experts Question His Claim

Arno Rosenfeld •Washington Correspondent

Yehuda Kaploun says X's location labels have curbed anti-Jewish hate, but watchdogs insist there's no evidence the feature has made a meaningful difference as antisemitic abuse remains rampant

WASHINGTON — Yehuda Kaploun, the U.S. envoy to combat antisemitism, told reporters Monday that Elon Musk had overseen a significant drop in antisemitism on X, a claim disputed by experts who insist anti-Jewish hate remains rampant on the billionaire's platform.

"We've seen a very large reduction in antisemitic posts now that people are having to put their location," Kaploun said, referring to a transparency feature rolled out last fall that shows the country or region where X estimates an account is based. "It's a positive step."

Kaploun said that Musk had launched the location tags one day after a user based in Poland posted claiming to be a Palestinian living in Gaza.

But experts say there is no evidence that the location feature has meaningfully reduced antisemitism on X, which surged after Musk purchased the platform in 2022 and loosened restrictions on hate speech and harassment.

"The addition of limited location data for accounts has not changed the fact that antisemitism continues to run rampant on X," said Imran Ahmed, who heads the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

"The idea that location data alone would solve the epidemic of hate on X is fanciful."

Following the stabbing of two Jewish men in London's Golders Green neighborhood in April, the organization found 130 hateful posts on X aimed at prominent Jewish users and organizations — including messages celebrating the attack, minimizing the Holocaust and using antisemitic slurs.

"Any visibly Jewish person on X can attest that antisemitism has certainly not gotten better," said Amy Spitalnick, CEO of the Jewish Council for Public Affairs, which jointly released a study with Ahmed's organization shortly before X introduced the location feature.

The report described as "one of the most dangerous vehicles in history for spreading antisemitism."

Kaploun's praise for Musk, who has endorsed antisemitic views on X, came after he was asked whether Musk and Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive of Meta, should do more to counter antisemitism given their close ties with the Trump administration.

He offered no evidence for the claim that antisemitism has decreased on X.

He was speaking to a group of international reporters, many of whom were participating in a week-long trip organized by the State Department to promote the administration's efforts to counter antisemitism.

"More can be done, and we'll be working with those groups," Kaploun added.

Kaploun has drawn criticism for making sweeping claims about his ability to counter antisemitism and secure Holocaust restitution.

He claimed earlier this year that he would settle all outstanding Holocaust restitution claims within the next two years, despite longstanding diplomatic obstacles to resolving them He has also reportedly been campaigning to fold the Office of the Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues into his own office.

text:
WHAT NEW ITALY ? (Guess who reversing decades of stable government has had as many as four prime ministers... since with nearly four years in office and the longest-running government since Mussolini old-Britain Giorgia Meloni came to lead the formerly 80-governments-in-60-years land of perpetual change ?)

Number 10’s famous front entrance has become the most notorious revolving door in Europe. We have had as many prime ministers in the last 10 years as in the previous 40. The United Kingdom is the “new Italy”, now infamous for constant changes of government. And the instability is getting worse. (...) The irony is that the UK has become the “new Italy” just as Italy itself is showing signs of becoming “old Britain”. Its current prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, is about to reach the four-year mark, and will soon become the longest-lasting head of a government since Mussolini. She is also favourite to win Italy’s general election due next year, so could conceivably be at the helm in Rome for years to come. (...) On every front—political, economic, immigration—Meloni’s record is mixed, or hard to read across into lessons for the UK. She has played the Brussels well and secured big EU post-pandemic funding, but Italy’s growth this year is below both the UK’s and the EU average, she has offered no bold economic reform, and her country’s huge debt burden isn’t reducing. Illegal immigration has fallen sharply, but legal immigration has risen as a deliberate policy to counter population decline. She has tamed a fractious political coalition but in March decisively lost a referendum on judicial reform, shattering a flagship strategy and any notion of her invincibility. However, wading through analysis and commentary on the mercurial Italian leader, one theme becomes ever more apparent. Meloni has consistently exceeded expectations. Starting from a very weak political and economic position in 2022, with a record as an extreme populist—pro-Putin, Eurosceptic, anti-immigrant, involved in culture wars, the lot—she rapidly became a masterclass in “tough pragmatism”, earning plaudits in Brussels, Washington, Rome and beyond. Partly this was about retreating from previous extremes, notably on Russia, but equally important was the building of strong alliances across the political and international spectrum, bringing big benefits in, for example, securing EU funding and curbing illegal immigration. Contrast this with the UK. Since Cameron lost his EU referendum in 2016, every prime minister has performed worse—mostly far worse—than already low expectations. If Meloni is any guide, the leader who stabilises the ship won’t be a genius. They will just be far better than generally expected. Fortunately for Burnham, the most likely next leader, this offers real hope. General expectations could hardly be worse.

Andrew Adonis (June 10, 2026)

text:
Well, what the world’s problems are due to is very tough to pin down. We can blame human greed and it explains a lot. We can similarly blame systems that emerge from groups of people and are hard to change. But we can say with confidence that it’s not intelligence because there’s already tons of evidence.
1) Many brilliant people exist, but the masses hardly listen to them
2) We have roads connecting Africa to Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. Nations still choose to hardly invest in them at all. Check the numbers, it’s appalling. Every nation is responsible for themselves, but when they’re ok, sadly local focuses are still overall preferred to helping other nations
3) Musk at DOGE learned if he altered certain corruption too much he’d be killed
4) The most intelligent people get hired to do pretty much whatever the market pays a lot for that satisfies them overall balancing the challenge of the world and the pay. There’s no forcing function that they work on the problems that actually matter, other than their own internal drive to do so…but that gets overridden all too often
5) The ‘first world’ is already so optimized that it’s difficult for startups and young people to contribute anything more valuable than just running the existing machinery; and if they do, they get acquired and the existing machinery remains the determinant of what runs the given country. There are exceptions, and they drive progress. (But even Tesla was once offered to Apple for acquisition.)

What’s needed to fix most of societies problems, I think, are some key innovations:
• How do you make a market reward the well-being of all instead of whatever is most profitable? I believe there’s are ways, pooling money like taxes and rewarding it to those who reduce the most bad, particularly where the bad causes loss of compounding GDP growth. Ironically it’s just better economics. Doesn’t seem like rocket science. Higher intelligence might help with that, but implementing it also means overcoming the above entrenchment, so once again intelligence probably isn’t really a blocker here.
• How do you get companies to be aligned with people?
Accountability and transparency. The implementation has to be clever, but I know this doesn’t require more intelligence. It requires barreling through all the many individual forces that will try to stop such a thing from threatening their bottom line.
• How do we fix politics? The broken system can only be fixed by making moves within the broken system, so any fix is slow and at minimum requires massive political organization, like 5M people marching on Washington DC, not intelligence.

The class that owns wealth, having earned it somehow, determines what happens. There are many intelligent plans and intelligent ideas already that just don’t get implemented because of a variety of blockers the current system presents. I’m sure higher intelligence could help fix the system, but it’s most willpower, bravery, political organization, activism, distributed strategy, grass roots movement, and money that are needed.

The Carolina Panthers delivered a dominant Week 4 win over the Detroit Lions, and while concerns about Bryce Young’s long-term fit at quarterback have lingered, the early results suggest he’s answering those questions decisively. Young has been exceptional under center, and Carolina’s offense appears as potent as ever through four games.

Over the past few years, the Panthers pursued a quarterback of the future, with several names in the mix. One of those players, Jack Plummer, spent time with the team in 2024 and drew interest from the Washington Commanders in free agency as injuries at quarterback mounted.

The Commanders recently brought in Plummer for a workout. Plummer wasn’t selected in the 2024 NFL Draft but joined the Panthers as an undrafted free agent. Although he spent the 2024 season on Carolina’s practice squad and was released before the 2025 season, his performance later earned him the 2026 United Football League MVP after leading the Orlando Storm with 2,166 passing yards and 17 touchdowns, placing him among the league’s top quarterbacks. This strong play put him back on NFL teams’ radar.

Following the workout, reports indicated that Plummer impressed but was not signed by Washington at that time, though a signing could be possible in the future depending on roster needs and injuries. Washington currently features four in-house quarterbacks, with Marcus Mariota and others in the mix, limiting immediate movement unless a clear opportunity arises.

Looking ahead to Week 5, Plummer could remain a potential option should quarterback injuries persist across the league. Washington is dealing with injuries to several quarterbacks, and while Jayden Daniels is aiming to return in Week 5, there’s no guarantee a signing would make immediate sense. For Carolina, the focus remains on continuing Bryce Young’s strong start. A challenging test awaits in Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. If the Panthers want to reinforce their position with a statement victory, this matchup offers a prime opportunity.

Washington just blinked, and almost nobody noticed.

In April, Trump's red line was ZERO enrichment in Iran. Vance flew to Islamabad and demanded that all enrichment end and every major enrichment facility be dismantled. Reports had the US asking for a 20-year halt.

Now Vance is reportedly asking for a "meaningful reduction."

In six months the demand went from zero enrichment to less enrichment.

That isn't firmness. It's a retreat dressed in tough talk.

Nations with improving leverage don't walk back their own red lines. Nations losing a war of attrition do.

Tehran sees it. That's why Iran is holding firm on enrichment rights while Washington quietly moves toward it.

But "Iran flatly rejects" isn't the full story either.

In April, Iran offered a shorter enrichment halt. Its hard line was never "no limits." It was "the uranium doesn't leave Iran." And "nothing moves until our conditions are met" is a demand about sequencing: blockade and frozen assets first, nuclear second.

So the outline of a deal is already visible:

→ Iran's right to enrich is recognized in principle.
→ Enrichment is capped in practice.
→ The 60% stockpile is diluted or held by a third party.
→ The steps are sequenced so neither side moves first and gets burned.

The gap between the two sides isn't really about the nuclear question anymore. It's about who moves first.

Washington is moving. It just won't admit it.

THE COPENHAGEN MOMENT: How Senator Dino Melaye's Voice at the IBA Redefined Nigeria's Place in Global Politics

At the Bella Center in Copenhagen, where over 6,000 lawyers, jurists and world leaders have gathered for the IBA Annual Conference 2026 from October 4-9, one voice cut through the legal technicalities and spoke directly to the conscience of the world.

That voice was Senator Dino Melaye – the erudite Senator, human rights activist, and as millions call him, the hope of the common man.

Speaking at the highly charged session “The Rule of Law in a Trump Era”– a session the world was watching – Senator Melaye did not just represent Nigeria. He represented the voiceless.

1. ON GLOBAL POLITICS: Truth Has No Volume

In an era where global politics is being reshaped by power, not principles, Dino Melaye reminded the world that the rule of law must not be selective.

His position was clear and globally impactful: You cannot preach democracy abroad and weaponize the law at home. You cannot defend freedom in Washington or London and suppress dissent in Africa.

For the international audience, this was powerful. A Nigerian Senator standing in Europe telling world powers that the crisis of democracy is not a regional problem – it is a global contagion. When courts are captured, when activism is criminalized, when opposition is tagged as treason – democracy dies, whether in America, Europe or Nigeria.

That message trended instantly. Clips from his intervention titled “Senator Dino Melaye at The Rule of Law in a Trump era session in the ongoing IBA conference. Listen.” have gone viral on TikTok and across legal networks.

2. ON RULE OF LAW: Asking Government to Do Right is Not an Offence

This was the heart of his erudite intervention and his most profound global impact.

Senator Melaye argued forcefully: Asking government to do the right thing should not be seen as an offence, but as an offer for a leader to have peaceful coexistence with the people.

In Copenhagen, he redefined activism for the world:

When a citizen criticizes power, he is not fighting the government - he is helping and nurturing the government to avoid fighting it's own people.

For young lawyers from 130 countries listening, this was a new doctrine of governance. True rule of law is not when people fear the government, but when government fears to betray the trust of the people.

His years as Nigeria’s most fearless voice – facing arrests, persecution, yet never silenced – gave him moral authority that no textbook can teach. He is not just a politician; he is a case study in the resilience of human rights.

3. ON U.S. INFLUENCE: A Mirror to the Superpower

On U.S. influence, Melaye was brilliant, balanced and bold. He acknowledged America’s role as a historic defender of the rule of law, but warned that in the Trump era and beyond, American influence must be measured by consistency.

The world cannot have two standards of justice – one for the powerful and one for the powerless. If the U.S. wants to remain the moral compass of the world, it must stand for justice in Africa as loudly as it does in Ukraine, in Gaza, and in its own Capitol.

This resonated deeply with delegates from the Global South.

THE GLOBAL IMPACT

Why did this one speech matter so much?

a) It Restored Nigeria's Image: At a time when Nigeria is often reported for negative news, Dino Melaye showed the world that Nigeria produces courageous, intellectually grounded human rights defenders.

b) It Empowered African Lawyers: He gave African delegates language to challenge shrinking civic space without fear.

c) It Reconnected Law to the People: The IBA is often seen as elitist. Melaye brought the street, the market woman, the unemployed youth into the Bella Center. He reminded 6,000 Senior Advocates that law without the common man is just a rule book.

In the end, the erudite Senator left Copenhagen with a standing message that will outlive the conference:

text:
Go VOTE!! [2/2]

Major rollback of California climate regulations, which he argues are responsible for high electricity and fuel prices.
AI / technology
Pro-AI but favors guardrails: worker protections, audits of government AI systems, transparency around employment decisions, AI education and monitoring job displacement.
Generally favors lighter regulation so AI companies remain and grow in California; has raised concerns about AI inequality and children’s technology use but is much less regulation-oriented.
Sources for those positions include their campaigns and independent California voter guides. ⁠
Xavier Becerra’s basic vision
Becerra’s pitch is essentially: California’s underlying direction doesn’t need to be reversed, but government needs to work much better and make the state affordable again.
On housing, he’s actually more pro-construction than the stereotype of a traditional California Democrat might suggest. He says he’d declare housing a state emergency on his first day, create a team reporting directly to the governor to unblock projects, accelerate permitting, and find financing for approximately 40,000 approved affordable units that haven’t yet broken ground. He would simultaneously retain renter protections and environmental standards. ⁠
His economic philosophy relies considerably more on government intervention. He talks about attacking price gouging, healthcare consolidation, utility-rate increases and other market failures, rather than primarily lowering taxes and regulation. ⁠
Healthcare is probably the area where Becerra has the most detailed agenda. He wants California to protect people affected by federal Medi-Cal cuts, expand primary care, increase the healthcare workforce, use the state’s purchasing power to lower prices and continue toward universal coverage. ⁠
On homelessness, he’s proposing something between the old status quo and the tougher enforcement model Hilton advocates: more prevention and Housing First funding, but also accountability for results and the position that someone offered appropriate shelter shouldn’t simply be allowed to remain indefinitely on the street. ⁠
Politically, Becerra also makes resisting the Trump administration a significant part of his governorship. He says he’d challenge federal actions in court when they conflict with California policies on immigration, healthcare, environmental regulation and other areas. ⁠
Steve Hilton’s basic vision
Hilton’s pitch is much closer to: California’s existing governing model itself is the problem, so the state needs a significant reset.
His centerpiece is affordability through tax and regulatory reductions. His campaign promises no state income tax on the first $150,000 of earnings, abolition of California’s $800 minimum business tax, $3 gasoline, substantially lower utility bills and a major reduction in what he describes as state bureaucratic spending. ⁠
Housing is one area where Hilton and Becerra actually agree on part of the diagnosis: California needs considerably more housing. Their methods differ. Hilton wants to weaken the ability of private parties to use CEQA lawsuits to delay developments, reduce fees and zoning restrictions, and allow California to expand outward with more small single-family starter homes instead of concentrating almost entirely on infill apartments. ⁠
His homelessness strategy represents a much sharper departure from current policy. Hilton supports clearing encampments, enforcing anti-camping laws, spending more money on inexpensive shelters and sober housing and expanding compulsory treatment/institutional care in severe cases. ⁠
On energy, Hilton is making one of the clearest contrasts in the campaign. He argues California’s environmental mandates have substantially contributed to high gasoline and electricity prices and proposes rolling many of them back. Becerra instead wants to preserve the clean-energy transition while modifying policies where affordability becomes a serious problem.

Go VOTE Californians!! [1/2]

As of October 7, 2026, California’s governor race is between Xavier Becerra (Democrat) and Steve Hilton (Republican) for the November 3 general election. They’re offering substantially different approaches to the state: Becerra generally wants to use state government more aggressively to lower costs, expand services and regulate markets, while Hilton wants to reduce taxes, regulation and the size of state government. ⁠
Here’s the clearest comparison.
Issue
Xavier Becerra
Steve Hilton
Taxes / cost of living
Keep California’s progressive tax structure; use state enforcement against price gouging and unjustified rate increases; expand childcare and other assistance. He opposes the proposed one-time billionaire wealth tax.
Make the first $150,000 of income exempt from California income tax, then move toward a flatter structure above that; halve the gas tax; eliminate the $800 annual minimum business tax.
Housing
Declare a housing emergency, accelerate permitting, push cities to allow more apartments/duplexes/condos, fund roughly 40,000 already-approved affordable units, strengthen tenant protections and expand down-payment help.
Cut development fees and regulations, sharply restrict CEQA lawsuits, encourage starter homes and suburban expansion, and create financing assistance for first-time buyers.
Homelessness
Focus heavily on preventing homelessness through rental assistance and eviction prevention, but says people shouldn’t simply remain on the street after shelter is offered. Continue Housing First while pairing housing with treatment where necessary.
Clear encampments more aggressively, enforce anti-camping laws, increase police involvement, expand lower-cost group/sober housing and make it easier to institutionalize people with severe mental illness in some circumstances.
Energy / gas
Continue California’s transition toward clean energy but says affordability should influence how quickly some mandates proceed. Invest in grid resilience and clean energy while trying to reduce utility costs.
Roll back major climate and energy mandates, increase oil/refinery activity and reduce taxes/regulations with a stated target of $3 gasoline and utility bills roughly half their current level.
Healthcare
This is one of his signature issues. Protect and strengthen Medi-Cal, expand coverage, lower drug prices, invest in primary care and healthcare workers, and ultimately move toward universal coverage/single payer.
Focus more on competition and cost transparency. His plan calls for published healthcare pricing, tougher oversight of PBMs and insurer/provider competition. He would end state-funded Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants.
Education
Expand early education, childcare, tutoring and intervention; strengthen public schools and higher education. He opposes shifting public-school funding into private-school voucher-style programs.
Strong emphasis on literacy: every child reading by third grade, phonics, skills/vocational training, easier removal of ineffective teachers, more charter-school options and allowing some public funding to follow students to other/private schools.
Crime / policing
More conventional Democratic approach combining law enforcement with prevention, treatment and social services.
Much more enforcement-oriented. Wants to expand the CHP into what he calls a California State Police Force, add officers and take on crime that crosses city/county boundaries.
Immigration
Defend immigrant protections and healthcare access; challenge federal actions he considers unconstitutional.
Much more restrictive approach, including ending Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants and aligning more closely with federal immigration enforcement.
Climate regulation
Broadly preserve California’s climate strategy, though he has indicated specific mandates could be reconsidered if affordability becomes too burdensome.

🇯🇵 🚨 ADVANTEST CONFIRMS PERSONAL DATA WAS STOLEN IN FEBRUARY CYBERATTACK

Advantest, the Japanese maker of semiconductor test equipment, is notifying people that data taken in a February 2026 cyberattack included their personal information, according to a notice letter dated October 6, 2026 and filed with the California Attorney General.

What Advantest says:
• Advantest says it became aware in February 2026 that an unauthorized third party had accessed its systems and extracted some data from its servers; the California AG filing (Advantest America, Inc.) lists the breach date as Jan 23, 2026
• Data types listed in the notice: contact information, date of birth, Social Security numbers, national ID numbers, driver's licenses, passport numbers, medical and financial information, and other ID numbers
• The incident was contained and the network restored; authorities, including law enforcement, were notified
• Affected people are offered 18 months of free Kroll credit and identity monitoring (enroll by Jan 4, 2027)

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The notice does not give the number of people affected or say whether they are employees, customers or partners. Advantest says it has no information that the data was published or misused, and no group has publicly claimed the attack. Recipients should watch for phishing that uses the breach.

Spawn of the North (1938) - Imprint Collection #707

Director Henry Hathaway transports us to the icy salmon fishing waters of Alaska in Spawn of the North, starring George Raft and Henry Fonda as childhood friends on opposite sides of a dangerous feud.

Jim Kimmerlee runs an honest salmon cannery on the Alaskan coast. When his old friend Tyler Dawson reappears after years away, the two friends are drawn toward an inevitable confrontation.

Presented with a Special Academy Award in 1939 for outstanding achievement in Special Photographic and Sound Effects, this rousing late-30s slice of Hollywood adventure also stars Dorothy Lamour (Creepshow 2), Akim Tamiroff (Touch of Evil), and a scene-stealing John Barrymore (Grand Hotel). With a score by Dimitri Tiomkin (It’s a Wonderful Life) and screenplay by Jules Furthman (Rio Bravo), this is old-school Hollywood craftsmanship on full display.

Technical Specs:

1080p High-definition presentation on Blu-ray
Audio: English LPCM 2.0 Dual Mono
Aspect Ratio 1.33:1
Optional English HOH Subtitles

Sea Devils (1953) - Imprint Collection #708

Worldwide first on Blu-ray!

A swashbuckling Technicolor adventure from director Raoul Walsh (High Sierra), Sea Devils reunites Rock Hudson and Yvonne De Carlo in a rousing tale of smugglers, spies, and Napoleonic intrigue.

In the early 1800s, fisherman-turned-smuggler Gilliatt is offered a pardon in exchange for a dangerous mission: sail to France and rescue Droucette, a beautiful British spy whose cover as a French countess has been blown. But as Gilliatt and the mysterious Droucette are thrown together across a series of increasingly perilous escapades, trust proves as treacherous as the sea itself - with Napoleon's forces closing in on all sides.

Loosely based on Victor Hugo's novel The Toilers of the Sea and shot on location in the Channel Islands and on the Brittany coast of France, this is adventure filmmaking at its most gloriously entertaining, with lavish cinematography from Wilkie Cooper (Jason and the Argonauts, The 7th Voyage of Sinbad).

Special Features and Technical Specs:

1080p High-definition presentation on Blu-ray
NEW Video essay by writer / podcaster Suzanne Boleyn
Audio: English LPCM 2.0 Mono
Aspect Ratio 1.33:1
Optional English HOH Subtitles

Hurricane Smith (1952) - Imprint Collection #709

Worldwide first on Blu-ray!

Yvonne De Carlo and John Ireland star in Hurricane Smith, a sun-drenched tale of pirates, buried treasure, and the South Seas - directed by Jerry Hopper (Secret of the Incas) and based on the novel by Gordon Ray Young.

Stranded on a Pacific island, adventurer Hurricane Smith and his two companions seize a passing slave trader's ship and set course for the South Seas in search of a fabled treasure. The beautiful Luana, however, holds the key to the treasure's location and has her own reasons for keeping it secret, prompting a round of double-crosses, shark fights, and shipboard skullduggery.

With rich Technicolor cinematography by Oscar-winner Ray Rennahan (Gone with the Wind), Hurricane Smith is glorious adventure fare and an entertaining swashbuckler.

Special Features and Technical Specs:

1080p High-definition presentation on Blu-ray
NEW Audio commentary by film historian and host of Cereal At Midnight Heath Holland
Audio: English LPCM 2.0 Mono
Aspect Ratio 1.37:1
Optional English HOH Subtitles

A Perilous Journey (1953) - Imprint Collection #710

Worldwide first on Blu-ray!

A Perilous Journey is a spirited Western adventure from Republic Pictures, directed by R.G. Springsteen and starring Vera Ralston (Fair Wind to Java), David Brian (The Damned Don’t Cry), and Scott Brady (Gremlins, Johnny Guitar).

Among the dozens of women aboard a ship bound for gold-rush California on a "barter-bride" deal is Francie Landreaux, who has her own reasons for making the voyage. She is already married to a deserter, and she intends to find him. But her search draws her into the orbit of two dangerous men with competing claims on her fate.

With a score from Oscar winner Victor Young (Shane, Around the World in 80 Days), A Perilous Journey is a lively adventure ready to surprise and delight.

text:
In Kibbutz Be’eri, the air inside a child’s bedroom was still. Behind a small bed, a doll lay where it had fallen. The wall above it was scarred with bullet holes and blood stains.

The scene needed no explanation. An Israeli girl had hidden behind her bed as Hamas terrorists rampaged through her home, clutching her doll in the dark and hoping to survive. 

But she was found and murdered for nothing more than existing.

As the father of three daughters, this room left an indelible impact on me during a post-October 7th visit to Israel. I worry about what it means that the world has largely moved on already.

The October 7 massacre revealed how quickly some will rationalize evil when the victims are Jewish. The same hatred that fuels terror against Jewish civilians in Israel does not stay contained. It spreads, adapts, and rebrands itself globally with new slogans and justifications.

Antisemitism has reemerged across the political spectrum. On the far left, it dresses up in ideological language, presenting hostility toward Jews as moral or political virtue, and often merges into the legitimization of Islamist aims.

On the far right, it has evolved too, from old nationalist branding into a foreign-amplified “groyper” rhetoric targeted at young men who feel alienated, rootless, and eager for a cause.

To comprehend why antisemitism keeps returning, one must realize what it offers — a shortcut around reason. Once hate hardens into a kind of faith, words lose their meaning, and arguments no longer need to make sense.

In the aftermath of October 7, antisemitism moved from the margins to the mainstream. 

In Virginia, Jewish students were prevented from walking on sidewalks at UVa. Outside agitators tried to occupy the VCU campus. At George Mason, antisemitic threats led to law enforcement intervention.

After returning home from Israel, the first image I saw on TV at the airport was of American students chanting pro-terror slogans.

Virginia had a duty to act, and we did so quickly. Our efforts were rooted in an understanding that the fight against contemporary antisemitism requires a multi-faceted strategy, spanning policy, law enforcement, and education, with a focus on concrete steps to prevent violence before it occurs.

We prioritized training for law enforcement. Hundreds of VSP officers have participated in antisemitism awareness seminars, facilitated by @CombatASemitism, where they learned to identify and counter extremist threats, resulting in real-world outcomes that have made our communities safer.

We focused on maintaining order on campuses, meeting with the general counsels of every public higher education institution to help them navigate First Amendment questions while ensuring schools had increased security and resources. Working with law enforcement agencies and university leaders, we proactively prepared for the unrest seen in other states before it arrived in Virginia.

We ensured families and students understood their rights, providing clear guidance on how to report and file formal complaints when antisemitic discrimination occurs. 

For elementary, middle, and high schools, we developed a curriculum module about Jewish religion, culture, and history to counter distorted narratives that frequently circulate.

In 2025, we became involved in a case where three young Jewish siblings were expelled after their parents complained about antisemitic harassment one child suffered at school. The eventual settlement saw the school agree to implement a new nondiscrimination policy, including adopting the IHRA Working Definition of Antisemitism.

Reflecting on my term as attorney general, I remember that child’s room in Be’eri and the abandoned doll. It strengthens my resolve to refuse the world’s excuses and insist on better. 

As Americans, we must be clear-eyed about what antisemitism is, honest about how it proliferates, and unafraid to counter it wherever it appears. That is what this moment in history calls for.

🇺🇸🇷🇺 The United States has formally demanded more information from Russia about the death of an employee at a plague research institute.

According to The Washington Post, Washington is preparing a diplomatic démarche reminding Moscow of its international obligations to promptly share information about potential outbreaks of infectious diseases.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Russia “obviously has an obligation to share more information with the world.” U.S. State Department health officials reportedly contacted the Russian Foreign Ministry on October 2.

President Donald Trump also expressed concern about reports of plague in Russia, calling the situation a “big problem” and saying the United States could potentially offer assistance. He also said he planned to discuss the issue with Vladimir Putin.

The concern follows the death of 27-year-old Daria Shipilova, an employee of an anti-plague institute in Siberia. Reports have offered conflicting explanations: one says she had recently returned from Buryatia, near an area where plague cases had been detected; another claims she accidentally broke a vial containing a dangerous bacterium in a laboratory.

After her death, a hospital in Shelekhov was reportedly quarantined and 189 contacts were hospitalized for observation. Russian authorities say none showed symptoms and described Shipilova’s illness as “pneumonia of unknown etiology.”

U.S. officials cited by CNN say Washington remains concerned because it still lacks clear information about what actually happened.

text:
A ballot still arriving years after you moved is a registration-records problem, not fraud by itself. Fraud would be someone completing and returning that ballot, or you voting in California after you no longer live there. An unused ballot in the wrong mailbox is an error.

Mail ballots can be misused, which is why both parties have warned about them. That is a risk, not a count of crimes. Proven cases are uncommon relative to ballots cast.

The Heritage Foundation, a conservative think tank, keeps a database of convictions and official findings. It is a sampling, not a full census. As of Dec. 2025 it listed 1,619 cases of all types of election fraud from 1982 on. Absentee-ballot cases are the largest category there, on the order of a few hundred across those decades. Analyses of Heritage’s mail cases for the 2016–2022 general elections put detected fraud around four cases per ten million mail ballots. That counts proven cases, not every attempt.

“Almost all democracies ban them for that reason” overstates it. International IDEA counts about 32 countries that allow in-country postal voting, including Canada, Germany, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, and New Zealand for all voters. Many other countries do not offer it domestically.

text:
A 54 year old unemployed man from New Jersey, out of work for 15 years, bought two Mega Millions tickets, got distracted by his phone and walked out of the shop without them. He went back the next day, got them back from the store, and one of them was worth $273 MILLION. He said he wouldn't have it if it wasn't for the honest person who handed them in.

> Mike Weirsky is a 54 year old from Alpha, New Jersey.

> He spent the last 15 years unemployed while his wife worked. They divorced in October 2018.

> He said he was being offered jobs paying $8 to $10 an hour at 54.

> He spent about $20 a week on mostly quick-pick lottery tickets.

> On Thursday February 28 2019 he bought two $2 Mega Millions tickets at a QuickChek in Phillipsburg, near the Pennsylvania border.

> He put the tickets down to put his money away, started doing something on his phone and walked out without them. He called it "the typical cellphone deal."

> He assumed they were gone for good.

> Someone had found the tickets and handed them in, and the store held them for him.

> He went back on Friday, proved they were his, and the employees gave them back.

> The Mega Millions drawing was that night.

> The winning numbers were 29, 33, 39, 60, 66 and Mega Ball 21.

> He didn't check the tickets until Sunday. The New Jersey Lottery said he went out in a snowstorm to scan one.

> It said he was the jackpot winner. He sat down and told his mother he had won 273 million dollars. She asked what that meant.

> Lottery officials later said that if the person who found the tickets had signed them, they could have claimed the jackpot.

> He chose the lump sum of $162.5 million before taxes.

> The QuickChek received $30,000 for selling the winning ticket.

> The New Jersey Lottery announced his win at a press conference in Trenton on Thursday March 7 2019.

> He said he was looking for the person who handed in the tickets. He said he would give them something but keep it private.

> He said he wouldn't have the money if the finder had kept it, and that anyone that honest was good enough for him.

> He said he had met with a lawyer and a financial adviser, and that once they said he could, he would "go crazy."

> His first purchase would be a Ford Raptor pickup truck.

> He also planned to buy his mother a new car, remodel her house and take his family on holiday.

> He said he wanted to be able to wake up and decide to go somewhere, then just do it.

> That same week his ex-wife got in touch to say she was taking him back to court.

> He also got his first job interview request in months, and turned it down.

A man who hadn't worked in 15 years left two lottery tickets on a shop counter because of his phone, went back the next day, found they'd been handed in, didn't check them until Sunday, and told his mum he'd won $273 MILLION.

THE PUBLIC NUMBERS AND THE PRIVATE NUMBERS TELL COMPLETELY DIFFERENT STORIES.

🔥 TRAFFIC ISN'T THE SAME AS CUSTOMERS.

KNOWING THE DIFFERENCE CAN SAVE YOU YEARS.

I have a Honda and could say the same thing about their service department in Columbus, OH. I had a brand new van with an insanely loud squeaking seat. It was especially annoying on road trips when the kids were sleeping because the squeaking would wake them up…we bought the van for comfortable road trips.

They replaced part after part without fixing it. Honestly, I don’t believe the service technicians were being told what problem they were supposed to be fixing. Three different times they told me it was fixed, I’d show up to pick up the van, give the seat a wiggle, and immediately hear the same loud squeaking.

During all of this, they ripped the leather on my seat and weren’t even going to disclose it. I noticed it myself and had to make them replace it. Then they installed the replacement incorrectly, which resulted in even more parts having to be ordered.

They had my van for SEVEN WEEKS, and after all of that, the seat still squeaks. I finally gave up because I was more worried about them causing additional damage, and I needed my van back.

I love Honda vehicles, but I won’t buy another one here because the service department is so incompetent. A warranty doesn’t offer much protection when you can’t trust the dealership to actually repair the vehicle without creating additional problems. At that point, service itself becomes a risk.

text:
HOW TO SUCCEED WITH NOTHING 

Brother to Brother:
Nobody is coming to rescue you.
No mentor.
No investor.
No friend secretly planning to change your life.
When things get hard,
most times it will just be you
facing the pressure alone.

And truthfully,
this is where most men give up.
But the men who survive this stage
usually become the men nobody can ignore later.
Because there is something powerful about a man
who learned how to build without depending on anyone.

Here is how to win when you have nobody.

1. Accept that you are alone, and use it.

Stop waiting for support that may never come.
The moment you accept that nobody is coming to save you,
you stop wasting energy looking around for permission.

No support means no masters.
Nobody to report to.
Nobody to impress.
Nobody whose opinion can delay your next move.

Every step forward becomes fully yours.
Every win carries your name on it.
That is not a curse.
That is freedom in its rawest form.

Use it.

2. Move in silence.

Stop announcing everything you want to build.
Not every idea needs an audience.

Every time you talk too early,
you spend energy that should have gone into execution.

And most people will not fuel your vision.
They will question it.
They will project their fears onto it.
They will remind you why it may not work.

Protect your vision while it is still growing.
Go quiet.
Work silently.
Let results do the introduction for you.

3. Become your own mentor.

Nobody is coming to hand you the blueprint.
So study.
Learn.
Teach yourself.

Read the books.
Watch the lessons.
Ask yourself the hard questions.
Hold yourself accountable.

You must become both the coach and the player.
The one who pushes
and the one who refuses to quit.

Because at this stage of your life,
excuses are expensive.

4. Turn the pain into power.

The loneliness is real.
The rejection is real.
The feeling that nobody sees your effort is real.

But do not waste that pain.
Use it.

Do not distract yourself from it.
Do not bury it in scrolling, partying, or excuses.

Channel it into the work.

Most strong men were built in seasons nobody clapped for.
The people who eventually become unstoppable
are usually the ones who had the most to prove.

Use your pain as fuel.
Not as weakness.

5. Build a strict daily system and obey it.

Without discipline,
dreams collapse.

No boss is coming to monitor you.
No team is coming to push you.

You are the structure.

Wake up with intention.
Win the morning before emotions wake up.
Work in focused blocks.
Feed your mind with things that sharpen you.

And every night,
review your day honestly.

Where did you waste time?
What did you avoid?
What must improve tomorrow?

That daily self-audit
is one of the highest forms of growth.

Do not skip it.

6. Stop chasing people. Become valuable.

Networking without value changes nothing.

If you have nothing solid to offer,
all you will collect are contacts that lead nowhere.

Instead of chasing attention,
build something undeniable.

Build skill.
Build value.
Build substance.

Become so good,
so useful,
so excellent at what you do,
that the right people naturally find you.

A magnet does not chase metal.
It becomes magnetic.

Become magnetic.

The man who succeeds alone
builds more than money.

He builds confidence.
He builds resilience.
He builds the unshakable belief
that he can survive hard seasons and still win.

That kind of belief cannot be borrowed.
Cannot be gifted.
Cannot be faked.

It is earned quietly.
In the struggle.
In the unseen days
when nobody was clapping
but you kept showing up anyway.

That man is you.

Keep going.

text:
A message from Cardus Senior Fellow, the Rev. Dr. Andrew Bennett, and Cardus's President, Canada, @BrianDijkema, on the anniversary of the October 7 attacks and the relaunching of the Canadian Christian Declaration on Antisemitism. (Add your name at https://t.co/h5fVaikeQZ).

***

Three years ago, over 700 Christian clergy and lay leaders declared that they stood side by side in solidarity with our Jewish cousins as fellow citizens of this great country of Canada. 

We did so after the Jewish people had experienced a terrorist attack that resulted in the greatest number of deaths and murders since the Holocaust. Our intent was to show solidarity with our Jewish neighbours in Canada, and to show them that Christians stood beside them, that they were loved, and that we offered friendship, comfort, and support. We did so out of theological convictions grounded in the universal and objective goods of human dignity, justice, and freedom.
 
However, since we released our first declaration, we have not seen a widespread expression of solidarity and support for the Canadian Jewish community in our country. Indeed, we have seen the opposite of solidarity in Canada; we have seen a renewed outbreak of an even more assertive, and virulent, strain of antisemitism expressed across the country. 
 
The major institutions that should be expressing solidarity—our governments, many educational institutions, trade unions, and more— turn away from solidarity with the Jewish people, and, in fact, express and show hatred towards them or aid and abet those who showed hatred. 
 
Our governments have spoken sweet words, but have failed to take the necessary steps to protect Jewish citizens, business owners, athletes, academics, teachers, and others from harassment, threats, and actual violence. Indeed, their lack of clarity and specificity has emboldened those who wish to harm Jews in Canada.
 
Despite being one percent of Canada’s total population, Jews have been on the receiving end of an ever-increasing number of hate crimes. Jewish congregations and Jewish institutions—from synagogues to schools and businesses—must navigate security to simply go about their daily lives. 
 
Educational institutions that ought to focus on truth and which should provide the peace that is necessary for learning have instead perpetrated lies and allowed hatred to take place on campuses, in classrooms, and even among teachers. 
 
Trade unions, whose very role it is to show solidarity for all workers despite race or religion, have either turned a blind eye or actively encouraged antisemitism within their structures. 
 
Media have failed to tell the truth and failed to provide clarity, thus providing an informational fog that provides cover for acts of violence, threats, and belittling of our Jewish neighbours. 
 
Three years on from the horrors that took place, Jews in Canada, instead of feeling safer and more secure, feel less secure, feel less safe, and feel more isolated and alone.  
 
And so, as Christians, we declare again, and we call on Christians across the country to declare with their signature, that we continue to stand with Canada’s Jewish community. 
 
We will continue to stand side by side with you and to speak clearly and openly about the need—across all of Canada’s institutions—to make Canada a place where Jews are not just welcome, but where they are safe to live, worship, raise their families, and continue the great tradition of outsized contribution to this country that we have seen since this country began.
 
For those who signed during our previous reach-out, thank you. We have a different request for you. Can you send this to three friends who would sign this declaration?
 
We repeat that this is not a geopolitical statement; it is a theological declaration grounded in the universal and objective goods of human dignity, justice, and freedom. And it recognizes that these goods must be instantiated in Canadian society. 
 
Let us continue to stand with Canadian Jews in these days. In particular, today would be a great day to reach out to any Jewish persons you know and ask them sincerely: how are you doing? Too few people did this in the wake of October 7, and it remains important we do so even as the anniversary moves further into the distance.
 
Because what was unleashed that day is still with us now. But it doesn't have to be that way. Stand with us.
 
May God bless us and guide us in this noble endeavour.
 
In Christ,
 
Rev. Dr. Andrew P.W. Bennett
Canadian Ambassador of Religious Freedom, 2013-2016
 
Brian Dijkema
Cardus’ President, Canada

text:
🔸 October 7 – Saints Bacchus and Sergius 🗡️🔸

Today, we commemorate the Holy Martyrs Saints Bacchus and Sergius. These military saints suffered for Christ during the persecutions of the late third century. Saints Bacchus and Sergius lived during the reign of Emperor Maximian in the year 296, and both were from Rome. Finding favor with the emperor - even while they lived as Christians in secret - they were appointed to high ranking military positions.

When envious people informed the emperor that his two trusted counsellors did not honor the pagan gods, Maximian summoned them, wanting to see the truth of this accusation. He ordered Bacchus and Sergius to offer sacrifices to the idols, but they boldly confessed that they only worshiped the One True God Jesus Christ. The infuriated Maximian commanded that the martyrs be stripped of their military insignia, and to humiliate them further, he had them dressed in feminine clothing and chained by their necks, parading them around the marketplace.

The emperor then commanded that they be sent to the governor of the eastern part of Syria, Antiochus, a fierce hater and torturer of Christians. When the Saints stood before him, they were not overcome, neither by the flatteries nor by the threats of the tyrant. For this reason, St Sergius was sent to a prison cell, while St Bacchus was beaten mercilessly with raw ox-hide.

After suffering hours of beatings, St Bacchus finally delivered his soul to the Lord. St Sergius was then taken out of his cell to be tortured. His feet were nailed into iron shoes, and wearing these he was forced to run great distances while his feet bled profusely. Finally, St Sergius received his crown of martyrdom by beheading. Not long after their martyrdom, Christianity was legalized and promulgated in the Roman Empire by the Emperor St Constantine the Great.

By the 5th century, Saints Bacchus and Sergius had become venerated as protectors of the Byzantine army. A church was dedicated to them in Constantinople in 527 AD by the Emperor St Justinian the Great. This church was converted to a mosque after the Fall of Constantinople, and is today known as the “Little Hagia Sophia”.

text:
✝️ God Begins to Fulfill His Promises

1. God always keeps His promises. No matter how impossible it seems, or how long it may take, every one of His promises will come true.

2. God gave a son to Zacharias and Elisabeth, even though they were very old. They named him John, as God had told them. (Lk. 1:57)

3. Zacharias believed in God’s promise to send a Savior, Who would save the world from the power of sin and Satan. The Spirit of God told him that the Savior would come very soon. The promised “seed of the woman”, the “seed of Abraham”, was about to be born. John would be the prophet to prepare the way for the coming of the Savior, “the Lord”. (Lk. 1:67-79, Gen. 3:15, Gen. 12:3)

4. God Himself is the great Savior. He saved Noah from the flood, Isaac from the sacrifice, Lot from Sodom, and Joseph from prison. He saved Israel from slavery in Egypt, from Pharaoh’s army at the Red Sea, and from death in the wilderness. (Is. 43:11)

5. People like to think that they are strong, wise, and in control. Satan wants us to be confident in ourselves. The unpleasant truth is that we are all sinners, hopelessly lost and unable to save ourselves. We are condemned to everlasting punishment in Hell. We need a Savior that will rescue us from our sin.

6. Zacharias prophesied that the Savior would come as the sunrise to us, who are in darkness, and would guide us to the way of peace and forgiveness of sin. He would give us the light so that we could see the way of Salvation. When you are lost, the light can show you where you are, and which way you need to go. Just as there is only one sun, there is only one Savior. (Lk. 1:77-79)

7. John lived in the desert until it was time for him to begin preaching. He was a sinful man, but he believed God, and trusted in the promise of a coming savior. It would be his job to tell the people that the Savior had finally come. (Lk. 1:80)

8. Jesus, the coming Savior, had to meet many qualifications in order to fulfill all the promises that God had made for 4000 years. He had to be a descendant of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and David. 
He had to fit all the descriptions of the prophets.

9. Many of the prophecies in the Old Testament had double meanings. They were talking about something that happened back then, but they also had a message about something that would happen in the future. Often it was not clear exactly what would happen, but after it happened, you could clearly see how God had foretold it in the prophecies. Sometimes the prophets themselves did not completely understand what they were writing about. They just wrote the words that God gave them. (1Pet. 1:10-12)

10. Hundreds of years before Jesus was born, the prophets told many things about what He would be like, what He would do, and what would happen to Him. Every one of these details came to pass.

11. Jesus is also called “the Christ”, which means “the anointed One”. This means He was specially chosen by God to perform a certain mission. Another form of this same name is “the Messiah”.

12. As the Messiah, Jesus has three special roles in God’s plan of salvation. He is a prophet, who came to tell us the way of Salvation from sin, Satan, and Hell. He is a priest, who offered the blood of the sacrifice as a payment for sin. He is a king, who will someday rule over all the nations of the world.

Envious people informed Maximian that his two trusted counsellors did not honor the pagan gods. This was considered to be a crime against the state.

The saints refuted the emperor’s words, and demonstrated the folly of worshiping the pagan gods.

The emperor commanded that they be sent to the governor of the eastern part of Syria, Antiochus, a fierce hater of Christians. Antiochus had received his position with the help of Sergius and Bacchus. “My fathers and benefactors!” he said. “Have pity on yourselves, and also on me. I do not want to condemn my benefactors to cruel tortures.” The holy martyrs replied, “For us life is Christ, and to die is gain.” The enraged Antiochus ordered Bacchus to be mercilessly beaten, and the holy martyr surrendered his soul to the Lord.
