text:
Podcast Summary | Candace: CAUGHT! Eastern Europe, Erika Kirk, And The SHOCKING Truth Behind TPUSA’S “ANTI-CANDACE” Campaigns.

Overview
Candace Owens alleges a coordinated, funded smear and clipping operation designed to attack her and elevate Erika Kirk, linking it to Turning Point USA, a Latvian-run clipping network, a Las Vegas marketing company, and even a federal employee. The central claim is that what looks like spontaneous conservative grassroots enthusiasm is actually paid astroturfing, organized through Discord, Google Drive, and platforms that pay editors by impressions. Owens argues the operation targeted her during the Tyler Robinson preliminary hearing week, while her show was off air, and that it intensified after her debate with Andrew Wilson. She frames the campaign as a betrayal of Charlie Kirk, a manipulation of his legacy, and a broader machine that rewrites narratives, controls sponsors, and buries inconvenient questions.

Key Themes
- Owens alleges a coordinated, funded attack on her during the Tyler Robinson preliminary hearing week, involving government and PR intermediaries rather than organic critics.
- Jennica Pounds, known as Data Republican, was hired by the Department of War as a special government employee in July and then posted a long X thread attacking Owens while defending the official Tyler Robinson narrative.
- Claims that critics are not paid to attack Owens are technically misleading, since money can flow through PR firms or platforms while keeping direct sponsors’ hands clean.
- A bounty system allegedly offered millions for anti-Candace videos, orchestrated through Discord and a company doing business as Clipit or Monster Lab.
- Monster Lab and Clipit run impression-based campaigns, and an Elephant Clipping campaign explicitly prohibited clipping Candace Owens while allowing only approved Turning Point USA affiliates or Charlie Kirk associates.
- The operation shifted to clipping Andrew Wilson to make him and Turning Point USA look good, paying a seventy-five-thousand-dollar pool for one week after Owens debated Wilson on August 14.
- A hidden paid clipping network uses editors in Eastern Europe and the global south to manufacture viral conservative content that looks spontaneous, a form of astroturfing.
- Discord records and Google Drive files tie the Turning Point USA clipping campaign to a folder mostly containing Erika Kirk videos uploaded September 15, 2025, five days after Charlie Kirk’s assassination.
- Turning Point USA publicly denied involvement and said it did not know the clipping company, despite reported Discord evidence suggesting otherwise.

Detailed Summary
Owens says email tips claimed one point five million dollars was offered to make anti-Candace videos during the Tyler Robinson preliminary hearing week. A leaked campaign offered one hundred twenty thousand dollars for the month, paying three hundred dollars per one million views, running August 3 through 31, for Charlie Kirk clips. It stated that participants could not clip Candace Owens and only approved Turning Point USA affiliates or Charlie Kirk’s close associates.

After Owens debated Andrew Wilson on August 14, the campaign instructions changed. The focus shifted to clipping Andrew Wilson to make him look good, with a seventy-five-thousand-dollar pool for one week. The campaign reportedly complained that participants kept posting old Charlie Kirk or Turning Point USA debate clips, which were disallowed through August 23. Owens could appear only where she looked bad and Turning Point looked good, and other portrayals would be rejected.

Owens claims the anti-Candace attacks occurred while her show was off air for two weeks while she was in Spain, and she describes them as coordinated and over the top. She dismisses Pounds as a fraud for not disclosing her Department of War employment while presenting as an independent investigator. Pounds announced her resignation from the Department of War, citing a book tour and midterms analysis, and said she was disappointed by how special government employees were treated.

The person running Monster Lab and Clipit is described as Matt Servious from Latvia. The Elephant Clipping channel is described as the main political campaign channel for anti-Candace campaigns. An Atlantic article titled Inside a Conservative Operation to Hijack Your Social Media Feed, by Ali Breeland, describes paid clippers, many from Eastern Europe and the global south, chopping company-provided videos into short clips intended to go viral.

The article links the campaign to Matt Servius and a Latvian-run operation with subcontractors in poorer countries, often outside the United States. Servius reportedly said in April that the campaign had been running about a year, placing its start around September 2025. The article reports other linked conservative clipping campaigns with budgets of nine hundred thousand dollars, including campaigns in February, March, and April. A later August campaign had a one hundred twenty thousand dollar budget and instructed clippers to use videos from the Turning Point USA YouTube channel.

A Turning Point USA spokesman, Andrew Kovat, said he could pretty much guarantee the nonprofit was not working with the Latvian company and that its contractors were unfamiliar with it. Google Drive folders in the campaigns appeared to contain files uploaded by three people affiliated with Enclave and Key, a Las Vegas marketing company: Jules Katz, Benjamin Goodman, and Jack O’Hara. Enclave and Key’s CEO and founder is identified as Blake Wyn, the twenty-six-year-old nephew of billionaire conservative donor Steve Wyn.

Files appeared uploaded via Enclave and Key company email addresses, and in at least one instance O’Hara also appeared to use a personal email address. Enclave and Key stated it is an American company engaged in a routine, long-standing, lawful practice and disputed the article’s characterization. Blake Wyn responded to questions by saying there were a number of inaccuracies but declined further clarification.

Blake Wyn was present with Erika Kirk at events including the White House Presidential Medal of Freedom event on October 14, Turning Point USA’s annual winter gala, and the opening of Club America in Little Rock, Arkansas on March 11, 2026. In a podcast appearance, Blake Wyn said Erika Kirk fits into a rare bucket of people he looks up to as human beings and described their friendship as developing over a couple months. The speaker explicitly says they do not believe Blake Wyn and Erika Kirk are in a romantic relationship, describing it as a business relationship.

Files were reportedly uploaded September 15 with footprints to Blake, Las Vegas, and Eastern Europe. After outreach to the Wyns and others involved, campaign materials began disappearing. By Thursday afternoon, video folders uploaded by Katz and O’Hara disappeared. The same files were then posted by Goodman using an email address not linked to Enclave and Key. Discord channels for US politics clipping and elephant clipping were delisted from publicly visible campaigns. Campaigns remained on Monster Lab but descriptions explaining their purpose were removed. By Friday morning, Enclave and Key Google Drives for the campaigns were taken down.

In a November 2025 interview on the podcast Bring the Juice, Blake Wyn said he and Enclave and Key do a lot of work in politics, that he regularly speaks with FBI director Cash Patel, and that he was good friends with Kirk. Blake Wyn recounted sitting next to Trump at Mar-a-Lago on election night in 2024 alongside Elon Musk, UFC CEO Dana White, and Steve Witkoff. He has posted Instagram photos at small gatherings, the White House, and Mar-a-Lago alongside the Kirks and Tulsi Gabbard.

Elephant Clipping banned clippers from posting videos of Megan Kelly, Nick Fuentes, Tucker Carlson, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and Riley Gaines, among others. Banned subjects included the January 6, 2021 attack on the Capitol and cryptocurrencies promoted by members of the Trump family. Clippers were barred from posting videos of Candace Owens. Two sub-campaigns in the Discord offered extra money for clippers to post favorable videos about Vivek Ramaswamy, a GOP candidate for Ohio governor, and Tulsi Gabbard.

Enclave and Key also manages clipping campaigns for Ben Shapiro and Steven Crowder, both listed on Monster Lab with thirty-thousand-dollar budgets for last month. Crowder’s campaign also links to an Enclave and Key-connected Google Drive. Neither Shapiro nor Crowder responded to requests for comment. The speaker notes an Enclave and Key footprint in Romania.

Owens says Monster Labs and Clip It used ChatGPT and paid people across countries for impressions. She cites a million impressions for three hundred bucks. She states the site was a splash page on May 3, 2024 and August 3, 2025, then active by September 15, 2025 for Erika Kirk. She says early Wayback captures from September 12, 2025 show only loading, which she has never seen before. She suspects Erika Kirk may have been the first campaign on the site, but explicitly labels this a feeling or dream, not a fact.

Owens alleges Ben Shapiro is paid thirty thousand dollars a month on the platform. She says Steven Crowder snuck in his producer to back up Andrew Wilson and did not disclose who was coming to her house. She names Matt as running the campaign and references a Latvian guy running clipping campaigns. She says the company’s terms and about section only lists trade names Monster Lab and Clip It, and LLC docs have not revealed who is at the top.

She names people allegedly involved or promoted in the campaign, including Tulsi Gabbard, Ben Shapiro, Steven Crowder, Vivek Ramaswamy, President Trump, and JD Vance. She alleges Andrew Kovac put one million dollars against Candace and pro-Erika during the week. She claims Department of Defense people are attacking Candace and calls it gaslighting. She references Miriam Adelson purchasing the presidency and says it cost three hundred million dollars. She says RFK cannot be clipped because of big pharma wealth and cross-contamination with Adelson and methadone interests.

She compares the situation to the Mormon mafia around Howard Hughes and says all roads run into a Las Vegas syndicate. She says Blake Wynn is connected and that his employees had Google server clips of Erika ready on September 15. She says Cash Patel is from Las Vegas and is friends with these people, and recalls him wanting to stop archive websites. She says she wants to know who sits at the top of the chain. She mentions Andrew Tate built Hustlers University around clipping and that people discussed stealing it.

Andrew Tate created Hustlers University in 2021, instructing members to clip his livestreams, post them from related accounts, add affiliate links, and earn commissions for signups. Tate’s clips reportedly reached billions of views on TikTok through many accounts, not just his own. Tate was later banned from TikTok, and the speaker says his clips continued via a clipping army. Nick Fuentes is cited as another banned figure who remains visible on Instagram through clippers reposting his content.

The speaker says Erika Kirk was CEO and chairman by September 12, and https://t.co/gY4oaYiFv0 was also purchased on September 12, though the purchaser is unknown. The speaker questions whether Erika Kirk knew about the site, given her roles and political ambitions. The speaker says Turning Point USA was in cahoots with the effort, citing private planes and promotion of Erika. A commenter’s question is cited about a fire captain performing CPR on a corpse deceased for fifteen minutes in a fire truck to a hospital ER. The speaker says the hospital seemingly knew someone was coming because audio and chats show redirection to Teenagos or Tonogos. The speaker notes Wayback Machine allegedly malfunctioning for September 12 archives, calling it a cleaning up of the tracks. The speaker asks who sponsored the Latvian and who is doing the clip work, calling it significant. The speaker claims to have never taken a single dollar from Turning Point USA.

Owens alleges the September 12 archive was wiped to hide which campaign was live that day, framing it as a cover-up of tracks tied to the Charlie Kirk investigation. text:
#Space #Cosmos
 'Completely unexpected': Astronomers spy never-before-seen 'phoenix planet' rising from the ashes of a dead star  https://t.co/z6gHfSEnqm 

Astronomers have spotted a never-before-seen type of "phoenix planet" rising from the ashes of a dying alien sun. The discovery, which the scientists say was "completely unexpected," raises hopes that more of these reborn alien worlds could be lurking throughout the cosmos — and may offer a glimpse of our own solar system's fate. 

The unnamed exoplanet was spotted circling the white dwarf HS 0209+0832, which is located roughly 270 light-years from Earth. White dwarfs are stellar remnants, sometimes dubbed "zombie stars," that form from the leftovers of massive red giants that run out of fuel before eventually collapsing into shriveled husks. HS 0209+0832 is a particularly young white dwarf, still burning at around 63,000 degrees Fahrenheit (35,000 degrees Celsius), which suggests it made this transition within the past few million years.

Scientists previously discovered some surprising heavy elements within the visible spectrum of HS 0209+0832, which was first captured by the Hubble Space Telescope in the late 1990s. These elements — which included aluminium, titanium and nickel — are not normally found inside white dwarfs, so their presence suggested that something unusual was going on. But until now, there was not enough data to figure out what. 

In the new study, published Oct. 5 in the journal Nature Astronomy, researchers took a closer look at HS 0209+0832. Using some of Hubble's updated instruments and data from other observatories, the team captured a more detailed spectrum of the stellar zombie. This revealed a high concentration of additional heavy elements, including zinc and copper, as well as niobium, which has never been seen in a white dwarf before.

The researchers think these out-of-place elements were created during the death throes of the former red giant and later coalesced into a "second-generation" planet around the newly forged white dwarf. They suspect the atmosphere of this hypothetical planet is being stripped by the white dwarf's stellar winds, causing the rare elements to fall back onto the zombie star. 

HS 0209+0832 was once a main-sequence star like the sun (top left) that ballooned into a red giant after it ran out of fuel (top right). Eventually, it collapsed into a white dwarf (bottom left), before an exoplanet emerged from the ashes of the red giant (bottom right).  (Image credit: NASA, ESA, L. Hustak (STScI))

Follow-up observations then revealed a recurring dip in the brightness of HS 0209+0832, suggesting that an exoplanet was repeatedly passing in front of the undead star. Based on the alien world's orbit, which lasts approximately 4.4 Earth days, and the duration of its transits in front of the star, the team predicted that the planet is roughly the size of Jupiter. (Its close proximity to the white dwarf also supports the hypothesis that its atmosphere is being stripped away.)  

"Second-generation planets are worlds that form out of the material a star casts off as it dies," study first author Jamie Williams, a doctoral candidate in astronomy and astrophysics at the University of Warwick in the U.K., said in a statement. "They're incredibly rare, and finding one around a white dwarf was completely unexpected. It's a bit like finding a planet that has risen from the ashes of the very star it once orbited."

"Completely unexpected"

This is not the first time astronomers have spotted an exoplanet around a white dwarf. For example, in 2019, some of the authors of the new study previously spotted an alien world surrounding the white dwarf WDJ0914+1914. However, in that case, they were confident that it was a first-generation world that somehow survived its star's fiery end.

But the heavy elements that seem to be falling onto HS 0209+0832 — and the relative lack of other elements common in first-generation planets, such as silicon and iron — suggest that's not what's happened for this recently detected world.

"This pattern of elements is a telltale sign of the 's-process,' a nuclear reaction that builds heavy elements inside dying stars during their bloated red giant phase," study co-author Nicholas Stone, an astronomer at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, said in the statement. "It's a chemical signature no ordinary, 'first-generation' planet should carry, which told us that this new planet was something different."

The elements in HS 0209+0832's visible spectra, strongly suggested that it was accreting material from a second-generation exoplanet. The transit data later confirmed this theory.  (Image credit: Illustration: NASA, ESA, Leah Hustak (STScI))

Instead, the newly detected exoplanet likely formed directly from the material that was shed by the dying red giant after it expanded and before it collapsed in on itself.

Similar phoenix planets have been spotted alongside other stellar remnants, such as pulsars, which form when stars explode as supernovas. However, until now, such worlds have never been seen around a white dwarf. 

Rising from the ashes   

"What's remarkable about the planet around HS 0209+0832 is that this isn't a planet from somewhere else, or a survivor from the system's birth, it looks like it was built from the very material its own star cast off as it died," study co-author Boris Gänsicke, an astrophysicist at the University of Warwick who also helped to discover the exoplanet around WDJ0914+1914 in 2019, said in the statement. "In a sense, this system has given birth to a new world using the foundations of the old one."

HS 0209+0832 may have once harbored other exoplanets when it was a red giant. But if they existed, these alien worlds likely perished in flames as the dying star ballooned — similar to what experts think will happen to Earth when the sun runs out of fuel and transitions into a red giant in around 5 billion years.

HS 0209+0832's exoplanet likely has very little to no atmosphere left due to strong gusts of stellar wind stripping it away.  (Image credit: Dr Snehalata Sahu/University of Warwick)

Once the sun has finished bulging, it will turn into a white dwarf too. The new discovery hints that our star could also host brand-new worlds after it has transformed, creating a sort of solar system 2.0.

RELATED STORIES

Scientists identify 10,000 'impossible' exoplanet candidates, potentially tripling the number of known alien worlds

A giant cosmic 'fart' is making a wobbling zombie star repeatedly flash us, 'groundbreaking' observations reveal

"Finding this one example raises the question of how many more might be out there and might our own solar system host a second-generation planet formed from the ashes of our sun," Gänsicke said.

However, more work is required to figure out exactly how the newfound exoplanet formed and, as a result, how likely this scenario is. The researchers suspect that another object, such as a lost stellar sibling, may have been required to create the new world.

"Forming the protoplanetary disc in this situation is not easy and helps explain why these planets are so rare," Williams said. "To form a disc of material necessary to birth a planet, HS 0209+0832 likely required a companion star that pulled the ejected material back into orbit, rather than letting it escape."

                          Harry Baker

text:
The British Union of Fascists (BUF) was a British fascist political party formed in 1932 by Oswald Mosley. In 1937 it changed its name to the British Union. In 1939, following the start of the Second World War, the party was proscribed by the British government and in 1940 it was disbanded.The BUF emerged in 1932 from the electoral defeat of its antecedent, the New Party, in the 1931 general election. The BUF's foundation was initially met with popular support, and it attracted a sizeable following, with the party claiming 50,000 members at one point. The press baron Lord Rothermere was a notable early supporter. As the party became increasingly radical, however, support declined. The Olympia Rally of 1934, in which a number of anti-fascist protestors were attacked by the paramilitary wing of the BUF, the Fascist Defence Force, isolated the party from much of its following. The party's embrace of Nazi-style antisemitism in 1936 led to increasingly violent confrontations with anti-fascists, notably the 1936 Battle of Cable Street in London's East End. The Public Order Act 1936, which banned political uniforms and responded to increasing political violence, had a particularly strong effect on the BUF whose supporters were known as "Blackshirts" after the uniforms they wore.Growing British hostility towards Nazi Germany, with which the British press persistently associated the BUF, further contributed to the decline of the movement's membership. The party was finally banned by the British government on 23 May 1940 after the start of the Second World War, amid suspicion that its remaining supporters might form a pro-Nazi "fifth column". A number of prominent BUF members were arrested and interned under Defence Regulation 18B.

History

Background
📷Flowchart showing the history of the early British fascist movement
Oswald Mosley was the youngest elected Conservative MP before crossing the floor in 1922, joining first Labour and, shortly afterward, the Independent Labour Party. He became Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster in Ramsay MacDonald's Labour government, advising on rising unemployment.[27]In 1930, Mosley issued his Mosley Memorandum, which fused protectionism with a proto-Keynesian programme of policies designed to tackle the problem of unemployment, and he resigned from the Labour Party soon after, in early 1931, when the plans were rejected. He immediately formed the New Party, with policies based on his memorandum. The party won 16% of the vote at a by-election in Ashton-under-Lyne in early 1931; however, it failed to achieve any other electoral success.[28]During 1931, the New Party became increasingly influenced by fascism.[29] The following year, after a January 1932 visit to Benito Mussolini in Italy, Mosley's own conversion to fascism was confirmed. He wound up the New Party in April, but preserved its youth movement, which would form the core of the BUF, intact. He spent the summer that year writing a fascist programme, The Greater Britain, and this formed the basis of policy of the BUF, which was launched on 1 October 1932[29] at 12 Great George Street in London.[30]
Early success and growth
📷The Olympia Exhibition Centre in London, site of the party's 1934 rally sometimes cited as the beginning of the movement's decline
📷Italy's Duce Benito Mussolini (left) with BUF leader Oswald Mosley (right) during Mosley's visit to Italy in April 1933
The BUF claimed 50,000 members at one point,[31] and the Daily Mail, running the headline "Hurrah for the Blackshirts!", was an early supporter.[32] The first Director of Propaganda, appointed in February 1933, was Wilfred Risdon, who was responsible for organising all of Mosley's public meetings. Despite strong resistance from anti-fascists, including the local Jewish community, the Labour Party, the Independent Labour Party and the Communist Party of Great Britain, the BUF found a following in the East End of London, where in the London County Council elections of March 1937, it obtained reasonably successful results in Bethnal Green, Shoreditch and Limehouse, polling almost 8,000 votes, although none of its candidates was elected.[33] The BUF did elect a few councillors at local government level during the 1930s (including Charles Bentinck Budd (Worthing, Sussex), 1934; Ronald Creasy (Eye, Suffolk), 1938) but did not win any parliamentary seats.[34][35][36][37] Two former members of the BUF, Major Sir Jocelyn Lucas and Harold Soref, were later elected as Conservative Members of Parliament (MPs).[38][39]Having lost the funding of newspaper magnate Lord Rothermere, that it had previously enjoyed, at the 1935 general election the party urged voters to abstain, calling for "Fascism Next Time".[40] There never was a "next time" as the next general election was not held until July 1945, five years after the dissolution of the BUF.[citation needed]Towards the middle of the 1930s, the BUF's violent clashes with opponents began to alienate some middle-class supporters, and membership decreased. At the Olympia rally in London, in 1934, BUF stewards violently ejected anti-fascist disrupters, and this led the Daily Mail to withdraw its support for the movement. The level of violence shown at the rally shocked many, with the effect of turning neutral parties against the BUF and contributing to anti-fascist support. One observer claimed: "I came to the conclusion that Mosley was a political maniac, and that all decent English people must combine to kill his movement."[41]In Belfast in April 1934 an autonomous wing of the party in Northern Ireland called the "Ulster Fascists" was founded. The branch was a failure and became virtually extinct after less than a year in existence.[42] It had ties with the Blueshirts in the Irish Free State and voiced support for a United Ireland, describing the partition of Ireland as "an insurmountable barrier to peace, and prosperity in Ireland".[43] Its logo combined the fasces with the Red Hand of Ulster.[44]
Decline and legacy
The BUF became more antisemitic over 1934–35 owing to the growing influence of Nazi sympathisers within the party, such as William Joyce and John Beckett, which provoked the resignation of members such as Robert Forgan. This antisemitic emphasis and these high-profile resignations resulted in a significant decline in membership, dropping to below 8,000 by the end of 1935, and, ultimately, Mosley shifted the party's focus back to mainstream politics. There were frequent and continuous violent clashes between BUF party members and anti-fascist protesters organised by member of the Independent Labour Party, Communist Party and the Trade Union Movement, including supporters of these groups within the Jewish Community; most famously at the Battle of Cable Street in October 1936, when organised anti-fascists prevented the BUF from marching through Cable Street. However, the party later staged other marches through the East End without incident, albeit not on Cable Street itself.BUF support for Edward VIII and the peace campaign to prevent a second World War saw membership and public support rise once more.[45] The government was sufficiently concerned by the party's growing prominence to pass the Public Order Act 1936, which banned political uniforms and required police consent for political https://t.co/NXO8x58Njw 1937, William Joyce and other Nazi sympathisers split from the party to form the National Socialist League, which quickly folded, with most of its members interned. Mosley later denounced Joyce as a traitor and condemned him for his extreme antisemitism. The historian Stephen Dorril revealed in his book Blackshirts that secret envoys from the Nazis had donated about £50,000 to the BUF.[46]By 1939, total BUF membership had declined to just 20,000, and an active membership of only 5,800, more than half of which was in Greater London.[45][47] After March 1938, when the Czechoslovak Crisis brought Britain and Nazi Germany close to war, the BUF profited by re-orientating to a primarily anti-war campaign, something bolstered in 1939 by the German annexation of Bohemia and Britain's guarantee of Poland. The campaign was steeped in antisemitism, with Mosley blaming rising tensions as well as the British-Polish pact on 'Jewish finance'. At the peak of this campaign, Mosley was able to address an audience 11,000 strong at Exhibition Hall, Earls Court, on 16 July.[47]The BUF's anti-war campaign did not cease after the outbreak of war between Britain and Germany, so, on 23 May 1940, Mosley and some 740 other party members were interned under Defence Regulation 18B. The BUF then called on its followers to resist invasion, but it was declared unlawful on 10 July 1940 and ceased its activities.[48][49]After the war, Mosley made several unsuccessful attempts to return to political life, one such being through the Union Movement, but he had no successes.

Relationship with the suffragettes
Attracted by "modern" fascist policies, such as ending the widespread practice of sacking women from their jobs on marriage, many women joined the Blackshirts – particularly in economically depressed Lancashire. Eventually women constituted one-quarter of the BUF's membership.[50]In a January 2010 BBC documentary, Mother Was A Blackshirt, James Maw reported that in 1914 Norah Elam was placed in a Holloway Prison cell with Emmeline Pankhurst for her involvement with the suffragette movement, and, in 1940, she was returned to the same prison with Diana Mosley, this time for her involvement with the fascist movement. Another leading suffragette, Mary Richardson, became head of the women's section of the BUF.Mary Sophia Allen OBE was a former branch leader of the West of England Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU). At the outbreak of the First World War, she joined the Women Police Volunteers, becoming the WPV Commandant in 1920. She met Mosley at the January Club in April 1932, going on to speak at the club following her visit to Germany, "to learn the truth about the position of German womanhood".[51]The BBC report described how Elam's fascist philosophy grew from her suffragette experiences, how the British fascist movement became largely driven by women, how they targeted young women from an early age, how the first British fascist movement was founded by a woman, and how the leading lights of the suffragettes had, with Oswald Mosley, founded the BUF.[52]Mosley's electoral strategy had been to prepare for the election after 1935, and in 1936, he announced a list of BUF candidates for that election, with Elam nominated to stand for Northampton. Mosley accompanied Elam to Northampton to introduce her to her electorate at a meeting in the Town Hall. At that meeting Mosley announced that "he was glad indeed to have the opportunity of introducing the first candidate, and ... [thereby] killed for all time the suggestion that National Socialism proposed putting British women back into the home; this is simply not true. Mrs Elam [he went on] had fought in the past for women's suffrage ... and was a great example of the emancipation of women in Britain."[53]Former suffragettes were drawn to the BUF for a variety of reasons. Many felt that the movement's energy reminded them of the suffragettes, while others felt that the BUF's economic policies would offer them true equality – unlike its continental counterparts, the movement insisted that it would not require women to return to domesticity and it also insisted that the corporatist state would ensure adequate representation for housewives, while it would also guarantee equal wages for women and remove the marriage bar that restricted the employment of married women. The BUF also offered support for new mothers (due to concerns about falling birth rates), and it also offered effective birth control, because Mosley believed that it was not in the national interest to have a populace which lacked modern scientific knowledge. While these policies were motivated more out of making the best use of women's skills in state interest than they were motivated by any kind of feminism, it was still a draw for many suffragettes.[54]

Prominent members and supporters

(January 2024) (Learn how and when to remove this message)Despite the short period of its operation, the BUF attracted prominent members and supporters. These included:Mary Sophia Allen was a suffragette.
William Edward David Allen was previously a Unionist Member of Parliament for Belfast West.[55] Material in the National Archive shows that Allen acted as an MI5 agent within the BUF.[56][need quotation to verify]
John Beckett was previously a Labour Member of Parliament for Peckham.[57]

Robert Forgan was previously a Labour Member of Parliament for West Renfrewshire.[60]

William Joyce, later nicknamed 'Lord Haw-Haw', was naturalized as a German citizen and broadcast pro-Nazi propaganda from German territory. Captured in Germany at the end of the war, convicted as a traitor and executed.[60]
Ted "Kid" Lewis was a Jewish boxing champion; he left the party after it became overtly antisemitic.[69]

David Freeman-Mitford, 2nd Baron Redesdale, was a member of the House of Lords. His wife, Lady Redesdale, and two of his daughters were also members:Diana Mitford (Lady Mosley, after her marriage to Sir Oswald Mosley in 1936)

Edward Frederick Langley Russell, 2nd Baron Russell of Liverpool, was a member of the House of Lords.[65][66]His wife Lady Russell was also a member.[65][66]

Frank Cyril Tiarks, of German extraction, was a banker, a Director of the Bank of England and a prominent member of the Anglo-German Fellowship.His wife, Emmy née Brödermann, was also a member.

In popular culture
📷Emblem of P. G. Wodehouse's fictional Black Shorts movement that appeared in the television series Jeeves and Wooster
The Channel 4 television serial Mosley (1998) portrayed the career of Oswald Mosley during his years with the BUF. The four-part series was based on the books Rules of the Game and Beyond the Pale, written by his son Nicholas Mosley.[72]
In the film It Happened Here (1964), the BUF appears to be the ruling party of German-occupied Britain. A Mosley speech is heard on the radio in the scene before everyone goes to the cinema.
The first depiction of Mosley and the BUF in fiction occurred in Aldous Huxley's novel Point Counter Point (1932), in which Mosley is depicted as Everard Webley, the murderous leader of the "BFF", the Brotherhood of Free Fascists; he comes to a nasty end.

The BUF has been featured in several novels by Harry https://t.co/woXoHZZyCr his alternative history novel In the Presence of Mine Enemies, set in 2010 in a world in which the Nazis were triumphant, the BUF led by Prime Minister Charlie Lynton governs Britain. It is here that the first stirrings of the reform movement appear.
In the Southern Victory series, set in a reality in which the Confederate States of America became independent and the Central Powers (including the United States) won that reality's analogue of the First World War, the "Silver Shirts" (analogous to the BUF) entered into a coalition with the Conservatives who were led by Churchill with Mosley being appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer.
The BUF and Mosley also appear as background influences in Turtledove's Colonization trilogy which follows the Worldwar tetralogy and is set in the 1960s.
James Herbert's novel '48 (1996) has a protagonist who is hunted by BUF Blackshirts in a devastated London after a biological weapon is released during the Second World War. The history of the BUF and Mosley is recapitulated.
In Ken Follett's novel Night Over Water, several of the main characters are BUF members. In his book Winter of the World, the Battle of Cable Street plays a role and some of the characters are involved in either the BUF or the anti-BUF organisations.
The BUF also appears in Guy Walters' book The Leader (2003), in which Mosley is the dictator of Britain in the 1930s.
The British humorous writer P. G. Wodehouse satirized the BUF in books and short stories. The BUF was satirized as "The Black Shorts",[73] rather than "shirts", because all of the best shirt colours were already taken. Its leader was Roderick Spode, the owner of a ladies' underwear shop.
The British novelist Nancy Mitford satirized the BUF and Mosley in Wigs on the Green (1935). Diana Mitford, the author's sister, had been romantically involved with Mosley since 1932.
In the 1992 Acorn Media production of Agatha Christie's One, Two, Buckle My Shoe with David Suchet and Philip Jackson, one of the supporting characters (played by Christopher Eccleston) secures a paid position as a rank-and-file member of the BUF.
The BUF and Oswald Mosley are alluded to in Kazuo Ishiguro's novel The Remains of the Day.
The BUF and Mosley are shown in the BBC version of Upstairs, Downstairs (2010) in which two of the characters are BUF supporters.
The Pogues' song "The Sick Bed of Cuchulainn", from their album Rum Sodomy & the Lash (1985), refers to the BUF in its second verse with the line "And you decked some fucking blackshirt who was cursing all the Yids".
Ned Beauman's first novel, Boxer, Beetle (2010), portrays the Battle of Cable Street.
C. J. Samson's novel Dominion (2012) has Sir Oswald Mosley as Home Secretary in a "post-Dunkirk peace with Germany alternate history thriller" set in 1952. Lord Beaverbrook is Prime Minister of an authoritarian coalition government. Blackshirts tend to be auxiliary policemen.
In the film The King's Speech (2010), a brief shot shows a brick wall in London plastered with posters, some of them reading "Fascism is Practical Patriotism" and others reading "Stand by the King". Both sets of posters were put up by British Blackshirts, who supported King Edward VIII. Edward was suspected of fascist leanings.[74]
Sarah Phelps used the British Union of Fascists' insignia as a theme in her 2018 BBC One adaptation of Agatha Christie's The A.B.C. Murders.[75]
Amanda K. Hale's novel Mad Hatter (2019) features her father James Larratt Battersby as a member of the BUF.
Mosley was portrayed by Sam Claflin in Series 5 and 6 of the BBC show Peaky Blinders as the founder of the BUF.[76]
The legacy of BUF is a theme of the final episode of season 8 of the detective series Father Brown.

text:
In 1998, Warren Buffett gave a 1-hour masterclass on how to never lose money investing.

Here are the 22 most valuable lessons from his lecture:

1. You only have to get rich once. If you have $100 million and can make 10% unleveraged or 20% leveraged, the difference between $110 million and $120 million at year-end means nothing to your life, your family, or anything. But the downside, especially with other people's money, is disgrace, humiliation, and facing the friends whose money you lost. The equation never makes sense.

2. To make money they did not need, they risked money they did have and needed. That is just plain foolish, Buffett says, regardless of your IQ. If you hand him a gun with a million chambers and one bullet and offer him any sum to put it to his temple and pull once, he will not do it. There is nothing on the upside that justifies the downside. People do this financially all the time without thinking.

3. The smartest people in finance went broke, and that is the most fascinating story Buffett knows. Long-term Capital Management had 16 people with possibly the highest average IQ of any business in the country, 350 to 400 combined years of experience, and most of their own net worth in the firm. They still went bankrupt. Buffett says if he ever wrote a book, it would be called why smart people do dumb things.

4. Beta and sigmas tell you nothing about the real risk of going broke. The LTCM team relied heavily on mathematics and believed a six- or seven-sigma event could not touch them. They were wrong. History does not tell you the probabilities of future financial events. The real risk is not volatility. It is a permanent, irreversible blind spot in something crucial, often caused by knowing a great deal about something else.

5. Invest only in businesses you can understand. That one rule narrows the field by about 90%, and that is fine. Buffett can understand Coca-Cola. he cannot value an internet company, and he says if a student handed him a valuation of one on a final exam, he would flunk them. People thought Enron was incredible because it had a good track record, but almost nobody understood how it made money. That was the signal to avoid it.

6. You want a business that is a castle with a wide moat around it. Inside the castle, you want an honest, able, hard-working duke. The moat can be low cost, like Geico in auto insurance, or brand, or patents, or location. But a wonderful castle will always be attacked, so the job of every manager Buffett owns is one thing: widen the moat. Throw crocodiles and sharks into it to keep competitors out.

7. Moats change slowly and invisibly, but they change. Thirty years ago, Kodak's moat was as wide as Coca-Cola's. They had share of mind; the little yellow box meant best in everyone's head. Then they let Fuji into the Olympics and narrowed their own moat. Coca-Cola's moat, by contrast, is wider now than 30 years ago. Every time infrastructure gets built in a country that is not yet profitable, the moat widens a little. You cannot see it day by day, but in 10 years, the difference is enormous.

8. Share of mind beats share of market. When you say Disney, every person in the room has something in their head. Say Universal Pictures or 20th Century Fox, and you have nothing. A mother with two kids will pick the $17.95 Disney video over the $16.95 alternative because she knows it will be fine and does not want to preview ten videos to decide. That little bit of certainty in the customer's mind is worth a fortune.

9. The best businesses have pricing power and require little capital. see's candy sold 16 million pounds at $1.95 when Buffett bought it for $25 million. The entire thesis was whether the price could go to $2.25 without hurting sales. It could, because nobody wants to hand their valentine a box of candy and say, "This year I took the low bid." Today, See's makes $60 million on the same formulas and still takes almost no capital. Compare that to GM, which had to reinvest every dollar into better factories and whose stock barely moved over 50 years.

10. The best businesses earn a royalty on other people's capital. Coca-Cola sells a formula and collects a royalty on every drink. American Express takes a few percent of every dollar you spend. You put up the capital, they take a cut. Low capital intensity is one of the most underrated qualities in a business and one of the surest paths to durable wealth.

11. Define your circle of competence and stay inside it. The size of the circle does not matter. Staying inside, it does. If you know which 30 companies out of thousands you actually understand, you are fine. Buffett understood H.H. brown shoes and Frank Rooney, so he closed that deal in five minutes. If you do not know enough to understand a business instantly, you will not understand it in a month either.

12. Ignore the macro entirely. Buffett has never bought or skipped a business because of a feeling about interest rates, the economy, or any macro forecast. If Alan Greenspan and Bob Rubin both whispered exactly what they would do for the next 12 months, it would not change what he pays for anything. You want to focus on what is important and knowable. The macro is important but not knowable, so you ignore it.

13. Inactivity is the strategy, not a flaw. Wall Street makes money on activity. You make money on inactivity. A broker is like a doctor paid by how often he changes your pills. If everyone in a room trades their portfolio with everyone else every day, they all end up broke, and the intermediary keeps the money. Buffett looks for one good idea a year and rides it to its full potential. He measures Berkshire by how little turnover there is, like a church where the same people fill the seats every Sunday.

14. If you understand businesses, diversification is a mistake. For the 99% who will not evaluate businesses, Buffett recommends a low-cost index fund and extreme diversification. But if you bring real intensity to evaluating companies, owning more than six is a terrible idea. Very few people got rich on their seventh best idea. A lot of people got rich on their best one. Buffett keeps about half his money in what he likes best.

15. Buffett's biggest mistakes are mistakes of omission, not commission. The times he understood a business well enough to act and instead sat there sucking his thumb. He passed on healthcare stocks during the Clinton plan and on Fannie Mae in the mid-eighties, each a multi-billion-dollar miss. Accounting never captures these. The $2,000 he put into a Sinclair service station as a young man, money he lost, has an opportunity cost of about $6 billion today.

16. Focus on what will happen, not when. Coca-Cola went public in 1919 at $40 a share and dropped to $19 within a year. There was always a reason not to buy: the great depression, world war, sugar rationing, thermonuclear weapons. But one share bought then and reinvested would be worth about $5 million. If you are right about the business, you will make a lot of money. The timing is the tricky part, so do not focus on it.

17. When hiring, look for integrity, intelligence, and energy. But if the person lacks the first one, you actually want them dumb and lazy. Because a person with intelligence and energy but no integrity will destroy you. Buffett borrowed this from Pete Kiewit. The trait everyone screens for last is the one that matters most.

18. Here is a thought experiment Buffett gives students. Imagine you could own 10% of one classmate for the rest of their life. You would not pick the highest IQ or the best grades. You would pick the person you respond to best, the one who is generous, honest, gives credit to others, and has leadership qualities. Now imagine you also had to short one classmate. You would pick the egotistical, greedy, slightly dishonest one. The qualities that decide both are not talent. They are character.

19. Every quality on the admirable side is achievable, and every quality on the repellent side is removable. The things that make you want to own 10% of someone are not the ability to throw a football or run fast; they are behavior, temperament, and character, all of which anyone can choose. Buffett's point: you already own 100% of yourself, so you might as well become the person worth betting on.

20. The chains of habit are too light to be felt until they are too heavy to be broken. Buffett sees people in their forties and fifties trapped by self-destructive patterns they can no longer change. At a young age, you can choose any habits you want. Ben Franklin and Ben Graham both did exactly this, looking at people they admired and simply deciding to behave like them. There was nothing impossible about it.

21. Take a job you would take if you were already independently wealthy. Buffett told a 28-year-old at Harvard who wanted a consulting job "to look good on his resume" that it was like saving up sex for your old age. There comes a time to just start doing what you love. Buffett offered to work for Ben Graham for free, was told he was overpriced, and kept pestering him for years. Take the job you would jump out of bed for. You cannot miss.

22. You won the ovarian lottery, and that should shape how you think. Buffett imagines a genie 24 hours before your birth letting you design the world's rules, with one catch: you do not know which of 5.8 billion balls you will draw. Born here or in Afghanistan, with an IQ of 130 or 70, male or female, able-bodied or not. If you could put your ball back and draw one of 100 random others, most people would not, because they are already in the luckiest 1%. Buffett knows he is perfectly wired for a market economy that pays him like crazy, while an equally good citizen leading scout troops and teaching Sunday school is not, purely by luck.

text:
Jan van Eyck 
Portrait of a Man (Self Portrait?), 1433 
Oil on wood (probably oak) 
26 × 19 cm (10.2 × 7.5 in.) 
National Gallery, London
@NationalGallery 

This may be the only face of Jan van Eyck that has come down to us, and he set it under a red headdress so large it nearly fills the panel.

The cloth is a chaperon, a man’s headdress of the 1400s, folded and piled on the head. A strong light catches the ridges of the folds and leaves the creases dark, so the cloth looks carved. Usually the hood hung down over the neck and shoulders. Here it has been stacked on the head. The long tail wraps around and tucks in above the left eye, maybe to keep it out of the way while he painted, and the end flies up over the right temple. Under it sits a man in a dark gown, fur at the collar, a white shirt just showing at the throat. He looks out, slightly past the viewer, one eye a little off from the other. The National Gallery calls the picture Portrait of a Man (Self Portrait?), and the question mark is there because no other portrait of van Eyck survives to check the face against.

The gown is a houppelande, a loose overrobe worn by men and women in the later Middle Ages. The clothes fit a prosperous man, not a great noble. Van Eyck’s family were gentry, and he was court painter to Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy, on a handsome salary.

The case for a self-portrait is in the pose and the frame. The sitter leans forward a little, as if looking into a mirror, and the eyes do not quite match, as if he had studied one and then the other. Van Eyck usually put the sitter’s name on the frame. This frame has no name. Across the top, in letters made to look Greek, it carries his motto, Als Ich Can. That means “as I can.” The full Flemish saying is “as I can, but not as I would,” a modest way of saying he did the best he could, not as well as he wished. Ich, the word for “I,” sounds like the Eyck in his name, so the same line can be read “as Eyck can.” The modesty has his signature hidden in it. He used the motto on other paintings, including the portrait of his wife, Margaret, now in the Groeningemuseum in Bruges. Here it is unusually large. Along the bottom, painted to look carved, the Latin reads Johannes de Eyck me fecit, “Jan van Eyck made me,” on October 21, 1433. That line names the painter. It does not name the man in the hat. The letters for October are squeezed against the end, with no room for a stop. The guidelines for that line slipped and had to be ruled again.

The frame is original, and it is the only surviving van Eyck frame that is gilded. Most of his others were painted to look like marble. The sides are cut from the same piece of wood as the panel. The top and bottom are separate boards, pegged on. The round peg holes still show, one of them sitting in the word Ich. Similar frames survive on four other paintings by him, and may be the work of the same carpenter. In the 1400s a portrait was not always hung. It might live in a box or a bag and come out on occasion, so the frame, and the back, were meant to be seen. The back is now covered in later black paint. Near the lower edge a small patch of the old chalk ground still shows. That is the white coat of chalk and glue a painter spread on the wood before any color went on. The patch means van Eyck had the back prepared for paint, even though that paint is gone.

Only about twenty paintings by van Eyck survive. He is famous for surfaces that look minutely real, but the National Gallery says he painted with speed. The stubble is tiny dabs, dark brown first, then lighter, with a little blue mixed into the white on the chin so the dots catch the light. The head is enlarged and the shoulders narrowed, so the face takes over the panel. The nose was made larger in the painting than in the drawing underneath, a trick he used to make a face easier to recognize. Some color has changed. The background was once blue. The black is almost certainly later paint. The gown was a purplish brown, with pleats across the chest.

Nothing is known of the panel between 1433 and the 1640s. Thomas Howard, Earl of Arundel, had it with him in Antwerp in 1642–44. A collector who saw it there called it a portrait of the Duke of Barlaumont. It had probably come from London earlier in 1642, in a shipment of about sixty crates of Arundel’s pictures. After Arundel died in 1646, the collection passed to his widow, Alathea Talbot. She died in Amsterdam in 1654. An inventory made there in 1655 lists this panel as a portrait of Jan van Eyck by his own hand. From her it passed to her son, William Howard, Viscount Stafford, and then to his son, Henry Stafford-Howard, Earl of Stafford. No sale is recorded. The National Gallery treats that step as inheritance. In London early in 1682 someone offered a van Eyck self-portrait to an envoy of the Grand Duke of Tuscany. Whether that was this panel is not certain. The owners between the Stafford family and 1851 are not fully published. The National Gallery bought it that year. The price is not given on the museum’s page. It hangs in room 52. The frame tells us who painted the panel, and on what day. It does not tell us who sat for it. Van Eyck usually named the sitter. Here he left that out. That missing name is why the museum title still has a question mark. If the face is his, it is the only one we have.

text:
A Statement of Conscience on October 7

I will not start by saying ‘as a Muslim’ or ‘as an imam’, but as a human being.

On October 7, over 1,200 innocent people were killed in a single day. Families were shot in their homes. Young people out dancing were hunted across open fields. Over 250 people, including children and the elderly, were dragged into Gaza as hostages. I think of a mother hiding in a safe room with her baby’s mouth covered. I think of a father listening as the line went quiet. I think of families who waited month after month for someone to come home, only to receive a coffin. I didn’t need my faith to recognize the evil of what happened. My heart told me first.

But I’m a Muslim and an imam, and I owe the world one honest sentence: what was done that day was a crime against God. God teaches that whoever kills one innocent soul, it is as if he had killed all humanity.

This day has an author: Yahya Sinwar. He planned it, ordered it, and knew what would follow. Every death of that day and war he started rests on him and Hamas leaders who sat in tunnels and foreign hotels and called slaughter a victory. It rests on every Palestinian leader who cheered, excused, handed out sweets, or said nothing. They chose this. They own it.

But Sinwar did not invent himself. He was the fruit of a tree planted almost a century ago by the Muslim Brotherhood. Hamas named itself in its founding charter as the Brotherhood’s branch in Palestine. The Brotherhood’s poison is slow. It arrives through study circles, youth camps, charity boxes, and kind words to lonely young men. Drop by drop, it teaches him that his religion is a political party, his neighbour is his enemy, the Jew is the cause of his sorrow, and God is pleased by rage. By the time the gun arrives, the soul is already taken.

I have seen this poison in mosques where sermons became rallies and young men could recite slogans but not sit still for a verse on mercy. Every people that let the Brotherhood in has paid in blood and ruined generations. It has never built anything it did not first set on fire.

Behind Hamas stands another hand: the IRGC. It was the IRGC’s money, weapons, and training that turned a hateful idea into an army. One calls itself Sunni and the other Shia, and they may curse each other’s creeds, but they are united in what they worship. It is not God. It is power. The same IRGC that armed the killers of October 7 shoots Iranian girls for showing their hair, hangs young men for asking to be free, and has left graves from Tehran to Damascus to Beirut. They speak in God’s name. So did Pharaoh speak in the name of heaven.

So let me say this clearly. Hamas and the IRGC are not merely enemies of Islam. That would be too small a charge, as if their crime were only against us. They are enemies of God. God is the Giver of life, yet they deal in death. God calls Himself the Most Merciful, yet they have made cruelty a sacrament. God honoured the children of Adam, yet they look at a child and see a target or a shield. To murder what God created and sign His name to it is the oldest blasphemy.

And we Muslims have been too quiet. Some of us were afraid. Some told ourselves it was not our business. Some, God forgive them, felt something other than horror that morning and never confessed it. Silence was the soil this poison grew in. I will not add to it.

So on this anniversary, let us say plainly what our scripture already says. The Jews are not our enemies. They are our cousins in Abraham, and their dead were created by the same God who created us. Today belongs to them: the murdered, the hostages, and families who still set a place at the table. To them I say: I am sorry for what was done to you by men who used the words of my prayers. You’re not alone in your grief or remembrance.

The enemies of God are those who murder in His name. We know their names. It is time we said them from our own pulpits, in our own voices, before they speak for us again.

Imam Tawhidi

This day is profoundly painful for so many New Yorkers. It marks three years since the horrific war crimes of October 7. On that day, Hamas killed more than 1,100 Israelis and abducted 251 others. We grieve alongside our many friends and neighbors who still carry that unthinkable loss.

The suffering did not begin nor end that day. It instead continued through the Israeli government’s devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza, in which it has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians—including more than 21,000 children. Even since the so-called ceasefire, more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed. That suffering has intensified with every Israeli bomb dropped on ambulances waiting outside hospitals, every drone strike targeting a residential building or journalist, and every shipment of food aid turned away at a border crossing. Many New Yorkers are reckoning with this unbearable grief, and we mourn alongside them – all while knowing that our tax dollars fund these war crimes.

Three years later, we must refuse to accept a world in which occupation and apartheid continue, where war crimes are met with impunity, and our federal government continues its complicity with every arms shipment.

To honor the dead, we must fight for a world in which every person can live with freedom, safety, and dignity.

text:
THIS IS NUTS: Kilmar Ábrego Garcia was deported to El Salvador, brought BACK to America to face charges, and is now facing deportation to Liberia. After 18 months of legal battles, Tuesday’s hearing was canceled before the judge took the bench. The public wasn’t even told WHY.⠀

Ábrego Garcia is a Salvadoran man who entered the U.S. illegally as a teenager and later lived in Maryland with his family. In 2019, an immigration judge granted him protection against deportation to El Salvador because he faced persecution there. ⠀

The Trump administration sent him there anyway in March 2025. ICE acknowledged an administrative error, and after court intervention, he was brought back to the United States that June to face human-smuggling charges in Tennessee.

That indictment was dismissed in May 2026 after a judge found the prosecution vindictive. The Justice Department is appealing, while the administration continues pursuing his deportation to another country.

Now the government wants a judge to lift an injunction blocking ICE from detaining him and sending him to Liberia. His lawyers want the injunction made permanent.

Costa Rica has offered to accept him, and he says he’s willing to go. But the administration is pushing for Liberia, citing resources and political capital spent negotiating that destination.

Tuesday was supposed to bring arguments before the court. Instead, Ábrego Garcia arrived with supporters carrying “Free Kilmar” signs, the hearing was abruptly canceled, and the dispute remained unresolved.

A deportation carried out in error, a court-ordered return, a dismissed prosecution, and another proposed destination. Immigration enforcement requires decisions that survive legal scrutiny. How many more rounds will this take before the government and the courts reach a lawful resolution?

The Nebraska speech already answered the question. Trump tied the “small price to pay” line directly to higher gas prices from the Iran war, then said a nuclear-capable Iran could take out a city like Los Angeles or San Diego, and that ending that threat was worth the cost. The surrounding sentences make the sequence clear; the White House restated the same point the next morning.

Left-leaning outlets and Democratic accounts still cut the gas-price clause, paired the leftover words with captions claiming he offered the cities as acceptable losses, and kept asking the loaded version of the question the following day. https://t.co/u7NxbqO6mk, PolitiFact, and CNN’s Daniel Dale noted the paraphrase stripped the context; the posts and the four-second wave-off clip ran anyway.

That is the method: take the real words, drop the sentences that fix the meaning, and distribute the shortened version so the non-answer can be treated as confirmation. 

The speech supplied the explanation on the day it was given; the follow-up coverage manufactured the crisis and the division by refusing to use it.

text:
🏈 NFL WEEK 5 LINE MOVE REPORT

Six-point total drops. Favorites moving through three. Lines moving against the majority of tickets.

The reason behind the move matters. So does the price you can still get.

Week 5 starts October 8.
Snapshot: October 7, 11 a.m. ET.
Grades assess move quality, not predicted winning chances.

• WASHINGTON vs NEW YORK GIANTS
#RaiseHail #BigBlue

WAS -2.5 → -3.5
Only 17% of tickets on Washington.
Move quality: B+

Jayden Daniels’ expected return helps explain Washington’s support against a Giants team starting Jameis Winston after losing Jaxson Dart.

The move makes sense, but crossing three changes the bet. Washington -2.5 could win on a field-goal margin. At -3.5, that same result loses.

Watch Giants +3.5 if Daniels remains limited.

• NEW YORK JETS vs CLEVELAND
#JetUp #DawgPound

NYJ -1.5 → -2.5
Only 15% of tickets on New York.
Move quality: C

Cleveland’s injury concerns include Mason Graham and offensive linemen Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins. Those could explain support for the Jets.

However, other books have shown movement toward Cleveland. The 15% ticket share catches attention, but the broader market picture remains mixed.

Pass pending clearer availability and market confirmation.

• ARIZONA vs DETROIT
#RiseUpRedSea #OnePride

ARI +8.5 → +5.5
48% of tickets on Arizona.
Move quality: B
Sharp-driven confidence: B

Arizona’s passing attack offers a credible matchup argument, particularly Trey McBride against Detroit’s vulnerable defense.

Moving through seven is significant. The ticket split itself is modest, with almost half the bets already backing Arizona.

The strongest Arizona price was +8.5. Detroit -5.5 becomes the buyback side to investigate.

• TAMPA BAY @ DALLAS
#WeAreTheKrewe #DallasCowboys

Total: 52.5 → 47.5
Only 30% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: A-

Baker Mayfield’s throwing-thumb injury provides the strongest explanation. Rookie Jalon Daniels faces another start with a short preparation week.

Weekly opening reports already showed 47.5, suggesting much of this adjustment happened earlier.

Tampa Bay’s defensive injuries support an over counterargument. Still, a five-point drop does not automatically make the over valuable.

• NEW YORK GIANTS @ WASHINGTON
#BigBlue #RaiseHail

Total: 48.5 → 43.5
Only 24% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: B

Dart’s absence lowers New York’s offensive expectations. Washington has uncertainty around Daniels’ recovery and Marcus Mariota’s new knee injury.

Daniels returning would support scoring, so the entire decline cannot be explained by one injury story.

Over 43.5 becomes interesting if Daniels practices fully and Washington’s receiving group gets healthier.

• HOUSTON @ TENNESSEE
#HTownMade #TitanUp

Total: 43.5 → 37.5
Only 28% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: B
Sharp-driven confidence: B+

My leading over buyback candidate.

The decline appears to reflect lower expectations for Tennessee rather than a major new quarterback absence. Houston just scored 30 against Dallas, with C.J. Stroud throwing for 347 yards.

Early Nashville forecasts include rain and gusts around 22 mph. That supports some reduction, but does not independently explain six points.

At Houston -7.5 and a 37.5 total, the implied score is 22.5–15. A 24–17 result clears the over.

Conditional lean: Over 37.5 if weather holds or improves and final availability supports it.

• MINNESOTA @ NEW ORLEANS
#Skol #Saints

Total: 44.5 → 42.5
Only 29% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: B+

Justin Jefferson remains uncleared after an ankle injury. Minnesota also has offensive-line concerns involving Christian Darrisaw and Donovan Jackson.

Those support a scoring downgrade. New Orleans’ defensive injuries work in the opposite direction. Weather is not a factor indoors.

Jefferson and Darrisaw returning would strengthen an Over 42.5 buyback. Continued absences support the lower number.

• CINCINNATI @ MIAMI
#WhoDey #PhinsUp

Total: 49.5 → 42.5
Only 33% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: A-

Ja’Marr Chase entered concussion protocol. Tee Higgins has an adductor injury.

Potentially losing both receivers substantially changes Cincinnati’s passing ceiling. This move has a strong injury explanation.

Over 42.5 becomes interesting if both return. Without positive availability news, the seven-point decline alone is insufficient reason to buy back.

• INDIANAPOLIS @ PITTSBURGH
#ForTheShoe #HereWeGo

Total: 47.5 → 44.5
Only 30% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: B-

Indianapolis returns from London and immediately travels again. Pittsburgh has extra rest after Thursday Night Football.

Fatigue and preparation provide a plausible under argument. Indianapolis’ defensive struggles provide a scoring counterargument.

Over 44.5 belongs on the secondary buyback watchlist.

• CHICAGO @ GREEN BAY
#DaBears #GoPackGo

Total: 49.5 → 45.5
Only 26% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: B+

Tyson Bagent starts while Caleb Williams recovers from a hamstring injury. That supports lower offensive expectations.

Williams was injured in Week 2, so some of this adjustment reflects older information. Moderate wind also supports the under case.

Pass at 45.5. The explanation is credible, but the remaining value is uncertain.

• DENVER @ LOS ANGELES CHARGERS
#BroncosCountry #BoltUp

Total: 44.5 → 42.5
Only 35% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: B+

Los Angeles has offensive injury problems involving Rashawn Slater, Joe Alt and Ladd McConkey.

Denver’s missing Pat Surtain II and uncertainty around Riley Moss weaken its coverage, creating an opposing scoring argument.

Wait for availability. Injuries affect both sides of the total.

• BALTIMORE @ ATLANTA
#RavensFlock #DirtyBirds

Total: 48.5 → 43.5
Only 41% of tickets on the under.
Move quality: A-

Lamar Jackson’s ankle injury has coincided with a major spread reversal and lower total. Reports indicate he is unlikely to play, with Tyler Huntley trending toward the start.

This is the clearest quarterback-driven adjustment on the list.

A healthy Jackson return would strengthen an over buyback. With Huntley starting, the lower total has a clear basis.

📌 THE CURRENT WATCHLIST

• Leading buyback candidate: HOU–TEN Over 37.5.
• Availability-dependent overs: NYG–WAS, MIN–NO and CIN–MIA.
• Side buybacks to investigate: Giants +3.5 and Detroit -5.5.

text:
The ExxonMobil Contingent Community is ExxonMobil’s talent pool for temporary contract work, not a community-investment program. Raise Limited is the employer of record for that program.
Official description (on the Raise-hosted site for the program):

It is a network of people looking for contingent assignments at ExxonMobil, matched to openings that fit their skills.

Joining it does not block applications for full-time ExxonMobil jobs.

Contingent work is temporary. Workers are employed by a third party, not by ExxonMobil.

Roles are in various locations, with competitive pay and a possible path to full-time employment.
Assignments put people on site with ExxonMobil’s workforce.

How Raise Limited fits: if you are matched to an assignment through the Contingent Community, you are employed by Raise Limited, the employer of record for ExxonMobil’s Contingent Program. 

You work at ExxonMobil facilities alongside ExxonMobil employees and other contractors, but you are not an ExxonMobil employee. 

Raise handles the employment relationship (pay, employment status, and related admin). ExxonMobil uses the program to scale temporary labor. Raise describes itself as a hiring firm with a long operating history and runs the portal at https://t.co/vB7gOf6A6E.

Typical openings listed there include engineering, geoscience, research, warehouse, and recruiting-support roles, often in Spring or Baytown, Texas, and some in Calgary, with assignment windows often about a year. (https://t.co/vB7gOf6A6E).

~~~~~~~

Three parties sit in this arrangement: the contractor, ExxonMobil, and Raise Limited (the employer of record). Pros and cons are structural, not a review of any one assignment.

Contractor - Pros

Access to ExxonMobil work without winning a full-time offer. Roles run across engineering, geoscience, ops, and support, often around Spring, Baytown, and some Canadian sites.
Pay is often competitive for contract work, and the site claims conversion to full-time is possible.
Joining the pool does not block a direct ExxonMobil application.
A finite assignment (often about a year) can be a way in, or a way out, without a long commitment.

Cons

You are Raise’s employee, not ExxonMobil’s. Benefits, PTO, bonuses, stock, and internal mobility generally do not match ExxonMobil employee terms.

The work ends when the assignment ends. Conversion is not guaranteed.

You sit between two organizations: day-to-day direction from ExxonMobil, employment terms from Raise. That can slow raises, title changes, and issue resolution.

Contractors are often outside core decision-making and are first cut if headcount tightens.

ExxonMobil - Pros

Scales labor up and down without adding permanent headcount, benefits, or severance exposure.
Raise carries employer-of-record duties (payroll, employment law, onboarding admin).

A pre-built pool shortens time-to-fill for project and surge work. A trial period before any full-time offer.

Cons

Higher fully loaded hourly cost than an employee once agency margin is included.
Less control over retention, culture, and long-term knowledge. Contractors leave with the assignment.
Split accountability: ExxonMobil directs the work, Raise employs the person. Safety, IP, and performance issues need a clean contract.
Conversion friction and co-employment risk if ExxonMobil treats contractors like employees for too long.

Raise Limited - Pros

Recurring revenue as employer of record and staffing partner on a large, stable account.

Markup on wages plus admin fees, with volume from a named ExxonMobil program.

The Contingent Community is a reusable candidate database, not one-off requisitions.

Cons

Dependent on one major client. A program change or insource hits the book of business.
Margin pressure: ExxonMobil can push rates down, and contractors compare pay to direct ExxonMobil offers.

Employer-of-record liability (wage-and-hour, benefits administration, unemployment, workers’ comp) sits with Raise even though ExxonMobil controls the work.
Reputation risk if contractors feel underpaid or poorly supported relative to the ExxonMobil brand on the job posting.

Bottom line: ExxonMobil buys flexibility, Raise buys volume and margin, and the contractor buys access and pay at the cost of permanence and employee-level benefits.

text:
SUPPORT GOES BOTH WAYS.

Women have been a major part of Blue Cure’s community from the beginning, helping raise prostate cancer awareness and supporting men and families facing a diagnosis. During Breast Cancer Awareness Month, we’re asking men to return that care and support.

This 2013 KHOU 11 story features breast cancer survivor and Blue Cure board member emerita Carolyn Farb, who understood that cancer affects the patient and the people who love them.

Carolyn, thank you for championing Blue Cure in our early years, for your years of board service, and for helping raise awareness of prostate cancer and men’s health. Your leadership and service remain an important part of Blue Cure’s story.

Thank you also to journalist and anchor Lily Jang, who reported this piece and was an early supporter of Blue Cure and our message, and to KHOU 11 Houston for helping us reach more families. Stories like this can give men and women the nudge to ask questions, discuss screening with their healthcare team and take an active role in their health.

To Carolyn and all the women who raise awareness, share our message, ask questions and encourage the men in their lives to seek care: thank you. Women have strengthened Blue Cure as followers, volunteers, donors, leaders and advocates from the beginning. Your health deserves that same care and attention.

Men, ask how you can help. Listen, support breast cancer education and advocacy, and offer practical help with appointments or other needs. Let’s be there for the women in our lives.

To the women in our community: ask your healthcare team about your breast cancer risk and when to begin or continue screening, including mammograms. Screening schedules depend on age and personal risk. If you notice a new breast change, have it evaluated promptly.

To those living with breast cancer, its survivors and the families who have lost someone: we stand with you.

Archival footage: KHOU 11 Houston, 2013.
For education only. Talk with your healthcare team about your individual care.

authorBio: Diagnosed with prostate cancer at 35. TEDx speaker | Author, Unexpected Diagnosis | Men’s health advocate | Writer
