text:
To understand the magnitude of the problem recognizing and reporting egregious public health and safety practices at abortion facilities, you simply have to peruse the details from the Grand Jury Report on Kermit Gosnell – the abortion provider currently serving time in prison for murder following decades of deplorable abortion practices.27  The Pennsylvania Department of Public Health and Safety deliberately chose not to enforce law that would afford patients at abortion clinics the safeguards and assurances of quality care as patients of other medical providers. The Grand Jury stated that “the medical practice by which he carried out this business was a filthy fraud in which he overdosed his patients with dangerous drugs, spread venereal disease among them with infected instruments, perforated their wombs and bowels – and, on at least two occasions, caused their deaths.” “Over the years, many people came to know that something was going on here. But no one put a stop to it.”. Even the world class Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania and the Presbyterian Hospital turned a blind eye to women who presented with life-threatening complications from Gosnell’s clinic.

Gosnell is not an isolated rogue actor, since there are dozens of examples of gross medical negligence at abortion clinics from New Jersey to Florida, and from Pennsylvania to Indianna/Michigan and California. If robust Department of Public Health and Environment licensing, regulation, and inspections were in place, none of these regrettable tragedies would happen.

Here in Colorado, Mediatrackers first drew attention to the lack of regulation at abortion clinics in Colorado in 2013.28 This was prompted by a malpractice lawsuit against Planned Parenthood of the Rocky Mountains that alleged malpractice and health standard violations. They found that Planned Parenthood abortion clinics were not held to the same standards as other facilities which are regulated by CDPHE. Planned Parenthood’s only state oversight consists of the licensure of physicians, nurses and pharmacists who must maintain the requirements of the Colorado State Board of Health, the Board of Nursing, and the Board of Pharmacy. They also operate within the constraints of OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) and CLIA (Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments). There is no state licensing, regulatory, or inspection requirements for public health and safety at abortion facilities in Colorado despite receiving millions of dollars of direct aid from the state.

Another factor which is underappreciated is the fact that 29% of the abortions reported to CDPHE in 2023 were performed on out-of-state residents. Colorado is obligated to ensure quality care for these women so that don’t suffer severe complications after they return home. This could delay appropriate care, worsen the severity of the complication, and have implications for their long-term health. Out-of-state women probably assume that the State of Colorado has their back with appropriate, evidence-based licensing, regulation, and inspections.

Finally, the truth is that there is a global shortage of abortion providers and few OB/GYNs wish to include abortion in their practices.29There is a negative public perception of abortion providers, even if the public broadly supports abortion rights. According to a recent survey conducted by KFF after the Dobbs decision, only 7% of OB/GYNs offer telehealth abortions, 14% in-person drug induced abortions, 13% aspiration abortions, and 12% D&E abortions.30

Dr. Warren Hern, the prominent second and third post-viability abortionist who until recently practiced (at age 86) at the Boulder Abortion Clinic acknowledges the problem of maintaining and recruiting quality abortion providers in his recent book Abortion in the Age of Unreason.31 He lamented that there were two kinds of abortion providers. There are those motivated by “altruistic” concerns to help women and sacrifice much to deliver that care in a hostile environment. The second kind of abortion provider is the “commercial” provider who “cuts corners on patient care” and which is the “choice of many abortion providers”.

Even Planned Parenthood which has 11 clinics in Colorado isn’t immune from allegations of putting the abortion “mission” above the health and safety of women.32 The expose reported that “Planned Parenthood has enjoyed a fund-raising boom …but little of it goes to the state affiliates to provide health care at clinics. Instead, under the national bylaws, most of the money is spent on the legal and political fight to maintain abortion rights.” They went on to observe that “employees at various affiliates said it was common to run out of over-the-counter pain medication and I.V. flushes. Salaries are so low that it is not unusual for staff members to qualify for Medicaid and federal food assistance.” As a result of high staff turnover, they say that “they did not receive adequate training for patient intake, blood draws and other tasks.” “Dozens of current and former employees also said that their complaints were met with reminders that they were in a “mission moment,” meaning a time of crisis for reproductive rights so urgent that it overshadowed their concerns.” In this kind of environment would-be whistleblowers remain silent. Women’s health and safety is a secondary consideration because as one employee observed, “we’re afraid of damaging the mission”.

Given the risks, there is a compelling argument to be made why the state must act now to ensure the health and safety of women pursuing second and third trimester abortions in Colorado. Not only is there a large risk to women who undergo late abortion in the best of circumstances, but Colorado’s proabortion environment sets the stage for poorly qualified bad actors to come to the state to pursue remuneration for abortion services without regard for the women they may injure or even kill through their negligence.

In 2025 alone, there has been at least one death of a young woman post abortion and numerable reports of emergent ambulance transfers from second/third trimester abortion facilities suggesting severe complications. There is no way to differentiate anticipated complications from a procedure known to be high risk from medical negligence/malpractice without state oversight.

Conclusion:

Amendment 79 enshrined access to abortion at any time for any reason in the state constitution. Colorado voters could not imagine at the time that they might be casting a vote to undermine the health and safety of women.

Second trimester D&E abortions have a 10% complication rate and at least a 1.7% risk of severe, life-threatening complications such as severe hemorrhage and uterine perforation. At lower volume centers or using different techniques, or with underlying comorbidities and/or placental abnormalities, the complication rate can be as high as 56%. Hemorrhage is the greatest short-term risk and can be rapid and massive. Second and third trimester abortion clinics should be adequately prepared to minimize the risk for hemorrhage and mitigate its severity once established. They should be required to maintain a robust quality/peer review process. There is also an important role for screening tools given the high incidence of mental health and substance abuse disorders in abortion patients.

Oversight should not be limited to direct procedural regulations. Since late abortion not only poses an immediate risk to the health of a woman but also to the prospects of any future pregnancy and wanted child, review of the informed consent process is also crucial.
It is past time for Colorado to have CDPHE establish basic licensing, regulatory, and inspection authority over second and third trimester abortion facilities. CDPHE already has jurisdiction for other medical facilities with markedly less risk for significant morbidity and mortality. To do otherwise poses an unacceptably high risk to the women of Colorado.
Updated 2/15/2026
Thomas J. Perille MD FACP FHM
Democrats for Life of Colorado
Colorado Chapter, AAPLOG

A few important pieces to this $LTNC / Adios timeline 👀 Maybe overlapping in some areas, public information gathered. Let us know if we have anything mixed up, trying to seek clarity for shareholders. 

🔹 4/23/25 — CKS Distro / Next Gen AP agreement executed. 5-year initial term. Next Gen receives exclusive U.S. rights, the agreement addresses jointly developed products and Work Product, with 67% of net profits to Next Gen / 33% CKS.

🔹 7/17/25 — Adios RTD officially launches through the Kultura/$LTNC ecosystem with Cookies, Casa Rica and Flaviar.

🔹 11/26/25 — Kultura publicly calls Adios “the Company’s flagship” RTD brand and identifies CKS as Kultura’s national retail/wholesale partner.

🔹 Next Gen AP / Wyoming — $LTNC disclosures state Next Gen AP is where Adios “resides,” and later where Adios “will be managed.”

🔹 1/15/26 — Michael Araghi acquires the 51 Series A control shares and becomes $LTNC’s control person.

🔹 2/23/26 — Adios Holdco IP, LLC is formed in Wyoming.

🔹 5/7–5/8/26 — Scofflaw LLC becomes effective/filed in Florida while Michael is still on the $LTNC Board. Managers listed: Scott Darnell, Michael Araghi and Brent Albin.

🔹 6/4/26 — Scofflaw Manufacturing LLC formed in Florida. Managers listed: Scott Darnell and Brent Albin.

🔹 6/30/26 — $LTNC Q2 reporting period ends. Page 45 identifies “CKS Distro & Adios Holdco with Adios” as customers over 10%.

⚠️ Important: the Florida Adios Holdco LLC did not exist yet. That entity wasn’t formed until 9/22/26. However, Adios Holdco IP, LLC in Wyoming had existed since 2/23/26.

So which Adios Holdco is referenced in the Q2 financials?

🔹 7/7/26 — $LTNC announces Kultura Beverage Group as a subsidiary of Kultura Brands and its beverage operating platform, initially focused on Adios.

🔹 Manufacturing transition — Earlier Adios labels identify Brew Hub as canner for CKS Distro | Next Gen AP. Later labels identify Scofflaw LLC d/b/a Scofflaw Beverage Co. as canner. Manufacturing and ownership are two different things.

🔹 9/16/26 — Brad Wyatt sends cease-and-desist asserting $LTNC rights/property involving Adios and related IP.

🔹 9/17/26 — Brad publicly states the CKS owner confirmed the 4/23 agreement remained active, had not been terminated, and CKS had no present intention of terminating it or transferring Next Gen AP’s rights.

🔹 ~9/19/26 — Michael later says he believes the termination occurred around the 19th.

What changed between 9/17 and 9/19?

🔹 9/22/26 — A separate ADIOS HOLDCO LLC is formed in Florida, with Michael listed as manager.

So now we have:

2/23/26 — Adios Holdco IP, LLC / Wyoming
9/22/26 — Adios Holdco LLC / Florida

What is the relationship between the two? Did anything move between them? If so, what, when, who approved it and what did $LTNC receive?

🔹 10/6/26 — Michael says $LTNC was recently offered a deal to “finally own Adios” and that it was turned down.

Who turned it down? Was it presented to the full $LTNC Board?

Lots of pieces to this puzzle. No need to jump to conclusions.

Follow the dates. Follow the entities. Follow the contracts. Follow the money. 👊🏽💦 $LTNC #Transparency #ShareholderRights #FollowTheDocuments

text:
Tony Robbins has done a lot to get everyday investors focused on wealth building.

A recent podcast claim made waves across the industry: one million dollars in private equity grew to 293 million over 39 years, while the S&P 500 reached only 28.7 million.

Look at the actual mathematics.

The S&P comparison is price only. Reinvesting dividends turned one million into 62.9 million over that stretch (11.2% annualized per NYU Stern). Restoring dividends cuts the claimed gap in half immediately.

His own book agrees. It cites MSCI and Bloomberg showing the S&P 500 at 11.18% and US private equity at 16.40% over 37 years. That is roughly 5.5 times the ending wealth, not 10 times.

Now look at the institutional benchmark. Cambridge Associates data matching private equity cash flows against the Russell 3000 shows private equity ahead by 2.73 points a year over 25 years, and 1.13 points over 10 years. Trailing 1, 3, and 5 year periods are negative.

The excess return is real over multi decade horizons, but it is measured in basis points, not multiples.

Layer in a typical 1.0% wealth management access fee, and the net 10 year advantage disappears. Add partnership tax drag, and the friction compounds further.

We like private equity. We allocate to it. But the edge is paid for with illiquidity, leverage, and manager risk. You do not underwrite alternatives on retail pitchbook calculations.

text:
Who gets the dog after a breakup?

In most of the country, that fight can still look a lot more like a dispute over property than a custody battle.

But Illinois is changing the rules.

Starting January 1, 2027, judges deciding pet possession disputes can consider who actually cared for the animal, who paid for its care, its emotional bonds, age, routine, health, and which home offers more stability — even if the couple was never married.

The new Illinois pet custody law grew out of a fight over Rosie, a senior puggle whose caregiver helped push lawmakers to change the system.

So what should matter more: whose name is on the paperwork — or who actually cared for the dog?

text:
#OnThisDay 7 October 1916

222–0.

It remains one of the most absurd scorelines in college football history.

But the strangest part wasn't the score.

It was why the game was played.

Months earlier, Cumberland's baseball team had beaten Georgia Tech 22–0.

Tech's coach, John Heisman, wanted revenge.

So he offered Cumberland $500 to come to Atlanta and play football.

Cumberland accepted.

There was just one problem.

By October, Cumberland had effectively lost its football team.

A 16-man squad travelled to Atlanta. Three players abandoned the trip in Nashville, and the team even tried unsuccessfully to recruit players from Vanderbilt.

They still showed up.

Georgia Tech did not take it easy.

By halftime, it was 126–0.

Heisman eventually shortened the final two quarters, but Tech still added another 96 points.

Final score:

Georgia Tech 222
Cumberland 0

It remains a legendary reminder that sometimes the story behind a record is stranger than the record itself.

text:
My coworker's lease ended yesterday, so he went to return his 2023 base-model sedan.

He signed that lease three years ago with a $280 monthly payment.

When he sat down with the fleet manager to look at leasing the exact same 2026 entry-level trim, the new offer came back at $520 a month with $2,500 down.

He looked at the manager and said:

 "My salary went up 8% over the last three years, but the monthly cost to lease the exact same entry-level car doubled?"

The manager leaned over his desk and quietly said:

"Car companies don't make money selling $25,000 basic sedans anymore. 

They intentionally discontinued low-trim models to force everyone into $45,000 tech-loaded crossover SUVs."

He checked the inventory sheet: out of 140 vehicles on the lot, only 3 were under $30,000.

We didn't just experience price inflation in the auto market.

Automakers intentionally eliminated affordable entry-level options to destroy the budget tier and force the entire middle class into luxury-level monthly debt.

text:
Joe de la Cruz for State Senate sent this mailer into Senate District 18, so I’m going to respond to it as someone who has spent years fighting for vaccine choice in Connecticut. Joe’s campaign didn’t simply say he disagrees with Heather Somers on vaccines. He called her positions “dangerous anti vaccination stances” and said they “put our kids and public health at risk.”
DANGEROUS.
That word was chosen deliberately. So Joe, let’s talk about who these supposedly dangerous people actually are.
They’re nurses who worked through COVID and then faced losing their jobs over a vaccine mandate.
They’re firefighters, teachers, healthcare workers, military families, state employees and blue collar workers who believed their employer shouldn’t get to make a medical decision for them.
They’re parents who vaccinate their children but still believe they should have the final say over what goes into their child’s body.
They’re parents who chose some vaccines and declined others.
They’re families who wanted religious exemptions.
They’re people fighting through an increasingly difficult medical exemption process.
And yes, they’re also people who decided they didn’t want the COVID vaccine at all.
Those people aren’t dangerous, they’re your constituents.
Senator Heather Somers and I don’t even have the exact same position on vaccines. Heather supports vaccines. She supports access to vaccines.
But here is the difference that actually matters, Heather also supports your right to say NO.
She believes you should be able to get a vaccine if you want one and decline it if you don’t.
She believes parents should have a choice.
She supports religious exemptions.
She supports a reasonable path for people who legitimately need medical exemptions.
She believes that you don’t have to personally make the same medical decision as someone else to defend their right to make it.
THAT is choice.
Get every vaccine you want. Vaccinate your children according to what you and your doctor believe is right for them. Have access to vaccines. Ask questions. Read the information. Make your decision.
But don’t make mine.
And don’t have the arrogance to label people “dangerous” because they don’t surrender that decision to the government.
Especially when you’re a politician with no medical background telling families which medical beliefs they’re apparently permitted to have.
He’s been calling dirty anti vaxxers.
He’s dismissed no our concern without conversation.
He’s labeling us dangerous.
He voted in 2021 as a representative to remove the religious exemption.
He voted for mask mandates and emergency power extensions.
He voted to take people’s jobs and livelihoods during COVID if they refused the vaccine.
And somehow we’re still supposed to sit quietly while he mocks our suggestion that government shouldn’t have unlimited authority over another person’s body.
I have spent years dealing with politicians who don’t want to have the conversation. They don’t want to hear why a nurse might oppose a mandate. They don’t want to hear from the mother whose child had a reaction. They don’t want to discuss religious exemptions, medical exemptions or informed consent.
They just want a label.
Anti-vaxxer.
Dangerous.
Selfish.
Don’t tell me you’re a “working class bipartisan who puts people first” on one side of your mailer and then turn around and characterize a whole set of medical freedom positions as “dangerous” on the other.
Which people are you putting first, Joe?
Because the working class includes the nurse who didn’t want a COVID shot.
It includes the firefighter who opposed a mandate.
It includes the mom who vaccinates but still believes religious exemptions should exist.
It includes the parent who wants an accessible medical exemption for a child.
It includes the person who took every COVID shot offered AND STILL believes their neighbor had the right to say no.
Those people don’t disappear because you’ve found a convenient political label for them.
And this is why I’m asking Connecticut’s vaccine choice community to go follow Joe, comment on everything he posts! Ask him what he actually supports. Ask him about mandates. Ask him about religious exemptions. Ask him about medical exemptions. Ask him whether there is any point at which he believes the individual gets to tell the government, NO.
Make him answer.
Because Senate District 18 may be the district electing this senator, but the person sitting in that chair will vote on legislation affecting every family in Connecticut.
I’ve already spent enough years watching politicians dismiss people instead of listening to them.
I don’t want another senator who opens the drawer, throws everyone who disagrees with him inside it, labels it “ANTI-VAXXERS,” and slams it shut.
And Joe De La Cruz’s own mailer just gave Connecticut a damn good reason to start having it. @kateinthemix @CTCentinal @HEATHERSOMERS

text:
Nvidia's $20 billion Groq deal reaches court with the payout line blacked out.

Groq makes AI chips, and last December Nvidia paid to license its technology and hire most of its engineers. Groq's own release named no price. The $20 billion figure came from Alex Davis, whose fund had led Groq's September 2025 round, in an interview with CNBC. Nvidia declined to comment on it.

Two former Groq engineers now say that number is really two different numbers under one name. In their lawsuit, filed in Delaware and made public in early October 2026, $17 billion is a license fee owed to Groq and $3 billion is Nvidia stock for the roughly 150 to 200 engineers who moved. What ordinary stockholders got per share is blacked out in the public version.

Even the $17 billion comes in installments, with the last $1 billion due December 24, 2026, and the complaint says Nvidia can keep part of it to cover its own claims under the deal. That holdback clause sits in the complaint too, and we'd keep it next to any quote of $17 billion.

Where we think nearly everyone is wrong is calling this a sale. Nvidia paid for the technology and the team, and the company itself stayed behind. The lawsuit says its stockholders never voted on that before closing. In a later reorganization, the complaint says, outside stockholders were cashed out at a $3.5 billion valuation it calls underpriced, about half the $6.9 billion of September 2025.

Groq calls the suit meritless. Davis's fund is among the investors that approved the deal in writing after it closed.

Google paid about $2.7 billion around Character AI in 2024 and about $2.4 billion around Windsurf in 2025, both licenses with the founders hired. Groq is the largest of these we can find, and we doubt it will be the last.

The window we see is for engineers who hold stock options. Before we signed with an AI startup, we'd ask what the shares get if the company is licensed rather than sold, because that clause decides whether a $20 billion headline ever reaches the people holding them. We expect that question to be routine in offer negotiations within five years.

A $20 billion fight in Delaware comes down, for one engineer, to a paragraph about licenses in her stock plan.

text:
A Declaration of Commitment to a Generation

When, in the course of a nation's life, it becomes necessary for one generation to remind another of the promise under which both were born, a decent respect for the young requires that the country state plainly what it owes them, and by what lawful means it intends to offer.

We write not to dissolve the bonds that join us, but to mend them. The founders of this Republic took up their pens to end an abuse. We take up ours to end a neglect and renew a vow: the vow of a country to its own children, and of those children to the country that raised them.

The Truths We Hold

We hold these truths to be as evident today as on the day they were first set down two hundred and fifty years ago: that all are created equal; that they are endowed with rights which no government grants and none may revoke; and that among these are life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

We hold further that a pursuit requires a path. A right to seek happiness means little to one who has no means of setting out. Liberty is hollow where honest labor cannot purchase shelter, and equality is defined by which party is in power. These preeminent American ideals become a courtesy of speech where the circumstances of birth can still decide the course of a life.

We hold that the American dream was never a promise of riches. It was a covenant, plain and modest: that those who work hard and keep faith with their neighbors shall have a home, a livelihood, and the reasonable expectation that their children will fare better than they. It is not a system of economic equality that has been tried and failed around the world, it is a system of freedom and equal pursuit of opportunity. Every generation of Americans has inherited that covenant, and every generation is bound by the commitment to hand it on intact.

And we hold that when the covenant weakens, it is the right and the duty of the people to repair it, not by tearing down their institutions, but by using them.

The Facts Submitted

The history of the present age is not one of tyranny by any single hand. It is one of slow neglect by many hands, across many years, under every party. To prove this, let facts be submitted to a candid country.

The young were told that education was the gate to prosperity, and found the toll set so high that many begin their working lives already in debt.

They were told that work would lead to a home, and have watched the price of housing require two incomes and still outrun the wages of those who would live inside it.

They were told that a full day's labor would secure a living, and find that rent, taxes, medicine, childcare and food consume the whole of it, leaving nothing for emergencies or the future.

They have seen sickness become a cause of ruin, and the fear of a doctor's bill keep the ill from the physician's door.

They have put off marriage, children, and the founding of households, not for a lack of desire, but for want of means and opportunity.

They have been handed forty trillion in debts they did not vote to incur.

They have deployed and died around the world to fight forever wars; some wars to protect our way of life and others to protect corporate interests.

They have inherited an environment and climate less sound than their parents received; yet an environmentalist movement that restricts housing growth and energy generation.

They have watched the representatives of the nation grow old, and found their own concerns arriving late to the debate floor, if they arrive at all.

In every stage of this decline the young have done what was asked of them. They studied, they worked, they fought, they waited their turn. Their patience has too often been answered with advice to be more patient still.

The gravest injury is not any one of these. It is the loss of hope itself: the quiet conclusion, reached by too many before the age of forty, that the dream was meant for someone else. A people can survive hardship. They cannot long survive the belief that effort is useless.

The Obligation

In January of 1961 a young President stood before the Capitol and gave his countrymen a warning that still rings true today:

"If a free society cannot help the many who are poor, it cannot save the few who are rich."  — John F. Kennedy

We take him at his word. The fortunes of the comfortable and the struggling are not two ledgers but one. A republic who erodes its middle class and who’s young have no stake in prosperity cannot expect them to tend it, defend it, or believe in it. The prosperity of the few rests on the faith of the many, and that faith is not inexhaustible.

This is therefore no plea for charity. No request for economic equality or socialism. It is a matter of the nation's own preservation. The elder owe the younger what they themselves were given: schools that opened doors, wages that built households, and a government that believed tomorrow was worth investing in.

Nor is this a quarrel between generations. Those who came before built much that we cherish, and many among them share our alarm. We ask them not to step aside but to stand beside us.

We, therefore, citizens of the United States, appealing to the conscience of our countrymen and to the institutions our forebears built, do solemnly publish and declare that this nation owes its rising generation not a guarantee of fortune, but a fair chance at one. To that end we resolve:

That learning and the mastery of a trade shall be within reach of every willing mind, with a balanced teaching, at a reasonable expense and without the burden of a lifetime's debt.

That homes shall be built in abundance where work is to be found, so that wages may once more buy a dwelling.

That honest labor shall earn enough to live upon, to save from, and to raise a family by.

That no citizen shall be made destitute by illness, nor kept from care by fear of its cost.

That we will only commit our younger generations to war if we are willing to send our own sons and daughters.

That no generation shall spend the inheritance of the next, whether of treasure, of soil, or of sky, without a just accounting.

That the young shall be welcomed into the councils of the nation, to vote without hindrance, to stand for office, and to be heard.

These ends we will pursue by the means the Constitution provides and no others: by the ballot, by petition, by open debate, by the patient labor of writing and amending laws. We renounce force, and we renounce contempt for the institutions that are ours to improve. The remedy for a democracy that has grown deaf is more voices and votes within it, not fewer.

Let it be said of this generation of Americans, young and old together, that when the flame of hope dwindled among the young, the country did not counsel resignation or pursue socialism. It remembered the principles of its founding, and set to work.

text:
A Declaration of Commitment to a Generation

When, in the course of a nation's life, it becomes necessary for one generation to remind another of the promise under which both were born, a decent respect for the young requires that the country state plainly what it owes them, and by what lawful means it intends to offer.

We write not to dissolve the bonds that join us, but to mend them. The founders of this Republic took up their pens to end an abuse. We take up ours to end a neglect and renew a vow: the vow of a country to its own children, and of those children to the country that raised them.

The Truths We Hold

We hold these truths to be as evident today as on the day they were first set down two hundred and fifty years ago: that all are created equal; that they are endowed with rights which no government grants and none may revoke; and that among these are life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.

We hold further that a pursuit requires a path. A right to seek happiness means little to one who has no means of setting out. Liberty is hollow where honest labor cannot purchase shelter, and equality is defined by which party is in power. These preeminent American ideals become a courtesy of speech where the circumstances of birth can still decide the course of a life.

We hold that the American dream was never a promise of riches. It was a covenant, plain and modest: that those who work hard and keep faith with their neighbors shall have a home, a livelihood, and the reasonable expectation that their children will fare better than they. It is not a system of economic equality that has been tried and failed around the world, it is a system of freedom and equal pursuit of opportunity. Every generation of Americans has inherited that covenant, and every generation is bound by the commitment to hand it on intact.

And we hold that when the covenant weakens, it is the right and the duty of the people to repair it, not by tearing down their institutions, but by using them.

The Facts Submitted

The history of the present age is not one of tyranny by any single hand. It is one of slow neglect by many hands, across many years, under every party. To prove this, let facts be submitted to a candid country.

The young were told that education was the gate to prosperity, and found the toll set so high that many begin their working lives already in debt.

They were told that work would lead to a home, and have watched the price of housing require two incomes and still outrun the wages of those who would live inside it.

They were told that a full day's labor would secure a living, and find that rent, taxes, medicine, childcare and food consume the whole of it, leaving nothing for emergencies or the future.

They have seen sickness become a cause of ruin, and the fear of a doctor's bill keep the ill from the physician's door.

They have put off marriage, children, and the founding of households, not for a lack of desire, but for want of means and opportunity.

They have been handed forty trillion in debts they did not vote to incur.

They have deployed and died around the world to fight forever wars; some wars to protect our way of life and others to protect corporate interests.

They have inherited an environment and climate less sound than their parents received; yet an environmentalist movement that restricts housing growth and energy generation.

They have watched the representatives of the nation grow old, and found their own concerns arriving late to the debate floor, if they arrive at all.

In every stage of this decline the young have done what was asked of them. They studied, they worked, they fought, they waited their turn. Their patience has too often been answered with advice to be more patient still.

The gravest injury is not any one of these. It is the loss of hope itself: the quiet conclusion, reached by too many before the age of forty, that the dream was meant for someone else. A people can survive hardship. They cannot long survive the belief that effort is useless.

The Obligation

In January of 1961 a young President stood before the Capitol and gave his countrymen a warning that still rings true today:

"If a free society cannot help the many who are poor, it cannot save the few who are rich."  — John F. Kennedy

We take him at his word. The fortunes of the comfortable and the struggling are not two ledgers but one. A republic who erodes its middle class and who’s young have no stake in prosperity cannot expect them to tend it, defend it, or believe in it. The prosperity of the few rests on the faith of the many, and that faith is not inexhaustible.

This is therefore no plea for charity. No request for economic equality or socialism. It is a matter of the nation's own preservation. The elder owe the younger what they themselves were given: schools that opened doors, wages that built households, and a government that believed tomorrow was worth investing in.

Nor is this a quarrel between generations. Those who came before built much that we cherish, and many among them share our alarm. We ask them not to step aside but to stand beside us.

We, therefore, citizens of the United States, appealing to the conscience of our countrymen and to the institutions our forebears built, do solemnly publish and declare that this nation owes its rising generation not a guarantee of fortune, but a fair chance at one. To that end we resolve:

That learning and the mastery of a trade shall be within reach of every willing mind, with a balanced teaching, at a reasonable expense and without the burden of a lifetime's debt.

That homes shall be built in abundance where work is to be found, so that wages may once more buy a dwelling.

That honest labor shall earn enough to live upon, to save from, and to raise a family by.

That no citizen shall be made destitute by illness, nor kept from care by fear of its cost.

That we will only commit our younger generations to war if we are willing to send our own sons and daughters.

That no generation shall spend the inheritance of the next, whether of treasure, of soil, or of sky, without a just accounting.

That the young shall be welcomed into the councils of the nation, to vote without hindrance, to stand for office, and to be heard.

These ends we will pursue by the means the Constitution provides and no others: by the ballot, by petition, by open debate, by the patient labor of writing and amending laws. We renounce force, and we renounce contempt for the institutions that are ours to improve. The remedy for a democracy that has grown deaf is more voices and votes within it, not fewer.

Let it be said of this generation of Americans, young and old together, that when the flame of hope dwindled among the young, the country did not counsel resignation or pursue socialism. It remembered the principles of its founding, and set to work.

And for support of this Declaration, with a firm reliance on one another and on the enduring promise of this Nation, we mutually pledge our voices, our votes, our energy, and our sacred honor.

text:
Rapid Refactoring with Claude: https://t.co/79u2UD2IfE

😱 Claude and I wrote our own long-running task runner for Tollbooth MCPs. This week, we ripped it out and replaced it in minutes.

❓Tollbooth DPYC MCPs needed an asynchronous Task Runner for long-running tool requests which need more time than the conventions of synchronous HTTP TCP requests will tolerate. For example, in eXcalibur, a service for generating X posts, a post can hold a dynamic block whose text is an LLM prompt. Resolving that block often takes minutes: the LLM model needs to survey the web, analyze responses, synthesize and compose marketing content, and returns professional "copy".

However, as is common in industry, the Tollbooth DPYC MCPs are deployed as on-demand, serverless instances. This infrastructure has demanding synchronous response deadlines and it recycles containers. Work started in the context of one request does not reliably outlive the request. (In fact, it reliably dies at the end of the request response.)

🛠️ So Claude and I built a deferred execution task runner service with tools for the client to specify jobs, check job status, and to claim finished jobs. The runtime sealed a job description with AES-256-GCM, shipped the ciphertext to a generic remote flow, and that flow interpreted a small vocabulary of operations. Results came back through the platform's artifact store, because its own result storage was the worker's local disk and unreadable from anywhere else. A per-operator secret block held the seal key. A non-secret selector rode in the clear so the shared flow could pick the right one.

It took seven rather complex concepts to move one function call out of the synchronous flow into an asynchronous runner.

Every one of these concepts existed for a defensible reason. The remote flow could not execute our code. So we invented a wire format and an interpreter to describe our code to it.

It worked - but...

💥 It also failed in ways that were hard to observe and diagnose. A dispatch error fell back to running in the calling MCP process, which looked healthy but was a fakeout. So, we responded by adding instrumentation. Then more instrumentation. Then instrumentation for the instrumentation. We got better at observing a tortured implementation rather than implementing a better solution. That's a code smell whose stink gets more and more intolerable.

🔎 Two announcements made us look up. Anthropic shipped Managed Agents. Deno released celld, self-hosted Durable Objects.

These are attractive - but, after consideration, neither fit.

❌ Managed Agents runs Claude only, and we route every model call through our choice of LLM provider using (rockstar) OpenRouter. Any technology that is wedded to Anthropic is a non-starter.

❌ celld and Cloudflare Workflows offer TypeScript language support - but not Python. Adopting them would mean having to have second implementations for our encryption services, as well as for any code that we would want to be able to run "in process" or via async runners. Two implementations of one algorithm is killer-drift just waiting to happen.

😁 Fortunately, these technologies did something better than just fitting: they inspired us to write each other the requirements for our capability, which we had never actually shared with each other (Claude and me). Those are:

- Accept a request synchronously.
- Allow running for tens to hundreds of minutes.
- Let the client come back later and claim the answer.
- Nothing in that path may be bound to a synchronous HTTP deadline.
- Support Python, because our operators are Python.
- Be Model agnostic.
- Require no new stateful infrastructure.
- Offer Per-operator isolation.

Stated clearly, the field of candidate solutions thinned quickly. (Which we kind of knew because that is why we started this by writing our own solution without doing really good research.)

Temporal, Hatchet, Restate, DBOS, Kitaru. All capable durable-execution engines. Supported by the Pydantic Team, too - very comforting.

But, every one of them still needs a worker or a cluster that we would have to self host or at least provision.

Kitaru came closest in spirit, with checkpoints and a wait() that releases compute to zero while even waiting for a human to participate in the flow. Really nice.

Kitaru's current available hosting targets are Kubernetes and the big clouds. We will keep watching it. Setting up a cluster is too much of a heavy-lift for Tollbooth DPYC Operators.

⚡ Modal won. It's the one that ran our code.

In Modal, a decorator annotation marks a function as runnable asynchronously. The method spawn() returns a handle in milliseconds. Functions can run up to twenty-four hours. Billing is per second and scales to zero. The handle can be redeemed from any process, which is precisely the claim check our tools already hand out.

(According to Claude) the refactoring in the MCPs was a mere three lines. Where the old code started a background task, the new code spawns. The determination about which requests need long-running that we had already written did not change at all. What changed is only where execution occurs.

👍 Deleting the obsolete code for our own runner removed 1,940 lines from the tollbooth-dpyc Python wheel. The runtime module alone lost 511. Gone: the sealed closure, the key selector, the per-operator secret block, the operation vocabulary, the interpreter flow, the artifact result channel, the result shaper.

The DRY elegance matters more than the line count. We had been maintaining two implementations of one resolution. One ran in process. The other was baked into a sealed specification for the remote interpreter, with a third function to translate its answers back. Same behaviour, three places to keep in step. Now there is one registration and one path.

🔑 The identity story is the part we like best.

The Modal container requires only one secret: the operator's Nostr nsec. From that it derives its npub, finds its Authority's configuration DM on a Nostr relay, and receives its database URL and its vault key. We copy no database URL. We copy no encryption key. The container ends up holding exactly what the MCP host holds, and the operator's human only ever handles the one value they already know (the nsec of their Operator).

We also looked at MCP Tasks, the emerging standard for starting a long call and polling it. In the 2026-07-28 release candidate it moved out of the core specification and became an extension after a redesign, and anyone who shipped against the earlier version has to migrate. We kept our own claim-check tools for now and will adopt the standard once it settles.

Economically, for pricing tools to Patron users, the toll fares did not change. The tools did not change. The Operator remains at liberty to set prices dynamically based on the infrastructure expenses for using Modal.

😎 eXcalibur's dynamic Posts stopped dying and our Observability headaches stopped flaring up.

────────────────────

₿   Tollbooth DPYC™ is the efficient monetization service for MCPs whose BTC-using entrepreneurs want to avoid KYC and who agree to practice Don't Pester Your Customer™ commerce.

⚡  With Tollbooth DPYC, your patrons purchase, out of band, tranches of "𝐴𝑃𝐼 𝑆𝑎𝑡𝑠", using rapid-settlement Lightning. Patrons then spend these API Sats across different tool calls with zero per-request friction and no KYC.

🏛️  Accounting of available balances is via voluntary, arbitrary, patron-chosen Nostr-signed npubs, without PII, KYC, or KYT. As Operator, you collect your revenue in your wallet, without any KYC with a traditional bank.

Judaism and the Sins of Israel: On the Essential Nature of Religion
Israel, an "artificial state" established by Zionists, has brought immense catastrophe to Palestine and the Middle East, exerting a profound and unsettling impact on the global order while severely jeopardizing humanity's faith in justice. To enable a clearer discernment of the true nature of Judaism and the state of Israel, distinguish right from wrong, and offer humanity a glimmer of hope to rectify deviations and restore justice, this article systematically delineates their multiple transgressions.
1. Blaspheming God and Serving the Devil
Does God exist? It is a question to which no definitive empirical answer can be given. Yet, for any religion, the existence of God is an absolute certainty—a Supreme Being who created the universe and will ultimately deliver it. Since God created the world, the Divine must be inherently grand, righteous, and impeccable. God cannot behave like an earthly despot who blurs the line between right and wrong, harbors blind favoritism, or instigates conflict that leaves the earth devastated and drenched in blood. Any entity that perpetuates such horrors must be the devil, not God. God would deem it beneath Divine dignity to broker arbitrary covenants, grant exclusive real estate titles to specific mortals, demonstrate absolute partiality toward a selective few, or engage in physical wrestling matches with humans—much like a human would never engage in such absurdities with an ant, and would find it reviling to hear an ant boast of such a relationship. Therefore, what Judaism worships is the devil, not God; consequently, Judaism itself is the true object of divine retribution.
2. A Total Syndicate Snuffing Out the Beacon of Humanity
The ultimate purpose of religion is self-interest, utilizing individual benefit as a mechanism to attract adherents. This self-interest can be bifurcated into two categories: temporal self-interest in the material world, and transcendental self-interest in the afterlife. While the vast majority of religions pursue the latter, the modalities of religious dissemination can be categorized into three paradigms: self-interest, altruism, and self-abnegation.
· Righteous Religions: Expand their doctrines through structural altruism to attain both temporal and transcendental self-interest (modern Protestantism, to a qualified extent, approaches this paradigm).
· Neutral Religions: Enjoin strict self-abnegation to achieve transcendental self-interest (authentic Chinese Mahayana Buddhism emphasizes high self-abnegation and moderate altruism; Tibetan Buddhism, however, deviates from this).
· Malevolent Religions: Disseminate their faith via raw self-interest to maximize both temporal and transcendental gains (Judaism fits this mold).
· Criminal Syndicates: When a group systematically inflicts harm upon external populations to secure transcendental self-interest, it ceases to be a religion and becomes a criminal enterprise (such as ISIS).
True righteous religion is singular; it must rely on altruism as its proselytizing engine to fulfill its dual self-interest. Judged by this criterion, Islam must also be categorized as a cultish entity.
When a religion becomes pathologically insular yet fiercely unified for collective self-enrichment, it must perpetually extract illicit advantages from the external world to fulfill its internal theological promises and suppress external criticism or interference. This manifests through predatory usury, monopolistic syndicates, the systematic deprivation of opportunities for outsiders, the monopolization of media to strangle freedom of speech, the utilization of ill-gotten wealth to manipulate foreign governments, and the deployment of collective intimidation against dissenters. Judged by any objective metric, this exhibits the classic hallmarks of a mafia.
Consider the contemporary world: we witness the collective intimidation of protesting students at Harvard, where syndicates coerced the university administration to surrender blacklists and threatened a total hiring boycott against student dissidents. Even in my own experience, when attempting to publish a critique of Israel, editors at major media outlets felt compelled to cautiously warn me to "ensure my personal safety." These multi-faceted realities reveal a chilling truth: when confronting Israel, the constitutional right to free speech is immediately compromised by physical and professional security anxieties.
Look at the sheer absurdity of our global reality: within the United States—the very nation that birthed the United Nations and once stood as a beacon of civilization—the government stands in obstinate, isolated solidarity with Israel, defiantly opposing the overwhelming majority of the international community on Palestinian sovereignty. Nearly all mainstream political figures line up in lockstep behind Israel, even when the comment sections beneath their public statements are flooded with denunciation from the populace. Are we to believe that every single American politician is a fundamentally malicious actor? Facing the spilled blood of the Palestinian people and the living hell of their homeland, have these politicians truly been possessed by demons to consciously walk in alignment with evil? No matter how compromised these politicians may be, it is impossible that this reflects the genuine, uncoerced intent of all of them. This unveils a profoundly horrifying reality upon closer reflection: the United States is rapidly transforming into a hollowed-out zombie, its sovereign soul thoroughly extracted by Israel and Zionist interest groups.
3. Bloodlust Masked by Hypocritical Dogma
We must remain hyper-vigilant against a common tactic employed by certain theologians and scholars who attempt to sanitize Judaism by citing altruistic laws within its scriptures—such as the Decalogue, commands to "give alms to the poor," or prohibitions against "oppressing the stranger." However, any insular, predatory interest group must inevitably weave a cloak of righteous justice to survive within secular society and deflect external scrutiny. As the ancient proverb goes, "there is honor even among thieves"—the most ruthless cartels in history eagerly built bridges and paved roads for their local neighborhoods, and the most extreme cults frequently used charitable handouts to buy public compliance.
These manicured facades are by no means the essence of the system; they are merely moral ornaments designed to deceive the world. In practice, "giving alms to the poor" stands in irreconcilable, parasitic contradiction with "predatory usury and capital monopoly." Through usurious practices and financial blood-sucking, they drive millions of Gentile families into destitution and ruin; then, they turn inward to distribute welfare within their enclosed circle, placating their own kin and delivering on the material benefits promised upon initiation. This closed-loop mechanism of "extreme external predation coupled with internal distribution of spoils" precisely validates its absolute identity as a mafia syndicate. To evaluate an entity, one must look past its ornamental garments and examine whose fundamental right to survival it has stripped away. Any appeasement of this profound hypocrisy constitutes an outright betrayal of human justice.
4. Actions Divorced from Modern Civilization
The foundational premise of modern civilization dictating that the Earth is the shared home of all living things; even apex species possess no arbitrary right to violently displace or dispossess other creatures of their habitats. If humanity lacks the ethical authority to evict monkeys from a mountain to claim it for ourselves, who under heaven possesses the right to strip the Palestinian people of their sovereign right to exist and reside in Palestine?
Following the conclusion of World War II in 1945, Jewish populations no longer faced an existential threat to their survival; what, then, justified their subsequent threat to the very survival of the Palestinians? Apologists might argue that the Jewish community, having just endured the horrors of the Holocaust, was trapped in an extreme crisis of survival. Yet, this can never serve as a legitimate pretext for violent dispossession. Existential crises are not unique to the Jewish experience. According to the most basic threshold of fairness and justice in modern civilization, any localized catastrophe or crisis must be resolved at its historical source; it can never grant a right to displace the catastrophe onto innocent third parties by plundering their legitimate right to life. The bitter fruits of European anti-Semitism ought to have been borne by Europe itself. Forcing the native inhabitants of Palestine—who played absolutely no part in European crimes—to foot the bill for "moral reparations" of the Holocaust, and framing the so-called "two-state solution" as justice, represents one of the most hypocritical, shameless, and predatory acts of banditry in the history of modern international politics.
5. The Abuse of Violence to Perpetrate Genocide
For nearly eighty years, Zionist forces in Palestine have systematically displaced the indigenous population, brutally massacred and incarcerated Palestinians, and relentlessly expanded illegal settlements. This has triggered an endless exodus of refugees, resulted in innumerable casualties, and caused harrowing atrocities to play out on a daily basis—all driven by a calculated attempt to gradually liquidate the Palestinian people and completely usurp their land.
Thanks to the ubiquity of modern digital media, the tragic plight of the Palestinians is now laid bare before the collective conscience of humanity. Who, then, is the true terrorist? The moral framework governing the justifiable use of violence dictating that violence is righteous only when one's own survival or the survival of others is actively threatened. Consequently, the Palestinian people possess an absolute, legitimate right to employ violence against their Israeli oppressors. Their resistance is fundamentally just, whereas Israel constitutes the actual terrorist entity.
6. Constructing an Invisible Empire Parasitic Upon Modern States
By tightly binding religious identity to material self-interest, the Zionist cartel has engineered an invisible empire that effectively reigns supreme over sovereign nations. Leveraging their monopolized financial wealth and sprawling media conglomerates, they exert deep, manipulative control over Western political landscapes. This insular, self-serving apparatus utilizes aggressive financial lobbying to transmute the hard-earned tax dollars of foreign citizens into their own political leverage, ultimately hijacking the foreign policies of major global powers. This is a textbook case of a predatory interest group subverting, hollow out, and invisibly parasitizing modern democracy and sovereign civilization.
7. Ideological Thought Policing and the Destruction of Public Justice
To immunize themselves against external critique, these groups weaponize historical trauma, swiftly branding any discourse that interrogates their atrocities with the label of "anti-Semitism." This calculated form of ideological thought policing is brutally suffocating academic freedom and liberty of expression. As the world witnesses the blood-soaked purgatory inflicted upon the Palestinian people, Western politicians—paralyzed by the intimidation of powerful lobby groups—lapse into a collective, spineless silence, willfully aligning themselves with demonic forces. This absolute double standard has triggered a profound crisis of trust in modern morality, fundamentally dismantling humanity's self-evident faith in equity, justice, and universal law.

Despite the reality that certain factions within the Jewish populace remain bound by a nexus of religion and self-interest—forming an invisible, crushing force capable of flattening any individual resistance to suppress anti-Zionist critiques—there are still courageous Jewish individuals who actively resist Israeli policies and oppose draconian anti-Semitism legislation. Though born into the fold of Judaism, their conscience and commitment to justice have triumphed over institutional evil. They represent the true pride of the Jewish people and the sole beacon of hope for their eventual moral redemption.

Since God created the world, the Divine must be inherently grand, righteous, and impeccable. God cannot behave like an earthly despot who blurs the line between right and wrong, harbors blind favoritism, or instigates conflict that leaves the earth devastated and drenched in blood. Any entity that perpetuates such horrors must be the devil, not God. God would deem it beneath Divine dignity to broker arbitrary covenants, grant exclusive real estate titles to specific mortals, demonstrate absolute partiality toward a selective few, or engage in physical wrestling matches with humans—much like a human would never engage in such absurdities with an ant, and would find it reviling to hear an ant boast of such a relationship. Therefore, what Judaism worships is the devil, not God; consequently, Judaism itself is the true object of divine retribution.
2. A Total Syndicate Snuffing Out the Beacon of Humanity
The ultimate purpose of religion is self-interest, utilizing individual benefit as a mechanism to attract adherents. This self-interest can be bifurcated into two categories: temporal self-interest in the material world, and transcendental self-interest in the afterlife. While the vast majority of religions pursue the latter, the modalities of religious dissemination can be categorized into three paradigms: self-interest, altruism, and self-abnegation.
· Righteous Religions: Expand their doctrines through structural altruism to attain both temporal and transcendental self-interest (modern Protestantism, to a qualified extent, approaches this paradigm).
· Neutral Religions: Enjoin strict self-abnegation to achieve transcendental self-interest (authentic Chinese Mahayana Buddhism emphasizes high self-abnegation and moderate altruism; Tibetan Buddhism, however, deviates from this).
· Malevolent Religions: Disseminate their faith via raw self-interest to maximize both temporal and transcendental gains (Judaism fits this mold).
· Criminal Syndicates: When a group systematically inflicts harm upon external populations to secure transcendental self-interest, it ceases to be a religion and becomes a criminal enterprise (such as ISIS).
True righteous religion is singular; it must rely on altruism as its proselytizing engine to fulfill its dual self-interest. Judged by this criterion, Islam must also be categorized as a cultish entity.

This manifests through predatory usury, monopolistic syndicates, the systematic deprivation of opportunities for outsiders, the monopolization of media to strangle freedom of speech, the utilization of ill-gotten wealth to manipulate foreign governments, and the deployment of collective intimidation against dissenters. Judged by any objective metric, this exhibits the classic hallmarks of a mafia.
Consider the contemporary world: we witness the collective intimidation of protesting students at Harvard, where syndicates coerced the university administration to surrender blacklists and threatened a total hiring boycott against student dissidents. Even in my own experience, when attempting to publish a critique of Israel, editors at major media outlets felt compelled to cautiously warn me to "ensure my personal safety." These multi-faceted realities reveal a chilling truth: when confronting Israel, the constitutional right to free speech is immediately compromised by physical and professional security anxieties.
Look at the sheer absurdity of our global reality: within the United States—the very nation that birthed the United Nations and once stood as a beacon of civilization—the government stands in obstinate, isolated solidarity with Israel, defiantly opposing the overwhelming majority of the international community on Palestinian sovereignty. Nearly all mainstream political figures line up in lockstep behind Israel, even when the comment sections beneath their public statements are flooded with denunciation from the populace. Are we to believe that every single American politician is a fundamentally malicious actor? Facing the spilled blood of the Palestinian people and the living hell of their homeland, have these politicians truly been possessed by demons to consciously walk in alignment with evil? No matter how compromised these politicians may be, it is impossible that this reflects the genuine, uncoerced intent of all of them. This unveils a profoundly horrifying reality upon closer reflection: the United States is rapidly transforming into a hollowed-out zombie, its sovereign soul thoroughly extracted by Israel and Zionist interest groups.
3. Bloodlust Masked by Hypocritical Dogma
We must remain hyper-vigilant against a common tactic employed by certain theologians and scholars who attempt to sanitize Judaism by citing altruistic laws within its scriptures—such as the Decalogue, commands to "give alms to the poor," or prohibitions against "oppressing the stranger." However, any insular, predatory interest group must inevitably weave a cloak of righteous justice to survive within secular society and deflect external scrutiny. As the ancient proverb goes, "there is honor even among thieves"—the most ruthless cartels in history eagerly built bridges and paved roads for their local neighborhoods, and the most extreme cults frequently used charitable handouts to buy public compliance.
These manicured facades are by no means the essence of the system; they are merely moral ornaments designed to deceive the world. In practice, "giving alms to the poor" stands in irreconcilable, parasitic contradiction with "predatory usury and capital monopoly." Through usurious practices and financial blood-sucking, they drive millions of Gentile families into destitution and ruin; then, they turn inward to distribute welfare within their enclosed circle, placating their own kin and delivering on the material benefits promised upon initiation. This closed-loop mechanism of "extreme external predation coupled with internal distribution of spoils" precisely validates its absolute identity as a mafia syndicate. To evaluate an entity, one must look past its ornamental garments and examine whose fundamental right to survival it has stripped away. Any appeasement of this profound hypocrisy constitutes an outright betrayal of human justice.
4. Actions Divorced from Modern Civilization
The foundational premise of modern civilization dictating that the Earth is the shared home of all living things; even apex species possess no arbitrary right to violently displace or dispossess other creatures of their habitats. If humanity lacks the ethical authority to evict monkeys from a mountain to claim it for ourselves, who under heaven possesses the right to strip the Palestinian people of their sovereign right to exist and reside in Palestine?
Following the conclusion of World War II in 1945, Jewish populations no longer faced an existential threat to their survival; what, then, justified their subsequent threat to the very survival of the Palestinians? Apologists might argue that the Jewish community, having just endured the horrors of the Holocaust, was trapped in an extreme crisis of survival. Yet, this can never serve as a legitimate pretext for violent dispossession. Existential crises are not unique to the Jewish experience. According to the most basic threshold of fairness and justice in modern civilization, any localized catastrophe or crisis must be resolved at its historical source; it can never grant a right to displace the catastrophe onto innocent third parties by plundering their legitimate right to life. The bitter fruits of European anti-Semitism ought to have been borne by Europe itself. Forcing the native inhabitants of Palestine—who played absolutely no part in European crimes—to foot the bill for "moral reparations" of the Holocaust, and framing the so-called "two-state solution" as justice, represents one of the most hypocritical, shameless, and predatory acts of banditry in the history of modern international politics.
5. The Abuse of Violence to Perpetrate Genocide
For nearly eighty years, Zionist forces in Palestine have systematically displaced the indigenous population, brutally massacred and incarcerated Palestinians, and relentlessly expanded illegal settlements. This has triggered an endless exodus of refugees, resulted in innumerable casualties, and caused harrowing atrocities to play out on a daily basis—all driven by a calculated attempt to gradually liquidate the Palestinian people and completely usurp their land.
Thanks to the ubiquity of modern digital media, the tragic plight of the Palestinians is now laid bare before the collective conscience of humanity. Who, then, is the true terrorist? The moral framework governing the justifiable use of violence dictating that violence is righteous only when one's own survival or the survival of others is actively threatened. Consequently, the Palestinian people possess an absolute, legitimate right to employ violence against their Israeli oppressors. Their resistance is fundamentally just, whereas Israel constitutes the actual terrorist entity.
6. Constructing an Invisible Empire Parasitic Upon Modern States
By tightly binding religious identity to material self-interest, the Zionist cartel has engineered an invisible empire that effectively reigns supreme over sovereign nations. Leveraging their monopolized financial wealth and sprawling media conglomerates, they exert deep, manipulative control over Western political landscapes. This insular, self-serving apparatus utilizes aggressive financial lobbying to transmute the hard-earned tax dollars of foreign citizens into their own political leverage, ultimately hijacking the foreign policies of major global powers. This is a textbook case of a predatory interest group subverting, hollow out, and invisibly parasitizing modern democracy and sovereign civilization.
7. Ideological Thought Policing and the Destruction of Public Justice
To immunize themselves against external critique, these groups weaponize historical trauma, swiftly branding any discourse that interrogates their atrocities with the label of "anti-Semitism." This calculated form of ideological thought policing is brutally suffocating academic freedom and liberty of expression. As the world witnesses the blood-soaked purgatory inflicted upon the Palestinian people, Western politicians—paralyzed by the intimidation of powerful lobby groups—lapse into a collective, spineless silence, willfully aligning themselves with demonic forces. This absolute double standard has triggered a profound crisis of trust in modern morality, fundamentally dismantling humanity's self-evident faith in equity, justice, and universal law.

Despite the reality that certain factions within the Jewish populace remain bound by a nexus of religion and self-interest—forming an invisible, crushing force capable of flattening any individual resistance to suppress anti-Zionist critiques—there are still courageous Jewish individuals who actively resist Israeli policies and oppose draconian anti-Semitism legislation. Though born into the fold of Judaism, their conscience and commitment to justice have triumphed over institutional evil. They represent the true pride of the Jewish people and the sole beacon of hope for their eventual moral redemption.

This really happened. Yes, it happened. At the Ottumwa, Iowa City Council’s regular meeting on October 6, 2026, a resident named Matthew Dalbey delivered the opening invocation. It was a Luciferian/Satanic-style prayer that included phrases such as “Dear dark father,” references to the “luciferian impulse,” and ended with “Hail Satan.” ￼
The official city YouTube recording of the meeting (Ottumwa Iowa channel) captures it clearly in the auto-generated transcript and audio: the meeting is called to order, the mayor invites those who wish to participate in the invocation to stand, Dalbey gives the prayer, and it concludes with “Hail Satan” before the Pledge of Allegiance begins. ￼
This was not an official city endorsement of Satanism. In January 2026 the council adopted an open, non-discriminatory invocation policy (Resolution 18-2026) by a 4-1 vote. It allows any Ottumwa resident to volunteer on a first-come, first-served basis to offer a brief (≤2-minute) invocation before the Pledge, regardless of belief system. The policy explicitly states it does not affiliate the city with any particular faith. Council member Cara Galloway had warned during the debate that this approach would require equal access for satanic, anti-theistic, or other unconventional speakers and could produce public backlash—exactly what occurred. ￼
City records list Matthew Dalbey (no organization affiliation) as the scheduled invoker for October 6, 2026. After the invocation, some attendees and a local pastor objected on the record, calling it a “curse” and asking for a moment of silence or reversal; the mayor allowed a brief moment of silence before proceeding with the agenda. ￼
The episode has circulated widely on X and elsewhere in the last day, often with clips from the official meeting video. The underlying facts match the primary source (the city’s own recording and policy documents).

text:
On the afternoon of July 17, 1974, 15-year-old Norma Jean Countryman was sitting beside a road in Ridgefield, Washington, smoking a cigarette. She was going through abuse at home and just wanted to get away for a while. A blue van stopped beside her, and the man inside started talking to her. At first, she thought about walking away, but in the end, she accepted his offer to give her a ride home.
The driver was Warren Forrest, a 28-year-old worker for the Clark County Parks Department. As soon as Norma Jean got into the van, he pulled a knife on her and kidnapped her. He drove deep into the forests of southern Washington, where he tied her hands and feet together. He used rough rope to bind and gag her, then tied her between two trees so she was hanging like a hammock. Norma Jean later said she truly believed she was going to die that day. She remembered saying every prayer she knew over and over in her mind, hoping she would survive.
Forrest left her there, saying he would come back later. Instead of waiting, Norma Jean began chewing through the ropes around her hands until she finally broke free. Even with her hands and ankles still tied, she hopped through the dark forest all night until she finally found help.
After escaping, she went straight to the police and told them everything she knew. She gave them the kidnapper's name, described his face, his blue van, the rope he used, and the knife he threatened her with. But no one believed her. What investigators did not know at the time was that just one week earlier, Forrest had kidnapped 20-year-old Krista Blake. She had already been murdered, and her body was buried in the same forest, only a short distance from where Norma Jean had been tied up.
Because Norma Jean's report was ignored, more young women disappeared. Investigators now believe Warren Forrest may be connected to several murders from the early 1970s. He was not arrested until later that year after he kidnapped and raped a 19-year-old woman near Lacamas Lake. She survived the attack and helped police identify him.
Forrest was later convicted of murdering 20-year-old Krista Blake. In 2023, almost 50 years after Norma Jean's kidnapping, he was also found guilty of killing 17-year-old Martha Morrison, whose murder happened in 1974. Investigators are still looking into other unsolved cases that may be connected to him, including the murder of 20-year-old Carol Valenzuela, whose remains were found near Martha's.
It took nearly 20 years before Norma Jean Countryman felt ready to tell her story publicly. She lived with the pain and trauma for most of her life and was never offered professional therapy. Since then, she has spoken at several parole hearings. She said she attends not only for herself but also for every person whose life was affected by Warren Forrest's crimes, including victims she did not even know existed on the day she stepped into his van, and the families and children left behind.

text:
President Christofferson Warned Against Prediction Markets. They’re Still Available in Utah

President D. Todd Christofferson used part of General Conference last weekend to warn Latter-day Saints about the spread of sports betting and prediction markets.

Four days later, sports prediction markets are still available to Utahns, even as state officials maintain that sports betting is illegal and Utah has already won one federal court fight over the issue.

Christofferson, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, devoted his Saturday morning address to gambling. He pointed to online sports betting, online casino games and prediction markets as major drivers of its growth and warned about easy access through smartphones, especially among young people.

In the published version of his talk, Christofferson also addressed the argument that prediction markets are investments rather than gambling. A footnote acknowledges that some event contracts can hedge legitimate economic risk, but says most prediction-market trading does not serve that purpose and is functionally gambling.

That warning lands in a state already fighting the same question in court.

Kalshi sued Utah earlier this year after state officials took the position that its sports-event contracts were subject to Utah gambling law. Kalshi argued that because it operates a federally regulated exchange overseen by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, its contracts fall under federal commodities law instead.

U.S. District Judge Robert Shelby rejected that argument in August and granted summary judgment to Utah. His ruling allows the state to enforce its anti-gambling laws against Kalshi’s sports contracts. It was not a ruling that every prediction-market product offered by every company is illegal.

Attorney General Derek Brown said after the ruling that his office intends to enforce Utah’s gambling prohibition.

“Gambling is gambling no matter what any company calls it,” Brown said.

Kalshi appealed. On Sept. 8, the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals denied its request to temporarily prevent Utah from enforcing its laws while the appeal moves forward. The underlying case is still pending.

But sports prediction products have not disappeared from Utah.

DraftKings currently lists its Predictions service as available in Utah, and its platform includes markets tied to the NFL, college football, the NBA, NHL and college basketball. The Salt Lake Tribune reported Wednesday that DraftKings, FanDuel and PrizePicks continue allowing Utah users to participate in prediction-market or daily-fantasy products.

Brown told the Tribune this week that Utah’s position has not changed.

“Sports betting marketed as a prediction market or anything else is still sports betting,” he said. “And it is still illegal.”

Utah lawmakers also changed state law this year to expressly include a “proposition bet” within the state’s gambling definitions. H.B. 243 defines that as a bet on an individual action, statistic, occurrence or non-occurrence.

The legal fight is not finished. Kalshi continues to argue that federally regulated event contracts are under CFTC jurisdiction, and Utah’s case is now before the 10th Circuit.

But the situation inside Utah is already unusual.

The state won at the district-court level. The appeals court declined to shield Kalshi from enforcement. Utah’s attorney general says sports prediction markets remain illegal. And now one of the senior leaders of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has specifically warned members about prediction markets as gambling.

Yet Utahns can still find sports prediction products on their phones.

The question now is what Utah intends to do about the companies continuing to offer them.
